News.title: Heart-stopping moment hero neighbour digs through smouldering wreckage to save boy, 4, trapped in house fire
News.content:
Next

THIS is the nail-biting moment a man used his bare hands to dig through the smouldering remains of a Mississippi house to rescue a four-year-old boy.

Footage shows Kennard Hodge scouring a mountain of melted insulation covered by a thick layer of grey ash for several minutes before pulling out the child by his hand.



“You got him?” a firefighter is heard asking Hodge as fire crews raced to control the flames.

The hero shouts back: “Yeah, I got him, got him, got him!”



Covered in burns, the boy was unconscious and was not breathing.

“Come on, little man… Hang in there bud,” a responding officer is heard pleading during the frantic efforts to revive him.

The child was given CPR before being rushed to hospital in a “very critical condition”.

The incident happened in the town of Edwards on October 7, with the dramatic video captured on a police bodycam.



No other updates about the boy’s condition have been shared since.

Kennard was among the neighbours who searched through the debris to find the boy.

He was the only one out of six minors still trapped inside the burning home.

Explaining his decision to intervene, Kennard said he wanted to give the child a “chance” of survival.

“All I wanted to do is to get the baby out so he could have a chance,” the neighbour told WAPTNews.



Terrence Crump, the Edwards police chief, praised the rescue effort as “nothing short of a miracle.”

“At approximately 10pm, deputies responded to a house fire in the 200 block of Utica Street after receiving reports that six children were trapped inside the burning residence,” a statement from Hinds County said.

“When deputies arrived, the home was fully engulfed in flames, and neighbours were already attempting rescue efforts.

“Neighbours successfully rescued five children – ages 13, 9, 3, 2, and 2 – from the home.

“Deputies were informed that a four‑year‑old boy remained trapped inside.”



The cause of the blaze remains under investigation.

News.title: Moment rioter desperately tries to pull off trousers engulfed in flames as looters crushed by panes of glass in France
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment a frantic rioter tries to pull off his flaming trousers as looters are crushed by falling panes of glass during violent unrest in France.

More than 500,000 people took to the streets over the weekend as protestors torched streets and marches descended into chaos.



Nearly 2,400 people were arrested, with authorities now considering curfews to restore order as Emmanuel Macron‘s government spiralled into chaos.

Violence has also erupted across Europe, with streets set ablaze and shops ransacked in Belgium, Portugal, Italy and Albania.



Shocking footage shows the black-clad rioter fleeing a tram stop with several accomplices before suddenly realising his trousers are on fire.

He desperately tugs at his tracksuit bottoms before stumbling onto the pavement and spinning around in a frantic attempt to extinguish the flames.



With his trousers around his ankles, the masked man begins stamping his feet before losing his balance and crashing to the ground.

Fellow rioters then rush over and crowd around him in an apparent attempt to help.

Elsewhere in France, another masked thug was left seriously injured after a huge pane of glass came crashing down on him during an attempted raid on a Lacoste store.

Footage shows a crowd gathering around a man wielding what appears to be a manhole cover as a makeshift battering ram.



But as he smashes through the shop window, a massive sheet of glass collapses onto his head, knocking him to the ground.

Separate footage, which may show the same incident, captures another rioter trapped beneath a fallen window as police in riot gear charge towards the scene.

Several masked protesters appear to rush towards the injured man in an attempt to free him before officers swarm the area.



Dozens of people also gathered around a young rioter who reportedly had his hand blown off while handling what is believed to have been a police stun grenade in Saint-Étienne.

Sirens can be heard blaring as the crowd rushes to help the wounded man.

The shocking scenes emerged as France endured another night of violence, with Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez admitting police had “lost control” in several cities.

President Macron pleaded for unity following emergency talks with senior ministers and vowed to bring those responsible for the destruction to justice.

He blamed “agitators from far-Left fringe groups, joined by numerous criminals” for plunging France into “unbridled violence”.



Hundreds of police officers were injured as masked gangs hurled Molotov cocktails, erected burning barricades and smashed their way into luxury stores including Christian Dior and Louis Vuitton.

A protester also died in the “apocalyptic” scenes after reportedly collapsing on Boulevard Magenta in Paris as a march passed through the area.

Police confirmed the person suffered a cardiac arrest, with the circumstances surrounding the death still under investigation.



Macron condemned the destruction in a national address, saying: “Public buildings, shops and town halls were attacked and in some cases destroyed.

“Many hundreds of police officers were injured. When we saw the images, we all thought, what was in their heads? How can French people do this to France?”

We are all feeling anger and shame tonight. To see the cities, the streets of our cities, ransacked like this is unbearable.”

The French leader also promised that “all the necessary lessons” would be learned from intelligence failures surrounding the unrest.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, who chaired a second crisis meeting in two days, accused the “ultra-left” of fuelling the disorder.



He claimed intelligence agencies had warned that far-left groups could seek to disrupt the presidential elections.

But left-wing presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon furiously rejected the claims, demanding Lecornu “name and prove his accusation… otherwise, let him apologise, shut up and stop stoking disorder”.

The government has also threatened to make rioters pay for the destruction they have caused.



Meanwhile, tourists hoping to visit the Louvre were left furious after protesters blockaded the world-famous museum’s glass pyramid entrance.

Demonstrators held a banner declaring “French public services are falling apart” as visitors hoping to see the Mona Lisa were turned away.

Some frustrated tourists were seen shouting and raising their middle fingers at protesters.

The museum confirmed it had closed because of student strikes, while activists handed out leaflets declaring they were “proud” to be blocking the attraction.

Unrest initially erupted over deteriorating school conditions, with students demanding more teachers and urgent repairs to crumbling buildings.



But weeks of largely peaceful demonstrations spiralled into widespread violence as masked troublemakers joined the protests.

In Limoges, the town hall was reduced to ashes, with Mayor Guillaume Guérin accusing organised extremists of deliberately orchestrating attacks.

He said: “Those who organise everything, who bring the battering rams, who smash the windows and identify the basement entrances in this town hall so they can get in – they are not the kids.



“They are people who are organised to wage war.”

Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire said restoring law and order was the priority but appeared reluctant to support curfews.

He told reporters: “We don’t want to prevent everyday life. We don’t want the majority to be affected by the acts of a small minority.”

Grégoire insisted freedom of movement and assembly must be protected while calling for an independent inquiry into the unrest.

Across the border in Italy, masked mobs ransacked shops and attacked police as two days of rioting gripped Milan.



Around 200 people were detained after demonstrations over rising living costs erupted into violence.

Footage reportedly showed one furious shopkeeper armed with a baton confronting a black-clad looter fleeing his store with stolen goods.

Rioters hurled stones, paving blocks and firecrackers at police while setting barricades and bins ablaze.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Road signs were torn down and shops looted as officers fought back with tear gas and water cannons.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned the rioters as “thugs who exploit demonstrations to spread chaos, attack those who guarantee security, and hold entire cities hostage”.

News.title: Creep neighbour, 73, who performed sex acts in front of OAP widow & fondled bras on her washing line AVOIDS jail
News.content:
PERV FREE Creep neighbour, 73, who performed sex acts in front of OAP widow & fondled bras on her washing line AVOIDS jail







Next

A NEIGHBOUR-from-hell who performed naked sex acts in front of an elderly widow and fondled bras on her washing line has avoided jail.

Robert May, 73, made Margaret Day’s life a misery at the housing complex they both lived on in Chaddesley Corbett, Worcestershire.



The nightmare neighbour sent sleazy texts demanding to see the 79-year-old’s breasts and performed sex acts on himself in full view of her home on more than 30 occasions.

May was also captured on mobile phone and Ring doorbell footage touching bras on Margaret’s washing line as part of the creepy campaign.



The creep initially tried to deny his crimes by claiming he was just rubbing Deep Heat on himself.

But he later pleaded guilty to an act of outraging public decency at Kidderminster Magistrates’ Court.



May avoided a prison sentence but was instead handed a 27 month suspended prison sentence.

Sentencing, District Judge Ian Strongman told the court that the defendant maintained there had been no wrongdoing on his part despite his plea, which he branded “nonsensical”.

In a victim statement read out to court, Margaret said she now feels like an outcast in her own community.

She added: “I feel sad, anxious and I feel that my lovely life in Chaddesley has been contaminated and the people around me won’t speak to me.



“My blood pressure is really high and I’ve had to see doctors often.

“I feel as though it has affected who I can trust around me as he was a friend.

“He moved in with nothing and I felt sorry for him, but he got worse over time.”



Margaret and her daughter Sue Mason-Day, 54, previously spoke out about the “years of hell” the pensioner suffered.

Sue said the ordeal began when Margaret asked May to look after their birds while she went away with her late husband Brian.

May responded by saying yes “but only if he could look at her breasts”, Sue said.

He also texted the pensioner, saying: “When Brian goes to the pub, let me know I’m coming over to see your breasts”.

May then added: “I do things for you, so you should let me see your breasts.”



Sue said her mum initially asked if it was a joke, but May “wouldn’t let it go” – despite Margaret repeatedly telling him to stop.

Following Brian’s death in December 2014, callous May even asked to attend his funeral, which the family refused.

Sue said the creep continued to message Margaret so she installed a Ring doorbell at the home as she feared May was “constantly watching her”.



She continued: “I remember looking at the footage and it shows Rob going into her garden and putting his fingers on her bras.

“He gained access by the rear garden via the closed gate.

“Some of the clothing drying was my mum’s underwear including two bras. Once he got to the clothing he has then reached out with his left arm and touched both of the bras.

“He seemed to be rubbing the inside of the cup areas.”

The incident was reported to police, and Sue said she asked officers to speak to May and give him some words of advice.



But the situation worsened in July 2025 when Margaret saw what she at first thought was a doll in May’s window.

She was horrified when a few days later she realised the “doll” was actually May stood completely naked staring into her kitchen as she made a cup of tea.

Sue and her husband attempted to gather evidence by hiding in the back of her mum’s care while Margaret followed her usual routine.

Recalling what she saw, she said: “At the time my mum went out in the car, we watched Rob remove the net curtains and we started the video recording.

“It showed him completely naked, masturbating in his flat window.



“He tried to deny it when we reported it to police, and said he was rubbing in Deep Heat.”

May initially pleaded not guilty to the offence but later changed his plea on September 15.

Sue said: “It has been 11 years of hell for my mum.

“People in the village have turned against her as she’s been accused of being out to get Rob. I feel it is time that people knew the truth.

“Rob was friends with my mum and dad. They would bring over meals for him as he was on his own. They felt sorry for him.



“She felt as if she was being stalked by him and it made her feel very uncomfortable.

“It was horrendous.

“My mum was always proud of her garden, but now she can’t even sit out in it. It has been going on for too long.”

STRONG winds are set to hit parts of England and Wales on Friday (October 23) as the Met Office issues a yellow weather warning.

Wind speeds of up to 70mph could be recorded as the Met Office warn of “injuries and danger to life”.

The Met Office has issued a yellow weather alert for wind from midnight until midday on Friday, with the forecaster warning of damaging gusts and transport disruptions.



Large swathes of the South West, parts of Wales, and a small part of the South East along the coastline around Brighton and East Sussex are covered by this warning.



According to the Met Office, the severe weather warning highlights “the potential of 50-60mph gusts, possibly up to 70mph in exposed coastal areas”, but it is not confirmed where the strongest winds will be.

Heavy rain is also forecast during this time which will make travel in the impacted areas even more difficult.



The warning comes as the weather becomes increasingly more autumnal, with low pressure bringing spells of wet weather as soon as this evening.

Deputy chief forecaster at the Met Office, Tom Crabtree, said: “An area of the forecast we’re particularly focusing on is the development of a potentially deep area of low pressure that could cross the UK overnight on Thursday and through Friday.

“It has the potential to bring some strong winds, though the location of the strongest winds will be determined by the low position.

“At this stage, people should keep an eye on the forecast and be prepared for some unsettled weather at the end of the week.”



Residents in the affected regions have been urged to secure loose items outside their homes before Friday, such as trampolines, bins, tents, sheds, fences and general garden furniture.

There is a small chance of longer journey times or cancellations due to the weather, so it is important to check travel conditions before leaving the house.

Anyone visiting beaches should stay away from large waves and cliffs on the coast, and dogs should be kept on leads.

According to the Met Office’s warning, “there is a small chance that injuries and danger to life could occur from large waves and beach material being thrown onto sea fronts, coastal roads and properties.”

News.title: Booming 70s shopping hotspot is now ‘dystopian slum’ ruled by yobs – as 40 shops shut & councillors admit it’s ‘ruined’
News.content:
TOWN FALL Booming 70s shopping hotspot is now ‘dystopian slum’ ruled by yobs – as 40 shops shut & councillors admit it’s ‘ruined’







Next

A MARKET town once hailed as a shopping hotspot of the 1970s is now a “dystopian slum” blighted by balaclava-clad yobs, locals say.

Councillors have admitted Dudley is “falling apart and ruined”, with more than 40 shopping units sitting empty in the West Midlands town.



Locals say their home has become a ghost town, despite undergoing multi-million pound regeneration plans.

Other terrified residents have also spoken of a surge in antisocial behaviour, making it unsafe to go out after dark.



Some say they dare not venture into the town due to balaclava-clad yobs on e-bikes and youths brazenly taking drugs or drinking on the streets.

And speaking at a council meeting last month, Dudley’s former mayor even starkly admitted to his colleagues that their “town is ruined.”



Councillor David Stanley said: “We have a derelict pub right in front of it which we have done nothing about.

“When you get off the tram or the bus that’s the first thing you see, the place is falling apart, when you walk up the town it is ruined.”



Depressing photos have since laid bare the town’s derelict high street with rows of boarded-up shops – a far cry from its 70s heyday.

Councillor Stanley said people had been talking about regeneration in the town for years, but little seemed to happen.

His comments struck a chord with many locals, including Harriet Manly, 40, who went as far as to say that Dudley is “dead”.



The mum-of-one said: “They have spent millions on new transport connections but nobody wants to come here as all the shops are closed.

“I won’t come into town after dark, it’s proper rough. There’s idiots in balaclavas riding e-bikes and e-scooters.

“There’s loads of shoplifting, general antisocial behaviour and fighting – it’s just grim. It looks almost dystopian.



“When you’ve got your own politicians telling you it’s falling apart, that says everything you need to know.”

For more than 800 years, the market place was the beating heart of the town.

In the 1970 and 80s, it was home to Marks & Spencer, BHS, Littlewoods, Dorothy Perkins, Woolworths, Burtons and H Samuel.

But all those big names are long gone and current market traders say the current climate is bleak.



Some have reported taking as little as £60 a day as people swap the formerly bustling high street for online shopping.

Chris Bradwick, 62, of nearby Tipton, has run a stall at the town’s historic open-air market for the last five years.

He said: “I have watched as Dudley has slowly gone to nothing day-by-day.

“It hasn’t been helped by constant broken promises by the council.”



Even Dudley Council’s own walk-in shop closed last year, while a former Debenhams is now partly occupied by a Wetherspoons pub.

The area also counts Sir Lenny Henry, Sue Lawley, Sam Allardyce and Duncan Edwards among its famous residents.

But locals say they have little more to be proud of.

Pub-goer Stephen Bradley, 33, added: “My dad used to tell me how vibrant it was in the 70s and 80s.



“But now there’s nothing worth coming into town for apart from a pint. And even then you have to have your wits about you.

“It’s a shame as I’m Black Country born and bred but there’s little hope for the next generation if you stick around these parts.”

Dudley Council has invested £24 million on a new bus-and-tram station which is due to open within weeks.

But residents have slammed the move as pointless, fuming that “there are no shops to even visit”.



This week, a seating area added as part of a £150,000 market revamp was ripped out after 16 months.

The decision was made after the the stalls became infested with pigeons and people gathering to drink alcohol.

Anne Boyd, director of growth and place at Dudley Council said: “Dudley Council is working closely with Dudley town centre traders and community groups as our programme of regeneration continues to bring investment to the town.



“Market traders in Dudley town centre recently raised concerns that marketplace seating, which was installed last year with funding from the Government’s Shared Prosperity Fund, was sometimes creating issues around antisocial behaviour.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We have now removed the seating from the marketplace with it now benefitting visitors to Himley Hall and Park.”

Dudley Council has been approached for comment.

News.title: Horrifying moment migrant cradles BABY in his arms while steering overcrowded dinghy setting off for UK
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment a migrant cradles a baby as others clamber onboard an overcrowded dinghy preparing to cross the Channel to UK shores.

A man, who appears to be piloting the boat, is seen carrying the infant while more migrants climb onto the already packed vessel in Gravelines, northern France.



The alarming video shows him help guide the dinghy towards migrants swimming in the sea during a second pick-up at the same spot.

The man has no life jacket on as he steers the boat while clutching the tiny baby held in his left arm.



The tot is wrapped in clothes and wearing a red woolly hat as the vessel prepares to set off towards Britain.

The footage was filmed by a British photographer known as the Nowhere Photographer on X on September 27.

He wrote: “One man climbed aboard carrying a baby.

“Later, during a return pickup at the exact same location, the same man was driving the boat while holding the baby in his arms.



“Let that sink in. Driving a migrant boat across the English Channel with a baby in his arms.”

He questioned whether UK authorities would hold the man accountable for endangering the child’s life and for steering the boat.

The migrant could face prosecution under a new offence of endangering life at sea, which came into force on January 5.

So far, 45 migrants have been charged under the legislation, with 20 pleading guilty and being convicted.

All 20 received immediate prison sentences ranging from 16 to 27 months.



The offence carries a maximum sentence of five years in jail.

The disturbing footage comes amid mounting concerns over the risks faced by children making the perilous crossing.

Around one in eight migrants who cross the Channel are children.



Last month, a ten-year-old was among three people who died when an overloaded boat got into difficulty off the French coast.

Fourteen children died attempting the crossing in 2024, the worst year on record.

They included one-month-old baby Maryam Bahez, from Iraqi Kurdistan, who died after slipping from her father’s hands in an overcrowded boat.

The latest pictures are also reminiscent of an incident last month when a migrant climbed aboard a dinghy after leaving a child he had been carrying floating in the water.

French emergency services rescued the child as the migrant managed to board the vessel as it set off for the UK.



Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said the latest footage showed the dangers posed by people-smuggling gangs.

He said: “These despicable people-smugglers will do anything – including endangering a baby – to get people to the UK in return for profit.

“The French authorities are allowing lives to be risked and lost right under their noses.

“This vile people-smuggler should be prosecuted and then deported the moment his feet touch UK soil.

“The fact a baby’s life is being risked shows why this illegal immigration route needs to be shut down completely.



“But neither our Government nor the French government are taking the action needed.”

Mr Philp called on the Government to adopt the Conservatives’ borders plan to end the crossings.

Some 20,935 migrants have crossed the Channel so far this year, more than 40 per cent fewer than the 36,134 who had arrived by the same point last year.

The new endangerment offence was introduced as part of a package of Labour measures aimed at tackling people-smuggling gangs.

Border officials were also given powers to seize migrants’ phones to gather intelligence on those helping them cross the Channel.



Those convicted of acts in preparation for smuggling, such as buying boat parts, now face up to 14 years in prison.

A Home Office spokesman said: “We have made progress tackling the small boats. Crossings are down significantly, and we have just recorded the lowest number of summer arrivals since 2020.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We are taking action, with joint efforts preventing over 50,000 crossing attempts and seizing 1,100 boats and engines since the election.

“Reckless criminals who put lives at risk on flimsy, overcrowded dinghies will be locked up. We have now delivered nearly 40 years’ worth of combined jail terms under our new legislation, bringing more pilots to justice.”

News.title: ‘Cursed’ 90s attraction in Britain’s ‘worst seaside town’ dubbed ‘Costa del Dole’ is set for £5.5million makeover
News.content:
Next

A “CURSED” attraction in the UK’s “worst seaside town” is set for a £5.5 million revamp in a bid to restore it to its former glory.

The amusement park, opened in the 90s, is located in a resort dubbed the “Costa del Dole”.



Children’s Village in Rhyl, Wales, could be given a lifeline thanks to a surplus of cash from a sea defence project in the area.

Officials at Denbighshire County Council have said that up to £5.5 million saved on the project could be funnelled into revamping the amusement spot.



Councillors are due to discuss the proposals at a Cabinet meeting tomorrow, October 20.

Children’s Village is not the only attraction to fail to attract tourists to the once-bustling seaside town in recent years.



Others have included the Sky Tower, which shut down in 2010.

This was followed by the closure of The Sun Centre, Europe’s first indoor surfing pool, in 2014, and Seaquarium, which closed in 2023.

This has led some locals to report that the Children’s Village has placed “a curse” on the seaside resort.



A spokesman for Denbighshire County Council told The Sun: “The Council is considering using the underspend from the Central Rhyl Coastal Defence project to support regeneration and tourism improvements at the Children’s Village.

“The proposals include improved access and landscaping, accessible public spaces, and a flexible space for community activities, with the aim of creating a more welcoming and enjoyable destination and helping to reconnect the town centre with the stunning stretches of coastline and beach. The proposed use of the funding will be discussed by Denbighshire’s Cabinet on 20 October.

“Rhyl is a proud coastal community in transition, responding to the same long-term economic and retail challenges faced by seaside towns and high streets across the country.

“More than £200 million has been invested in Rhyl over the past decade, delivering stronger coastal defences, a renewed promenade, improved housing and public spaces, an upgraded theatre and attractions including SC2, the new Queen’s Market food hall and the events space which has recently been rebranded as Arena Mike Peters, in recognition of one of Rhyl’s best-known ambassadors and most successful musical figures

“That progress continues. Around £12 million from the Pride of Place and Natural Environment Fund is expected to support further improvements to the town centre and promenade, while a further £20 million from the Plan for Neighbourhoods programme will help deliver a 10-year regeneration plan rooted in community voice, creativity, and pride.”

News.title: Where is Storm Adam now? Latest Spain weather forecast after flooding in Ibiza, Valencia and other holiday hotspots
News.content:
Next

STORM Adam continues to batter Spain after torrential rain flooded Ibiza and Valencia, disrupting flights and triggering emergency warnings across holiday hotspots.

Two women have died during the severe weather, which has inundated roads and prompted authorities to order hundreds of thousands of residents to stay indoors.



The State Meteorological Agency (Aemet) expects conditions to begin improving on Tuesday, October 20, but more downpours are forecast before the worst passes.

Where is Storm Adam now?

On Monday, October 19, Storm Adam’s upper-air centre was positioned over France, but its influence continued to bring torrential rain and thunderstorms across eastern Spain and the Balearic Islands.



Adam is also threatening southern France, where five departments – Bouches-du-Rhone, Gard, Herault, Lozere and Var – are under orange weather warnings on Monday, October 19.

Meteo-France warned that up to 300mm of rain could fall in parts of Gard and Herault, with the severe weather expected to spread east towards Provence and Corsica on Tuesday.

The worst downpours in Spain affected southern Valencia province, northern Alicante, Ibiza and Formentera.

Heavy showers have been forecast to shift towards Catalonia during the afternoon, threatening Barcelona and other coastal communities with flash flooding.

Storm Adam is a weather system known as a DANA, which forms when a pocket of cold air becomes cut off high in the atmosphere.

When it meets warm, moist air from the Mediterranean, it can trigger violent thunderstorms and torrential rain.



Aemet officially named Adam on October 16, making it the first high-impact DANA of the 2026-27 season.

What happened in Ibiza and Valencia?

Spain’s east coast suffered devastating flooding after some areas of Valencia and Alicante provinces recorded more than 700mm of rain.

The regional government ordered people in 145 municipalities to remain indoors, with helicopters deployed to rescue those trapped by rising floodwaters.

Oliva, Gandia and Pego were among the worst-affected communities, while more than 100,000 pupils had their classes suspended.

In Ibiza, torrential downpours flooded roads and parts of the airport.



Flights were suspended twice on Sunday, October 18, while airport operator Aena reported 27 cancellations and 16 diversions by the evening.

Another 37 flights were cancelled at Palma airport in Majorca.

One woman died after being swept away by a swollen stream in Cabrera de Mar, near Barcelona, while another drowned off Sagunto, near Valencia.

What are the latest Spain weather warnings?

Aemet downgraded earlier red alerts across parts of Valencia and Alicante on Monday morning, but officials warned that floodwater remained dangerous.

Issuing the red weather warning on October 17, the agency said: “The meteorological danger is extraordinary.



“Vulnerable people and property in exposed areas could suffer very serious or catastrophic impacts.”

Ibiza and Formentera were placed under an orange rain warning until 3pm local time on Monday October 19, with up to 160mm possible in 12 hours.

The Balearic government maintained a separate red civil-protection alert for Ibiza, Formentera and Majorca.

Majorca also faced heavy rain, while Catalonia‘s weather service warned of powerful showers around Barcelona and Tarragona later on Monday.

Schools in Ibiza, Formentera and Majorca have been closed for the day.



When will Storm Adam end?

Storm Adam is expected to ease across much of Spain on Tuesday, October 20, although heavy showers could persist in the northeast and the Balearic Islands.

Southern France faces further torrential rain, with orange warnings in place for Gard, Herault and Lozere on Tuesday.

Aemet’s local forecasts show showers in Ibiza on Tuesday morning, followed by clearer skies, while Valencia should become mostly dry.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Wednesday, October 21, looks brighter in both destinations, with highs of around 24C in Ibiza and 25C in Valencia.

Holidaymakers should check the latest weather warnings and confirm their flights are running before travelling, as disruption could continue even after the rain eases.

News.title: Woman says she 'closed eyes and tried not to be there' during alleged Russell Brand rape
News.content:
Warning - this report contains graphic content

A woman who alleges she was raped by Russell Brand at a bar told the police "I just closed my eyes and tried not to be there" while the attack was taking place.

In a 2023 video interview with an officer shown to the jury at his trial, the woman said she had been speaking to Brand about him hosting the Channel 4 show Big Brother's Big Mouth when he allegedly sexually assaulted her.

Brand, 51, faces seven charges in the trial - three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.

The allegations, made by six female complainants, span a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009. He denies the charges.

In her recorded interview with police, the woman said "he literally just grabbed my boobs out of nowhere in the middle of the conversation, just in the middle of a conversation and I just remember this weird maniacal grin, looming in front of me as he just grabbed my boobs."

A short while later, she said he "dragged me in the toilets" where the floor was flooded, before "he unzipped himself" and allegedly orally raped her.

The woman is the third complainant the jury have heard from in the trial - and the second to allege rape.

The pair had been attending a birthday party in Soho in London in 2004 when the alleged incidents happened.

She said after the alleged sexual assault, "The visual I remember is just this big grin - it felt like a clown, (with) that sort of weird look in the eye. It was a normal conversation about him being on Big Brother. He just moved towards (me) and grabbed both my boobs".

She said the alleged rape was "swift", and left her "in disbelief and shock".

"The toilets were behind where he stood. It was literally just grab and pull. He was holding me quite strongly on the arm and pulled me in that direction," she said.

"Part of me was saying just get it over with so you can get out of here".

"I just closed my eyes and tried not to be there. I just remember it felt like a force. I definitely said I don't want to do this," she added.

After the alleged rape, the woman, who was in her 20s at the time, said Brand "turned to me and said 'oh I guess we should swap numbers now', like it was just all normal, like he hadn't just forced me to do that."

Russell Brand denies all the charges and has pleaded not guilty.

He has said that any sexual contact if it happened, would have been consensual.

The trial continues and is expected to last for six weeks.

News.title: Inside the shadowy world of anti-Putin sabotage from within Russia
News.content:
"You will get a file... from me or a colleagueâ¦ with the proposed target. The file will contain [the target's] photo, his data, his details, date of birth, age, and a description of him. There'll be information on his car, if he has one. When you go to the target, don't take a phone," he told his volunteers.

Foma was once part of the Russian elite, so he claims to have a unique set of contacts and constant flow of insider information.

He showed Mamon on his laptop how he mapped military targets.

"This shows a database... the location of storage warehouses, and military units. Where generals liveâ¦ Where the pilots of strategic bombers who shell Ukraine live.

"In order to break the system, you need to understand how it works. Then you can aim for their weak points."

He said there were about "three dozen" people in his network split between Russia, Ukraine and elsewhere in Europe, with the contingent outside Russia providing logistical support, such as tracking targets' digital footprints.

Foma stressed that the GUR suggests the targets to be surveilled, but that he and his team check for themselves that these individuals should be considered military criminals.

"As a ruleâ¦ we also check the data [on that person]â¦ Only after that we say whether we work or not."

But he argued that his team's actions were justified.

"I want people who do terrible things on behalf of Putin and Russia in Ukraineâ¦ to understand that they'll have to pay for it. I want them to get scared."

Foma stressed that he only passed on intelligence to the Ukrainians, and his network did not carry out any assassinations themselves.

Of the assassination of Gen Sarvarov, killed in December 2025, he later texted Mamon to say: "Keeping track of him took quite an effort. He lived alternately with his mistress and his colleague. Covered his tracks and constantly changed his schedule."

But Foma did not share any plans with Mamon and the BBC in advance.

Ivan, however, was tight-lipped about the work he had been involved with, even after the event.

Foma did his own digging on Ivan.

After checking with his military intelligence contacts in both Ukraine and Russia, he thought it likely that Ivan had been involved in a plan to strike Russia's largest military drone factory at Yelabuga in June last year, external. One person was reported to have been killed in the incident.

Ivan stressed that the aim is always to try to avoid harming civilians.

Operations have clearly been risky for Ivan too.

"The most serious case was when my car was stopped for inspection and I had the handmade explosives on me. The risk was very high - however as you can see, I was not detected," he said.

To mitigate the risk of being compromised, "there is no clear structure" to the work, he said, adding he had never met and did not know the identity of others he had been working alongside.

Foma has the same rule for his operatives.

"As soon as you start gathering people in groups, in general chatsâ¦ leaving a mark on the internet, with a high probability this whole group will be quickly detained or destroyed," he said.

Ivan stressed there were few people left in Russia suitable for this kind of work.

"Most of the ideological people have either left the country or are already behind bars," he said.

Many Russians involved in sabotage work on their native soil are therefore either oblivious - for example lorry drivers unaware that their cargoes have been compromised - or are individuals who have been paid, the BBC understands.

Ivan, on the other hand, says he is doing this work for ideological reasons - he used to be a member of the political opposition. As such, his movements would be expected to be monitored closely by the Russian authorities.

So it was a surprise that he managed to frequently leave Russia and return.

News.title: Born in jail to a mum with a heroin addiction - how US teenager Abby has been affected by drugs
News.content:
Generations of Americans have endured the drugs crisis.

In 2022, 110,000 people in the United States were dying from overdoses, mostly from opioids. The number has been dropping since, down to around 70,000 last year. But that doesn't mean the opioid crisis is over.

Former heroin user Karen knows how difficult it is to quit. She was still using heroin when she got pregnant with her daughter, Abby. She is now 17 years free from hard drugs.

Karen, now a recovery worker, says the drugs being used now are more dangerous.

Synthetic opioids are more powerful and in plentiful supply - and they have transformed the drugs landscape.

Read more on this story: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis

If you are suffering distress or despair and need support, you could speak to a health professional, or an organisation that offers support. Details of help available in many countries can be found at Befrienders Worldwide, external.

A list of UK organisations that can help is available via the BBC Action Line.

News.title: Four arrested after police officer injured in shooting
News.content:
Four people have been arrested - including a woman on suspicion of causing grievous bodily harm and possessing a firearm - after a police officer was shot in Nottingham city centre.

Nottinghamshire Police said the officer had approached two suspects at a bus stop in Angel Row shortly before 04:50 BST on Sunday.

The male officer remains in hospital and is in a stable condition, the force added.

Two women, 27 and 25, and a 24-year-old man were arrested after police stopped a vehicle in the Radford area of Nottingham on Sunday evening, while a 30-year-old man was arrested in Bedfordshire in the early hours of Monday.

The 27-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of causing grievous bodily harm with intent, and possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life.

The 24-year-old man and 25-year-old woman were also arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

Separately, after stopping a vehicle in Bedfordshire, the 30-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

News.title: Trial hears Robinson 'intimidated' Daily Mail reporters
News.content:
Political activist Tommy Robinson used "bully-boy, intimidatory tactics" to frighten two Daily Mail journalists, forcing them to employ security or leave home, a court has heard.

The 43-year-old from Bedfordshire, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, is charged with two counts of harassment causing fear of violence towards reporters Andrew Young and Jacob Dirnhuber.

Opening the trial, prosecutor Ben Holt said the case was about Yaxley-Lennon's reaction to what he perceived to be "an unnecessary intrusion into his holiday" in the aftermath of the 2024 Southport attacks.

Robinson, who founded the English Defence League, entered not guilty pleas to the charges in July last year.

The judge at Southwark Crown Court, Mr Justice Cavanagh, told the jury: "This is not a trial about or an assessment of the defendant's political views."

Ben Holt, for the prosecution, described Yaxley-Lennon as a "well-known public figure" with a "large, vocal on-line following" that now included more than two million followers on social media website X.

Robinson posted on X before the trial began to thank the social media platform's owner Elon Musk for funding his case â and said his court fees to date had cost him Â£400,000.

News.title: Apu returns to The Simpsons with new voice after race row
News.content:
The Simpsons character Apu has returned to the show voiced by a new actor, after almost a decade away amid accusations of racial stereotypes.

Apu Nahasapeemapetilon - to give the much-loved shopkeeper his full name - re-appeared in Sunday's episode titled The Revengening, voiced by India-born US-raised actor Sunil Malhotra.

The character has been seen but not heard around Springfield since the October 2017 episode The Serfsons, and his big return to action had reportedly been a closely guarded secret.

Malhotra said in a statement posted on Instagram that it feels like a reclamation. "It truly is his homecoming," he said.

The character, who has been part of the long-running US animation series since 1990, was previously voiced by a white actor, Hank Azaria, putting on a heavy Indian accent.

Indian-American comic Hari Kondabolu made a documentary in 2017, titled the Problem With Apu, saying the character - a South Asian convenience store clerk - was founded on racial stereotypes.

The following year, an episode of the long-running US cartoon addressed the controversy surrounding the Indian character for the first time, making a nod to the accusations, but some viewers found it insufficient.

Others defended the show and said all its characters were stereotypes.

Azaria first announced he was stepping down from the role in 2020, and he later told Dax Shepherd's Armchair Expert podcast: "Part of me feels like I need to go around to every single Indian person in this country and personally apologise."

News.title: Companies exploiting welfare system by using residents as 'cash cows', BBC finds
News.content:
Some private companies are making huge profits and exploiting the welfare system by receiving housing benefits on behalf of residents but failing to give them the support they are required to, BBC Panorama has found.

Property agents are drawing people into the taxpayer-funded system using social media videos that offer free rooms, PlayStation consoles and even holidays.

The system - called supported exempt accommodation (SEA) - is designed for people in the UK with additional needs, including former prisoners, people recovering from addiction and women fleeing domestic abuse. It provides housing along with care, support and supervision.

For many residents it works well to help them get back on their feet, but charities, politicians and residents tell us parts of the system are being exploited.

There are often complicated, multi-layered financial and management arrangements in place.

Rather than going to residents, most welfare payments are made to non-profit registered providers. In many cases these providers then hire profit-making private companies to manage properties and deliver support.

Many vulnerable people are being used as "cash cows to generate income" that goes from the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) into "the back pocket of the landlords", said Patricia Coleman-Taylor, who runs Birmingham anti-poverty charity Narthex.

Panorama has learned the DWP paid out Â£410m for SEA in Birmingham alone in the last financial year.

The city is the epicentre of the sector, with more than 34,000 people living in SEA. For context, in London about 22,000 live in supported housing despite its population being more than seven times larger.

Labour MP Jess Phillips, whose Birmingham constituency contains large numbers of these properties, said companies spending taxpayers' money while providing a poor standard of support was "an absolute catastrophe" and bad landlords "can make loads of money".

But she added that there are some housing providers who "get this money who are absolutely providing supported accommodation".

The leader of the city council, Liberal Democrat Councillor Roger Harmer, told us that "taxpayers' money is being wasted. It's a scandal."

In Birmingham, BBC Panorama's investigation found:

Vulnerable people are being left with little to no support in often unsuitable accommodation

One big housing provider wrote off Â£1.8m because of payments to some former directors and companies they ran

Evidence that some are willing to make benefit claims for people who do not live in their properties

Supported accommodation was set up for people like Alysha.

When she escaped a violent relationship, she returned to Birmingham seeking shelter. But her family did not have room so she had to look elsewhere.

News.title: PM says youth unemployment is a 'catastrophe and a moral failure'
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has warned the UK faces an "economic catastrophe and moral failure" due to the nearly one million young people not in education, employment or training.

Writing in the Times newspaper, external, Burnham has laid out his case for the government to "invest in the success of our young people" rather than "pay for failure through the benefits system".

"Benefits will become the backstop, not the starting point," Burnham wrote in his piece published in Monday's paper.

This week, the government is expected to announce plans aimed at giving young people thousands of job opportunities. The Conservative Party has labelled the government's youth employment strategy "a disaster".

According to the latest data from the Office for National Statistics, there are almost a million people aged 16 to 24 known as Neets - not in education, employment or training.

Around 39% are unemployed while the remaining 61% are economically inactive, meaning they are not seeking work.

The number of 18 to 24-year-olds claiming unemployment-related benefits stands at 331,000, almost double the number in 2016, but lower than the peaks of around 500,000 seen after the financial crisis in 2008 and Covid in 2020.

The UK government will spend Â£353bn on welfare next year, just under half of which will go on the state pension; while the remainder is spent on benefits such as health, disability and unemployment payments.

In his opinion column, the prime minister said this reflected a "generation being denied its chance to get on in life".

"This is an economic catastrophe and a moral failure. And it must change," he wrote.

Burnham said two years of Covid lockdowns, social media that erodes "confidence and sense of belonging", an education system focused on the "university route", job markets with "too few opportunities" and failures of previous governments have all contributed to the Neets crisis.

"Today, the welfare system provides an assessment, a payment and, after that, goodbye," Burnham wrote. "Too often there is no support, no offer of skills and no opportunity to get a job."

He flagged a shift in the approach to welfare, which he said "will no longer begin by establishing which benefits a young person is entitled to" but rather "begin with their ambitions and the help they need to achieve them".

"We either invest in the success of our young people or pay for failure through the benefits system. We cannot afford to do both," Burnham wrote.

Ministers are this week set to release plans for 22,400 apprenticeships a year in businesses such as accountants, legal services and consultants, in addition to 40,000 placements in the construction industry.

The Conservative shadow business and trade secretary Julia Lopez said: "Labour have been a disaster for youth jobs. Their tax hikes and red tape have made it harder for businesses to hire, invest and grow, destroying opportunities for young people looking to take their first step on the career ladder."

The party has said they would cut Â£36bn a year from the welfare budget including by reintroducing the two-child limit for Universal Credit and restricting who receives housing benefit.

News.title: Home sellers cut asking prices on 3,000 properties a day
News.content:
Home sellers cut asking prices on more than 3,000 properties a day on average in Britain during September, according to figures from Rightmove shared exclusively with the BBC.

The property website said the total was the highest of any month for 15 years and was driven, in part, by a glut of homes on the market and some sellers setting unrealistic expectations.

The proportion of listed homes that eventually had a price cut peaked in 2023 and has remained relatively high since.

One seller - Stewart, from Leicester - said some properties were being filtered out of buyers' search results.

He sold one property, and was now selling his late mother's, and both included an element of leasehold which more buyers have been avoiding. However, he said no one thing defined whether a property would sell at a certain price.

"Part of the issue is trying to work out the right selling price. Properties were on the market high and low but were not selling," he said.

He turned down an offer made on his home a day after it was listed. It was below the asking price and he held out for better offers that never came. In the end, he sold after 18 months for Â£30,000 less than the original asking price.

Colleen Babcock, of Rightmove, said: "Once a home has been on the market for a while and then has a price reduction, some buyers start asking questions, even when there is nothing wrong with the property.

"In a market with so much choice, first impressions matter."

Property portals say buyers are now having to be choosy, with many working to a tight budget as mortgage rates have risen to three-year highs.

News.title: Schools 'explosive device' email a hoax, say police
News.content:
An email threatening that "an explosive device" is located within hundreds of schools in Northern Ireland is being treated as a "hoax" by the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI).

Assistant Chief Constable Ryan Henderson said police take "incidents of this nature very seriously" however "at this stage we consider risk to the public as low".

Some schools have closed after receiving the email, however others have decided to stay open and are taking advice from the PSNI.

Police Scotland said they are investigating emails sent to schools and are also treating threats as a hoax.

One school in Lambeg emailed parents to say that they should "come immediately" and collect children adding: "Please don't panic the children are all safe."

The email originated from outside the UK police say and similar emails have been received by some schools across the UK.

The PSNI said up to 300 schools have reported receiving the same emailed message which contained a generalised threat.

"Checks have not, at this time, resulted in anything untoward," added the PSNI.

"Based on enquiries and information to date, police are treating this email, which originated from outside the UK, as a hoax."

Henderson said police "understand the concern in the community, not to mention the disruption it has caused in some school communities and for students and parents".

"We will continue to liaise with schools impacted and have been working closely with the Department of Education and the Education Authority this morning to provide reassurance."

Police enquires into the email are continuing.

News.title: Severe weather warning issued ahead of potential UK storm later this week
News.content:
The UK may see its first named storm of the autumn as forecasts show the potential for a deep area of low pressure to cross the UK later this week.

A yellow severe weather warning has been issued by the Met Office for Friday in south-western parts of the UK.

Strong winds, with gusts as high as 70mph, are possible in the worst affected areas.

The whole of the UK will experience rain at times, including places currently in drought, but amounts will depend on the exact track of a stormy low pressure system from late Thursday.

News.title: Southport killer faces trial for alleged prison attacks
News.content:
Southport killer Axel Rudakubana is due to face trial next year after he is alleged to have thrown boiling water mixed with sugar at a prison officer.

Rudakubana, who is serving a life sentence for the murders of three young girls in 2024, appeared via videolink at the Old Bailey on Monday where he spoke only to confirm his name.

He has been charged with attempted grievous bodily harm of a prison officer, two other assaults of officers and possession of a knife or other offensive weapon across separate dates last year at HMP Belmarsh, south London.

Rudakubana was not asked to enter any pleas and a preliminary hearing has been set for 5 February, with a provisional trial date of 8 October 2027.

Rudakubana, 20, is serving a life sentence for the murders of Alice da Silva Aguiar, nine, Bebe King, six, and Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, and the attempted murder of eight other children and two adults at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class on 29 July 2024.

On 8 May last year, it is alleged he threw hot water through a hatch in his prison cell door.

It is further alleged that two days before, on 6 May, Rudakubana threatened to "soak" a female officer outside his cell if she did not pass him a newspaper and then threw liquid at her.

Rudakubana also allegedly punched a male officer on 28 October.

The offensive weapon charge relates to sharpened stone shards that the prosecution say had seemingly been prised from the floor of the defendant's cell.

In July, he was moved from HMP Belmarsh, where the attacks allegedly took place, to Broadmoor high-security psychiatric hospital.

News.title: Bereaved families could face 'unjust' tax bill after civil service pension delays
News.content:
Bereaved families affected by severe delays paying out civil service pensions could face an "unjust" tax bill, the government has been warned.

Under HMRC rules, certain lump sum pension payments must be paid within two years of the pension scheme being notified of a death to remain tax-free.

Conservative MP Sir Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, who chairs Parliament's Public Accounts Committee, said it was "unconscionable" some families could face a "death tax" through no fault of their own.

The Cabinet Office said that if delays caused a tax charge there were existing avenues to claim compensation, such as the Pensions Ombudsman.

However, the ombudsman is currently advising that standard complaints are only likely to be resolved within 18 months, with more complex cases facing a longer wait.

The Civil Service Pension scheme manages the pensions of 1.7 million public sector workers in the UK.

Outsourcing firm Capita took over the administration of the scheme from a company called MyCSP in December 2025, saying it inherited a backlog of more than 86,000 cases.

Despite a two-year transition period to prepare for the takeover, problems have persisted and by February the backlog had grown to 120,000 cases.

Retired civil servants and bereaved families have been left waiting months for pension payments, with some struggling to pay bills.

News.title: Prime minister visits Aberfan ahead of 60th anniversary of 'horrifying tragedy'
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has visited Aberfan ahead of the Welsh mining village marking 60 years since a coal waste tip collapsed and engulfed a school, killing 144 children and adults.

Burnham laid a wreath at the memorial garden on Monday, alongside survivor Jeff Edwards, who was one of the last children to be brought out alive from the rubble, and Welsh Secretary Stephen Kinnock.

"It's been 60 years since one of the most horrifying tragedies this country has ever seen. All of those children lost," Burnham said.

On 21 October 1966, 116 children and 28 adults were killed when a colliery spoil tip collapsed, catastrophically engulfing a primary school and surrounding houses.

A survivor who spoke to the prime minister said that although she felt some "guilt" and missed those who died, it was important for her to talk about what happened.

The prime minister said the tragedy was something his parents had told him about when he was growing up, adding that he was there to "recognise the community" and what they had been through.

"The strength of the community today is something to see and something to feel," he said.

"To say also to them, I don't think Aberfan was treated properly by the authorities and that also needs to be recognised.

"Because at a moment like this, I think all of those things need to be said and it's right that the prime minister is here to say that to them."

News.title: People playing loud music on buses could face £100 fine
News.content:
Passengers who play loud music on buses in England could be fined up to Â£100 under an attempt by the government to crack down on antisocial behaviour.

The measures also seek to tackle littering, vaping and threatening behaviour to help improve journeys on all forms of public transport.

Offenders on buses could be issued with the fines under new powers for local authorities.

There have been laws against playing loud music, as well as singing, on trains since 2005 but the government will remind rail passengers of this with the launch of a national campaign asking people to "share the carriage, not the noise".

The proposed crackdown has been welcomed by campaigners, but some have questioned how it can be enforced.

"We've all been on the train when someone starts blasting music or videos from their phone. It gets on your nerves and can quickly spoil the journey," said Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

The phenomenon has been given many terms - including loudcasting or sodcasting - and in recent years, Ofcom, YouGov and Transport for London (TfL) have all published polls showing the vast majority of people dislike it.

The rail campaign will be launched across operator websites, social media, and in carriages.

Under existing powers, those who are asked to stop and refuse could be removed from a train or fined up to Â£1,000.

The government also said it had issued new guidance to local authorities on powers - which were introduced earlier this year - to help them crackdown on loud music and other antisocial behaviour on buses in England.

These new powers allow them to impose new rules on buses, but still need to be signed off by the Transport Secretary

Those who commit offences could face fixed penalties of up to Â£100.

The government says bus drivers will not be responsible for enforcing the new rules. It says authorised officers, including Transport Safety Officers and the Police, will deal with the incidents.

Commenting on how fines will be enforced, Chris McDonald, Minister for Science, Research and Innovation, told BBC Breakfast that passengers can complain to staff "or the British Transport Police if they wish".

"They don't have to tackle the individual themselves if they don't feel confident to do that," he said.

Justin from Newcastle-upon-Tyne, welcomed the proposal but wanted to know how it would be enforced.

He told the BBC noise on public transport had stopped him from using buses "due to the levels of antisocial behaviour including this unwanted attendance to someone's social media doom scrolling audio concert".

He said he'd "much rather enjoy my own company with my own music in the isolation of my car".

Transport for London, which operates London Underground, already has byelaws in place to prohibit people playing music or content aloud.

It said that in the first instance enforcement officers will ask the passenger to stop.

"Most people comply at this stage," it said, but added that if someone refuses, they may be asked to leave the train or they could be reported for possible prosecution.

News.title: Sentebale charity ‘pauses defamation claims against Prince Harry’ amid financial strain
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A charity co-founded by Prince Harry has reportedly paused its High Court defamation claim against him after it accused him of a “co-ordinated adverse media campaign”.

Sentebale, which was founded by the Duke of Sussex and Prince Seeiso of Lesotho in 2006, had claimed the royal had caused “operational disruption and reputational harm” after resigning in 2025.

The Duke had made it clear he intended to clear his name and was prepared to go to trial, which could see the charity liable for the costs of both sides if they were unsuccessful in proving their claims.

The Telegraph now reports that Sentebale has stalled its legal action over concerns that the charity could be forced to fold if made to cover legal bills.

The organisation’s annual report shows a 20 per cent drop in income since the public fallout, which is attributed to “lower event income, reduced gifts in kind and lower donations from trusts and foundations”.

open image in gallery Harry co-founded Sentebale with Prince Seeiso of Lesotho in 2006 (Chris Jackson/PA) ( PA Archive )

Overall income dropped from £2.345m in 2024 over a 16-month period to £2.024 in 2025 over a 12-month period, while net assets dropped from £567,000 at the end of 2024 to £250,000 at the end of 2025.

General reserves were in deficit by £10,000 while income from events dropped from £715,000 to just £70,000.

Gifts in kind dropped from £321,000 to £41,000.

Sentebale, which was founded in the memory of Princess Diana, is aimed to support children affected by HIV in Botswana and Lesotho.

Founders Harry and Prince Seeiso previously stepped down as the charity’s patrons in support of a group of trustees, who resigned after a dispute with board of trustees chairwoman Dr Sophie Chandauka.

Dr Chanduaka had accused the board of harassment and bullying, and had suggested that the charity was a vanity project for the duke.

open image in gallery The Duke of Sussex with Sentebale chairwoman Dr Sophie Chandauka, during a fundraising polo match for Sentebale (Yaroslav Sabitov/PA) ( PA Wire )

The Charity Commission subsequently published a report into the episode, criticising all sides for making the fallout public with interviews and statements.

The commission criticised all parties in the dispute for allowing it to play out publicly and described how all trustees contributed to a “missed opportunity” to resolve the issues that led to the serious disagreement, which risked undermining public trust in charities generally.

The regulator, which cannot investigate individual allegations of bullying, found no evidence of systemic bullying or harassment, including misogyny at the charity, but acknowledged “the strong perception of ill treatment” felt by some involved.

A source said in August 2025 that Harry had been left emotionally devastated by the events, after 19 years of working with the charity.

News.title: Selena Gomez says nicotine vaping habit has permanently changed her voice
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Selena Gomez has urged people not to take up vaping, saying the habit changed her voice.

The 34-year-old singer and actress has quit nicotine vapes and encouraged others to follow her lead.

In a clip posted to her Instagram Stories, Gomez said: “I’m not going to be able to change my voice. I vaped nicotine a lot.”

Gomez added: “Nicotine is so hard to quit. I think I just wanted to say if you’re going through it or if you’re even trying to vape, it’s just not worth it. It’s so stupid and it’s changed my voice.

“If you guys don’t like listening to my voice, that’s totally understandable, I don’t mind. Just don’t listen to it.”

She said: “I am really excited because I stopped and I just hope I can keep it up. “It’s really hard but I know if you’re going through something, you can get through it too. It sucks.”

open image in gallery Gomez says she has now quit nicotine vapes ( AP )

Gomez has found staying away from nicotine difficult but encouraged others trying to quit to keep going.

The NHS notes that nicotine vapes should only be used to help people stop smoking and that they are less harmful than smoking.

Between 2012 and 2014, Gomez was diagnosed with lupus, an autoimmune condition that causes joint pain, skin rashes and tiredness. Lupus is relatively rare and 90 per cent of cases have been diagnosed in women, according to the NHS.

Most people diagnosed with lupus will have a near-normal life expectancy, but some are still at risk of life-threatening complications caused by the damage to organs, such as a stroke.

open image in gallery Gomez was diagnosed with lupus more than 10 years ago ( AFP/Getty )

Gomez began her career as a child actress on Barney & Friends. She later found wider fame on the Disney series Wizards of Waverly Place, which ran from 2007 to 2012.

Her most recent film role was in Emilia Perez (2024), playing Jessica Del Monte. Her music career began in the 2000s, and she has released three albums with her band, Selena Gomez & The Scene, as well as three solo albums. She married music producer Benny Blanco in September 2025.

News.title: Australian MP in critical condition after ‘attack’ outside office
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

An Australian lawmaker is in a critical condition after being “attacked” outside her electoral office in Wangaratta, northeast of Melbourne, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said.

Independent ⁠MP ​Helen ⁠Haines, 65, was airlifted to hospital with critical injuries after being struck by a white Toyota Land Cruiser about 3.35pm on Monday, Victoria Police said.

"All of our thoughts are with Helen, her family, her friends, her team, and her community at this extremely difficult time. We are praying for her full recovery," Albanese told a news conference on Monday evening following the “serious incident”.

Police said a 43-year-old suspect had been arrested.

Acting Superintendent Ashley Mason said there was no further threat to the public and that they were treating it as an isolated incident.

open image in gallery Independent MP Helen Haines ( Getty )

Albanese told ABC's 730 programme: "This wasn’t an accident. There was a deliberate act; it would appear.”

Earlier, he told reporters: “There is a major police investigation underway, and I can confirm that a suspect is in custody.

“The Australian Federal Police, Victoria Police and ASIO are working together on this.

“The Joint Counter Terrorism Team has been activated, but the motive is not known.

“Helen Haines is incredibly hardworking. She is fiercely intelligent but most importantly she is just a thoroughly decent human being. Full of integrity and respected right across the parliament and by everyone who comes into contact with her.

“She is a well-loved member of her community, and this will come as an incredible shock to her community.”

Haines, a mother of three, is an Independent MP for the Indi division in Victoria.

She spent three decades working in rural healthcare as a nurse, midwife and academic, completing a doctoral thesis at Sweden's Uppsala University on childbirth before she was elected to the House of Representatives in 2019 and re-elected in 2022 and 2025.

Haines' election made history as the first independent to succeed another independent, Cathy McGowan, in the same seat in Australia's parliament.

In parliament, she has championed causes including climate change, regional housing and worked with the ruling Labor government to establish a National Anti-Corruption Commission.

In a post on her Facebook page, Haines’ family said: "We thank the swift assistance of bystanders and the dedicated health workers who assisted her, and police for their response.

“Our family, and Helen’s staff, will be making no further comment at this time, and ask that their privacy be respected by the public and media.

“Please keep Helen in your thoughts.”

In a statement, Victoria Police said: “It is understood a white Toyota Land Cruiser struck the 65-year-old woman outside an office on Murphy Street about 3.35pm.

“When he exited the Toyota, the driver, a 43-year-old Tarrawingee man, was arrested at the scene by a passerby. He will be interviewed in relation to the incident.

“The woman was taken to hospital with critical injuries. A knife was located by police and seized from inside the Toyota.

“At this stage, police are investigating as to whether this was an intentional act.

“It is not known yet if the parties are known to each other. Major Collision Investigation Unit detectives are en route. The investigation remains ongoing.”

Victoria Premier Ben Carroll said he was “deeply appalled by this violent attack on Helen Haines”.

“My thoughts - and the thoughts of all Victorians - are with Helen, her family, her friends, her colleagues and her community. I know how devastating this will be for the Wangaratta community and all those who Helen represents.

“Thank you to police, paramedics, firefighters and witnesses for their immediate response.”

open image in gallery Haines is an Independent MP for the Indi division in Victoria ( Getty )

The episode has renewed safety concerns for Australian lawmakers, in a country where politicians have historically been highly accessible to the public and usually go about their business without security officers present. But public incitement against officials is growing.

Australian Federal Police Commissioner Krissy Barrett said in 2025 that threats against parliamentarians had doubled over the past three years.

Police data showed more than 1,000 such threats against politicians in the 2025-2026 financial year, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said Monday.

In Britain, murders of politicians have prompted bolstered security. Labour lawmaker Jo Cox was shot and stabbed in 2016 by a far-right extremist, and Conservative David Amess was stabbed in 2021 by an attacker inspired by the Islamic State group.

open image in gallery Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and MP Helen Haines ( Reuters )

When asked whether the increased anger around politics had led to worries about attacks on politicians, the prime minister pointed to the anonymity of online content.

"The concern, if you look at anyone's social media feeds and look at the comments, people will say things that they would never say face to face. But the temperature has undoubtedly been increased. Not just here in Australia, of course. We've seen incidents internationally as well," he said.

"Here in Australia, it is a good thing that politicians are able to go about their community and engage with people. I don't want to see a political system in which you can't have conversations with people at the supermarket, in the street, at street meetings, public forums. That's an important part of our democracy."

Opposition Leader Angus Taylor described it as a "shocking day" for Australia.

"Our nation cannot become a place where violent attacks are normalised," he said.
