News.title: The GTA VI song proving to be an unlikely hit with Gen Z
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A classic Cliff Richard song is enjoying a new wave of popularity among younger music fans, after it was unveiled as part of the soundtrack for Grand Theft Auto VI.

The 1976 hit features in the hugely anticipated video game along with other Seventies and Eighties tracks like “But I Think It’s a Dream” from duo Captain and Tennille, “Everybody Have Fun Tonight” from Wang Chung and “Let Your Love Flow” by the Bellamy Brothers.

Since the soundtrack for the video game sequel was announced, all of the featured songs have seen a major surge in streams – “Devil Woman” increased its plays on Spotify by 325 per cent, according to reports last month.

The song originally appeared on Richards’ 18th studio album, I’m Nearly Famous, which helped bring him back into the public consciousness as an artist still capable of producing hits.

“Devil Woman” in particular was considered to show a new, edgier side to Richard and remains one of his biggest hits, at the time peaking at No 9 in the UK and also becoming his first Top 10 in the US, charting at No 6.

It has already enjoyed additional success thanks to its use in the 2017 film I, Tonya, which starred Hollywood actor Margot Robbie as figure skater Tonya Harding.

open image in gallery Cliff Richard in 1977, the year after releasing ‘Devil Woman’ ( Getty )

Gen Z in particular seem to be fans of the track, which is used prominently in an extended look at the game.

“The best song from the extended look, I've been hooked on it since August,” one fan wrote in a widely shared post to X this month.

One 21-year-old fan proudly shared that she’d tracked down the song on vinyl after hearing it used in the trailer.

Others shared their surprise that Richard appeared on the soundtrack, while praising the selection: “Who would’ve thought that Sir Cliff Richard would be on the OST for GTA 6,” one fan said. “Great song to pick though.”

“A Cliff Richard song in GTA VI has sent my head to Mars! Devil Woman is a certified banger though!” another fan wrote.

“Cliff Richard jumpscare in the GTA 6 extended look,” one joked.

open image in gallery A still from the extended look at GTA VI ( Rockstar Games/YouTube )

Video games and TV shows for younger audiences, along with the social media platform TikTok, have in recent years proved to be huge launchpads when it comes to introducing classic artists to younger audiences.

A viral TikTok of a man skateboarding down a highway while drinking cranberry juice to Fleetwood Mac’s song “Dreams” sent the track back into the charts in 2020, along with the album Rumours.

Similarly, Kate Bush’s hit “Running Up That Hill” surged to No 1 on the Official Singles Chart in the UK when it was used in a pivotal scene for Netflix’s sci-fi series Stranger Things in 2022.

So while Richard might seem painfully uncool to some, Gen Z seem refreshingly unconcerned and are instead just enjoying their new music discovery.

The eclectic GTA VI soundtrack will feature 34 new songs, including Yung Lean ft. Future and Metro Boomin with “That's It”; Travis Scott with “Rhyno” produced by Daft Punk's Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo; and CA7RIEL and Paco Amoroso, PinkPantheress, Fred again.. and Étienne de Crécy with “Sexy Magic”.

Also confirmed are Morgan Wallen with “The Last Thing You Need”; Rauw Alejandro with “Macacoa 2000”, and Keith Richards with “Bright Lights, Big City”; the game's radio stations will feature Bad Bunny, Lana Del Rey, and Robyn, with Slayer's King Kerry and Tom Araya confirmed as hosts.

Elsewhere in the GTA VI universe, French electronic duo Justice were revealed as the original score composers for the game last week.

GTA VI is out on 17 November.

News.title: Trump heads to Kansas amid concerns over a costly harvest season
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

For Glenn Brunkow, a fifth-generation farmer in Kansas, autumn is famously "go time," a busy period spent harvesting fields, transporting yields to town, and transferring livestock from summer pastures to their winter homes.

This year, agricultural workers are navigating the harvest alongside diesel fuel prices that have climbed by more than $2.50 per gallon compared to last year, compounding pressures from rising costs, volatile markets and shrinking profits.

"It seems like it’s coming at us from all directions," said Brunkow, president of the Kansas Farm Bureau.

The economic struggles are becoming a significant political issue for Republicans in states long considered party strongholds. President Donald Trump is traveling to Kansas on Monday before visiting Iowa later in the week, marking his latest effort to energize his base in the final weeks leading up to the midterm elections.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump is heading to Kansas on Monday and Iowa later in the week ( Getty )

The travel comes as Republicans direct substantial funds into Senate contests in Kansas, Nebraska, and Iowa to offset concerns over voter engagement. The concern is particularly acute in Kansas—where Trump beat Democrat Kamala Harris by 16 percentage points in 2024—as Republican Sen. Roger Marshall faces a serious challenge from Democrat Adam Hamilton. Democrats have not won a Kansas Senate race in 94 years.

Brunkow, whose group endorsed Marshall, said he is frequently asked whether financial hardship could push Republican farmers to vote Democratic.

"I don’t think it necessarily does that," Brunkow said. "But I think it dampens the enthusiasm for agriculture producers to get to the polls."

Republican voters' frustrations with the party have deepened

Don Hineman, a western Kansas rancher and former Republican state House majority leader, said he’s seeing growing frustration among GOP voters beyond just farmers, including some who have supported Trump in multiple elections.

He said farmers understand that Trump’s tariffs have hurt their businesses and are upset over the ongoing war with Iran. Immigration has also become a source of concern, particularly after recent immigration raids in western Kansas that resulted in the detention of more than 100 people.

“We need a secure border — we can all agree on that,” Hineman said. “But we also need workable immigration policy that provides the workforce that the United States has always depended on and will always continue to need.”

Hineman said the traditional Republican argument in Kansas — that electing Democrats would empower the party’s liberal wing — is losing its effectiveness with some voters, including himself.

“I am tired of being persuaded by charges that the boogeyman is going to get us,” he said. “I am so fed up with the Republican Party and their willingness to play sycophant to our current commander in chief that I’m willing to consider alternatives.”

Debbie Geneva, 61, of Nortonville, Kansas, said she was impressed by Hamilton after he visited a local market to meet people, something she hasn't seen Marshall do. She's never voted for a Democrat, she said, but remains undecided about the Senate race.

open image in gallery Republican Sen. Roger Marshall faces a tough challenge from Democrat Adam Hamilton (right) in Kansas ( AP )

“I’ve never voted for a Democrat in my entire life, so that’s a little scary for me to be undecided,” said Geneva. "I told one of my friends that, and they can’t believe it, but that’s just the way I feel right now.”

Geneva said rising costs for healthcare and everyday expenses have added to her frustrations.

“And then of course the trade agreements," she added. “The Republicans haven’t done the Midwest any favors with that.”

Farmers face a financial squeeze

Farmers have spent months feeling the squeeze as costs for inputs like diesel, fertilizer and seed have soared due to refinery constraints and supply disruptions tied to the Iran war.

Diesel averaged $6.30 per gallon nationwide on Friday, more than 70% higher than a year ago, according to motor club AAA. The surge has been especially painful during harvest season, when farmers depend heavily on fuel to operate machinery and transport crops.

“This is a time of year when we use a lot of fuel, and there just isn’t much we can do,” Brunkow said. “The margins are tight, and anything that cuts into that margin really hurts.”

The U.S. Department of Agriculture projects that net farm income will decline by 2.6% this year as production expenses rise by 4.5%. Fuel and oil expenses alone are expected to jump nearly 30%, according to the agency’s September forecast.

open image in gallery Republicans are pouring money into Senate races in Kansas, Nebraska and Iowa amid concerns about voter enthusiasm ( Getty )

The Trump administration has attempted to ease some of those burdens. Earlier this month, Trump signed an executive order to ease limits on the tax-free use of red-dyed diesel, a decision he said would save “millions” for farmers. That came after a $12 billion aid package for farmers announced by the Trump administration in December.

But those efforts have not erased frustrations among some farmers who expected their financial outlook to improve under Trump.

Brunkow said many farmers “thought it would be better” under Trump, although he thinks most would still consider him the better choice in the 2024 election.

“He’s made some unforced errors," said Brunkow. “Miscalculations, bad advice, that had unintended consequences.”

Concerns spread beyond Kansas

Trump will travel on Thursday to Iowa, where Republicans are defending competitive races for governor and Senate. The state, which Trump has carried in three consecutive presidential elections, is another agricultural stronghold where economic frustrations have become part of the political debate.

In Nebraska, Senate Republicans have poured nearly $15 million into a race between GOP Sen. Pete Ricketts and independent candidate Dan Osborn, an unprecedented amount for a state Trump won by 20 percentage points in 2024.

David McIntosh, president of the influential Club for Growth, said his group has kept a close eye on the heavy agriculture states since summer and acknowledged concerns about a drop-off in enthusiasm. His group is spending millions of dollars for GOP candidates in Kansas, Nebraska and elsewhere.

“Farmers are squeezed between higher input prices and less of an international market because of retaliatory tariffs,” McIntosh said. “The economic environment has not been good.”

Democrats, meanwhile, see an opportunity in the economic frustrations, even in states where they have struggled to win statewide elections.

Former Sen. Jon Tester, a Montana Democrat who lost reelection in 2024, said there is “no doubt” that Democrats will perform better than expected in agricultural states.

“These guys got to pay bills at the end of the month, and for a number of months now it’s been hard to do,” said Tester. “This is way beyond politics.”

A third-generation farmer, Tester said he first began farming in 1978 and witnessed the farm crisis of the 1980s, when “a fair number of my neighbors left town.”

“We’re setting up for the same kind of situation,” said Tester. “The economics in family farm production agriculture right now are probably worse right now than they were in the 1980s.”

News.title: Elon Musk promises SpaceX share for ‘every kid in America’ as tech firms fight AI unease
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Elon Musk and Anthropic will give away billions of dollars in shares to try and ease panic about artificial intelligence.

Anthropic, which makes Claude, said that least 5 per cent of its shares would be put into a “public benefit fund” that is intended to respond to concerns about the effects of AI. The company is planning an initial public offering that could value it at up to $1 trillion – which would mean that the fund is worth $50 billion.

It did not say what that money would be used for, though it ruled out political lobbying, and suggested that it was yet to decide. It said that it “might explore” the possibility of “large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations”.

After Anthropic’s announcement, Mr Musk said more specifically that he would distribute some of his shares to people. He did not explicitly say that it was intended to change people’s view of AI, or that it was a response to Anthropic’s announcement.

“Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America,” Mr Musk said in a post to his social platform X. “This will be the first of many.”

At the time of publication, SpaceX shares are worth just under $150, having risen more than 2 per cent in the wake of Mr Musk’s announcement. There are roughly 72 million children in America, valuing the giveaway at over $10 billion, though it represents only a small portion of Mr Musk’s 4.8 billion total shares.

Anthropic was less specific about the value of its fund. It said that it would initially commit 5 per cent of shares to the work, but that a further 2 per cent would be added “for every 50 per cent increase in the company’s value above a set baseline”.

“Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good,” it said.

“It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit.”

It said that it would share more about the way the fund would work, including those valuation milestones, in the “coming months”. It also committed to report on its progress through a public benefit report.

Anthropic was already founded as a public benefit corporation, a structure that is intended to show that it is working to make the world better as well as maximise shareholder value. That does not come with any particular requirements about the work it does, however.

It said that most of the work in pursuit of that mission “takes place inside the company” at the moment, pointing to work on AI safety, biomedical research, and giving discounted access to Claude for researchers. The fund will have more “flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways”, it claimed.

News.title: Three things to watch on stock market this week after sharp fall in tech share prices
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Tech stocks suffered steep drops in the second half of last week, as investors battled more concerns over the cost of AI infrastructure and ongoing global inflation worries.

And London’s primary index, the FTSE 100, fell almost 1 per cent on Monday morning in a tricky start to the final two weeks before the Budget.

Rising inflation makes it more likely central banks will raise interest rates. Getting a higher return on their cash without any risk can make people less likely to take additional risk by investing in shares, which can lead to them pulling money from stock markets.

Meanwhile, while some of the tech giants report enormous revenue and profits as more companies and consumers spend money on artificial intelligence, there are worries over how long the spending will last - and whether the huge fees on data centres, ever-improving chips and supply chains will actually lead to sustained profits in the future.

Here are three things to watch in the coming days in the market and in the lead-up to John Healey’s Budget.

open image in gallery Banks could be hit by additional taxes in the Budget ( AFP/Getty )

Traders bet against British banks’ share prices

Rumours of a rise in bank surcharge taxes have seen a wave of investors bet that London-listed financial institutions could take a hit to their shares too.

Data from investing platform IG showed a surge of 69 per cent in short-selling activity – in other words, investors speculating that prices will go down rather than up.

NatWest and Lloyds are hardest hit in this regard, whereas HSBC - which has huge operations globally and particularly in Asia - was exempt from this trend, with short-selling decreasing.

Angeline Ong, technical analyst at the firm, said the question now was over “how hard the Chancellor is prepared to hit the sector.”

“If the government goes too far, it risks punishing the very institutions it needs to support lending, investment and economic growth,” Ms Ong added.

CoreWeave and plunging trust

One of the big investor stories last week was CoreWeave, with shares falling more than a quarter (25 per cent) in just the past five days and down more than by more than half (56 per cent) over the last year.

A neocloud company which effectively rents out computing space for AI model training, the company’s debt was a big focus of last week as the repayment rate they’d have to renew further borrowing at shot higher.

open image in gallery Coreweave shares will rise slightly on Monday when the market opens ( Reuters )

The company, and some analysts, insist it’s not much of an issue - but comment on social media from Elon Musk (well, one word, “yikes”) and wider concerns over a potential AI “bubble” meant investors stampeded for the exit.

It’s up around 2.5 per cent in pre-trading before US markets open on Monday, but remains well down on the prices of even six months ago - despite Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang having “justified his company’s investment” in the firm, said Susannah Streeter, investment strategist at Wealth Club.

Tech giants reporting latest profits

Finally, among the big names in tech seeing falling share prices last week were Dell, down more than 22 per cent, and Intel, down around 15 per cent.

But this week the focus will be on some huge companies with big expectations on their numbers as they report their latest financials.

“Investors will be kept busy this week with updates from ‘Magnificent Seven’ members Tesla and Netflix, while elsewhere companies such as Ford, General Motors, American Express, IBM and AT&T will report amid another important week where expectations are high,” said interactive investors’ head of markets, Richard Hunter.

Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, added that previous dips in certain stocks this year so far have proven opportunities to buy at lower prices - and the same could yet be true again.

“Although volatility spiked last week, the recent bumps in the road for the AI trade have been short lived,” she sad. “Could signs of robust capex spending at Meta and Tesla rejuvenate the chip trade? Valuations fell sharply last week, and we think any sign that revenue growth for the chip makers like SanDisk, Micron, AMD, Nvidia etc. will continue to expand in the coming months could be used as a buying opportunity.”

News.title: Arsenal late show keeps heat on Man City
News.content:
In the ordinary course of a Premier League season, you would say Manchester City have applied pressure on Arsenal by opening up a six-point lead before the champions play at Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

This is not a normal Premier League season though, and we await to discover if the top of the league table is simply a mirage.

Regardless, Mikel Arteta and his Arsenal players have their own motivations to accumulate as many points as possible before January as they seek to retain the title for the first time since the 1930s.

Arsenal have struggled at the City Ground, drawing 0-0 on their last two Premier League visits. They also lost at Forest in May 2023, a result which confirmed Manchester City as champions at Arsenal’s expense, and were knocked out of the FA Cup by Forest in January 2022.

Forest are yet to score a home league goal under Oliver Glasner, another data point suggesting this will be a low-scoring game.

That might not be the full story though, with Forest creating a hatful of chances in their defeat at Crystal Palace last week and Arsenal also playing a more inventive, technical game with the ball so far this season.

Arsenal have yet to score from a non-penalty set-piece, and their percentage of goals from open play is now the highest in the Premier League.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt after sustaining what Glasner described as a “minor muscle injury” at Palace and his involvement in the game will be a last-minute call. With the exception of Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie and long-term absentee William Saliba, Arsenal’s squad is in pretty good health. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz, Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White could be recalled to Arteta’s starting XI after starting the Champions League win over Lille on the bench.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough
News.content:
Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

News.title: Pierre Sage fears for his Crystal Palace future after Brighton humiliation
News.content:
Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage said when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

News.title: Ruthless Daniel Dubois dispatches Fabio Wardley in just two rounds
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley.

When Wardley dragged himself out of the ring at Manchester’s Co-Op LIVE Arena, the physical damage was obvious, but the psychological sting was far deeper. Wardley had Dubois severely hurt early on, flooring the Londoner twice and teetering on the verge of a career-defining stoppage. Instead, he let the knockout slip away, allowed Dubois to find his rhythm, and was ultimately broken down and halted in the 11th round - surrendering his WBO heavyweight belt in a dramatic comeback victory.

Now, just five months after that gruelling night, the two heavyweights meet again at London’s O2 Arena in an immediate rematch that carries potentially massive implications for the entire division.

For Wardley (20-1-1, 19 KOs), the decision to trigger his rematch clause was instant. Dismissing concerns over the severe punishment he absorbed down the stretch, the Ipswich man is motivated entirely by redemption and the belief that his early success proved Dubois is beatable.

Dubois (23-3, 22 KOs), however, views things very differently. Entering as The Ring’s No. 1 heavyweight contender and a proven two-time world champion, Dubois has brushed off Wardley’s power, claiming his rival “punches like a baby” and insists Wardley threw away his one and only chance at glory in Manchester.

With Oleksandr Usyk approaching the final chapter of his career and the Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury blockbuster looming just eight weeks away, this London clash is far more than a personal grudge match. The winner won’t just walk away with the WBO strap; they will stake an undeniable claim as the torch-bearer for the heavyweight division’s next era if they can land another title fight in short order.

News.title: Newcastle jeers tell Matthias Jaissle his ‘vertical’ football is not working
News.content:
Newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

This has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

This was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

News.title: Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card
News.content:
Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

News.title: Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury
News.content:
This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso said: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”

News.title: Wallabies humiliated in ‘unacceptable’ thrashing by New Zealand
News.content:
New Zealand blew Australia off the field in an extraordinary first-half display in Sydney as they claimed a 13th successive win against the Wallabies and completed a 2-0 Bledisloe Cup clean sweep.

The annual series had already gone New Zealand’s way for a 24th successive year at Eden Park last weekend, but Australia did enough in a highly competitive first half in Auckland to suggest they could give the All Blacks a game on their home turf. And in a breathless opening six minutes in Sydney, it looked as if they might.

The ball-in-play time during that opening spell was incredible as both teams committed to fast, attacking rugby, offloading from everywhere. Like two heavyweights going toe-to-toe in the opening round of a boxing contest, throwing haymakers to see who would get knocked out first.

Ryan Lonergan produced an excellent turnover for the Wallabies to trigger an Australia counter, and the irrepressible Peter Lakai responded with one for the visitors, as the ball travelled from one end of the pitch to the other in one long unbroken spell.

But after New Zealand wing Josh Moorby finally crossed the whitewash, it was Australia who found themselves out on their feet, punch drunk.

JOSE MOURINHO’S Real Madrid replacement is already being lined up according to sensational reports in Spain.

Mourinho is one of the most decorated managers in the history of football and has had plenty of success at Madrid.



‘The Special One’ is the only manager in LaLiga history to win the league with 100 points in the 11/12 season.

Despite only just returning, club president Florentino Perez has a potential replacement lined up if things don’t take a turn for the better.



Real Madrid sit third in the division and are already six points behind Barcelona.

The upcoming El Clasico could determine the future for Mourinho if he fails to pick up a positive result at Nou Camp.



The club are on to their fourth permanent manager in under two years with Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa also sitting in the hot-seat.

Los Blancos have finished second in the last two seasons, behind arch rivals Barca.

The Portuguese manager has also had issues in the dressing room since his return.

Most notably, he has had clashes with Brazil star Vinicius Jr on multiple occasions.

Vini Jr was subbed off against AS Roma in the Champions League as his side were 3-1 down at the Stadio Olimpico after foolishly attempting a backheel which led to a Roma goal.

This led to a tense moment between the pair on the touchline with Vini Jr heckling “why did you take me off”.

Mourinho even said in an interview that Vini Jr should have left the club in the summer.

He said “If I were (Vinicius), in his place, I probably wouldn’t be here.”



One man that Perez has kept his eye on is World Cup winning manager Didier Deschamps, according to Sport.

Deschamps is currently out of work after stepping away as France boss after their exit from the World Cup this summer.

Sports.title: Fallen Champions League giants score first goal in SIXTH TIER in front of 450 fans

FORMER Champions League giants Bordeaux have scored their first goal in the SIXTH TIER of French football.

Bordeaux were one of France’s most successful clubs, winning the French top-flight six times, with the last title coming in 2009.



The club currently sit 12th in the sixth tier and occupy the relegation zone.

Bordeaux scored two goals against Aviron Bayonnais 2 and won the game 2-0 in front of around just 500 fans.



The club have only played two league games after the regional football association refused their entry into the league due to their ongoing financial chaos.

However a one euro takeover has saved the club and they will continue their climb back to the professional ranks of French football.



Their relegation in 2022 was the start of a slow and painful demise of one of Europe’s biggest clubs.

They only spent two seasons in Ligue 2 before being relegated again and being stripped of their professional status.

Their severe financial collapse has also led to termination of contracts, with the entire professional squad leaving on free transfers.

The club even had to rely on former legends like Rio Mavuba to come out of retirement in 2024 to try and help the club.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Despite this, Bordeaux have had some magnificent players in previous years who have helped them become one of France’s most recognisable clubs.

Zinedine Zidane played for the club from 1992-1996. The iconic French midfielder took the club to the UEFA Cup Final in 1996, ultimately losing to Bayern Munich 3-1.

Former Liverpool and West Ham United striker Andy Carroll also signed for the club in 2024 to help try and rebuild the fallen giant.

Along with their star-studded reputation, Bordeaux have produced some of the most promising young talents on the planet.



Real Madrid midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni and Barcelona defender Jules Kounde were apart of this illustrious academy.

Tchouameni spent seven years in the academy from 2011-2018 and Kounde from 2013-2017.

Bordeaux have seen the riches of French glory but find themselves stuck in a position no club could ever imagine.

The climb back to the promise land seems far away but with their unwavering support, anything is possible.

It adds that expulsion from the top flight is “unlikely” because it would throw the EFL into “unprecedented chaos”.

After City’s major punishment is confirmed, the club should be “allowed to rebuild” in what would be a seismic moment in English football.

Sports.title: Former Premier League stars’ surprising jobs after football from Uber driver to a detective recognised by a suspect
Sports.content:
Next

SOME footballers decide to remain in the Beautiful Game when their playing days end – but others decide on a dramatic change to bring home the bacon.

Passengers ordering an Uber in Lisbon, Portugal might have come across ex-West Ham star Hugo Porfirio at the wheel.



Influencer Andre Ramalho shared his shock after booking a ride with the ace, who made 27 appearances and scored four goals during his 1996/97 loan spell in East London.

Before another nine top-flight appearances followed at Nottingham Forest.



Now, his passengers can boast of being driven by a former Portugal international, 53, who appeared at Euro 96, earning three senior caps.

But not all encounters are as sweet with one ex-Prem centre-back being spotted across the interview table in his new detective role.

FAIR COP

Sat across the table, a suspect in a burglary case was stunned as they recognised Arjan de Zeeuw.

The former Barnsley, Portsmouth and Wigan defender, 56, made 146 Premier League appearances before his second career took him into detective work at Alkmaar.

De Zeeuw was studying medicine before starring in English football, and struggled to jump back into his studies on his return to the Netherlands.

In a 2015 Guardian interview, the ace revealed he was leaning into forensics – hoping to deal with more crime scenes.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

FIRE POWER

David Hillier needed four attempts to get into the fire service.

The former Arsenal midfielder, 56, applied after he and his wife heard a recruitment advert on the radio after returning from shopping.



And despite making 43 appearances for the Gunners, helping them win the First Division, the FA Cup and the League Cup, he struggled with the formal interviews.

But he did not give up – Hillier eventually admitted that training together, working under pressure and having an immediate result to aim for all dragged back familiar feelings from his playing days.

BATTER UP

Ken Monkou, 61, has shown what batter days look like after the Premier League.



Standing in an open kitchen with 150 hungry customers in the lunchtime rush, Monkou announced that he had opened the Delft pancake house.

Speaking to The FA in 2015, Monkou admitted it had brought back some of the pressure and excitement of playing from his Prem days.

But juggling life between Britain and the Netherlands proved too much and they only opened shop between 2007 and 2009.

HOLT EM’ UP



Grant Holt loved a tussle on the pitch as much as the next man, so much so he turned to professional wrestling in his post-Prem days.

Holt joined Forest in 2006 but truly starred at Norwich, winning the League One title in 2009/10 before securing back-to-back promotion to the Prem.

Then as he took a step back in 2022, the ace turned up in Norfolk’s non-league side Wroxham, while signing a World Association of Wrestling deal.

Dressed up as a manager, he dropkicked an opponent over the ropes to win a 40-man Royal Rumble on debut to lift the Crusher Mason Memorial Trophy.

The dad-of-three then notched another two victories before retiring unbeaten in the ring, heading back to the beautiful game – working as a Norwich academy coach and then scouting for West Ham.



BACK ON TRACK

Fabien Barthez had his pedal to the metal at the start line of the 2008 Porsche Carrera Cup France.

The ex-United and Monaco keeper was one most recognised footballers in the world in the late 1990s with his iconic bald head.

In 2016, he even set up the team Panis Barthez Competition with the 1996 Monaco Grand Prix winner with the aim of racing at Le Mans.



After reaching speeds of 206mph in 2017, Barthez was forced to retire from the competition the following year when he suffered a broken clutch three hours from the end of the race.

He’s now the goalkeeping coach for the France national team.

LEAVE YOUR MARC

With Leicester firmly in League One, the Foxes may be wishing for another Polish hardman like Marcin Wasilewski to turn up.

After helping the Midlands outfit secure the 2016 Prem title and retiring in 2020, he turned to cage fighting.



Stories of the fearless centre-back biting into a wine glass shocked fans in 2023 after it was confirmed that literally nothing would frighten the star.

GIFT OF THE GAB

Marco Gabbiadini gave up football at 35 and opted to run a ten-bed B&B in York.

Speaking to The Sun in 2023, the ex-Sunderland star revealed that he lives on-site and is well-equipped to get stuck in with manual labour around the building.

He said: “I cook breakfast some days and I’ll do some of the handyman stuff, like bleeding radiators or fixing toilets.



“I can do most things – plumbing, painting and decorating, but we will also get the professionals in too.”

POST-MATCH

A former Manchester United and England ace strutted the streets in his postman uniform, swapping a lunchtime kick-off for an early shift.

Neil Webb, 63, worked as a postman in Reading, where his day began with a 4.15am alarm.



His career also included winning the FA Cup with United in 1990 and spells at Forest.

And by May 2023, Webb said he was working as a delivery driver.

FATHER FIGURE

Gavin Peacock, 58, swapped Match of the Day for a different type of service.



The former Chelsea and Newcastle star had built up a solid broadcasting career with the BBC before he moved to Canada in 2008.

Joined by his family, Peacock began studying theology, before spending 13 years as a pastor in Calgary.

He and his wife Amanda returned to England in February 2025, and he now pastors Bethersden Baptist Church in Kent.



FRESH START

Philippe Albert, 59, is remembered for his magic finish against United, but he went on to work as a greengrocer in Belgium.

Albert spent 11 years working outside football before returning to the game as a TV pundit.

ORDER OF LAW

Stuart Ripley followed a Prem winner’s medal with a very different qualification.



After helping Blackburn lift the title in 1995, Ripley eventually enrolled at the University of Central Lancashire.

The ex-England winger qualified as a solicitor in 2010, working on football matters at law firm Brabners.

He later became a law lecturer, while he also served on the FA’s judicial panel.



WORK OF ART

Jody Craddock’s love for art started with his great-grandad’s illustrated letters from WWI.

It became respite from the day-job, before it turned into a career itself.

The 51-year-old’s old club even came calling…

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Wolves commissioned Craddock to produce artwork for all 25 matchday programmes during their 2017-18 season.

City launched an immediate appeal and claimed they had “irrefutable evidence” that would clear their name.

Should they lose the appeal, the club could face a hefty points deduction, massive fines and expulsion from the league.

But Arsenal legend Keown has shared what he knows from “rumours” that claim City’s punishment won’t be as harsh as first feared.

The former England defender believes City “might get off with huge fines” and that the case could be resolved in a matter of weeks.

He told talkSport: “They’re resolute, they believe that they’re right and their owners are giving them that firm message that irrefutable evidence will be revealed.

His co-presenter Simon Jordan took issue with Keown’s claims and said it was unlikely City would avoid a severe sanction unless they admitted wrongdoing.

City’s case is expected to be resolved well before Easter as a new fast-track process means an outcome must arrive 12 weeks after appeal.

The club’s uncertainty has not stopped the team from producing the goods on the pitch after Enzo Maresca picked up seven wins from seven to start the season.

The Cityzens were found guilty of 114 monetary infractions last month relating to a nine-year period spanning 2009 and 2018, with the Premier League accusing the club of "artificially inflating" their income via "sham" sponsorship deals. However, City have continually refuted any wrongdoing, lodging an appeal against the findings of the independent panel who found them guilty.

It means that football fans could be in for a lengthy wait until they discover City's true sanctions should they fail in their attempts to prove their innocence. According to the Mail, insiders believe that the club are in line for a hefty points deduction which would inevitably see them booted from the top flight, as well as a substantial fine.

Other punishments which have been speculated include transfer embargoes and stripping City of the titles that they won during the time period pertaining to their alleged financial breaches. Sports.title: Premier League title race becoming biggest farce of all - and there's no quick fix
Sports.content:
The title race is becoming the biggest farce of all.

Manchester City are clear at the top and appear to actually be using the Premier League case to fuel their campaign.

Enzo Maresca’s men have seven straight wins and normally we would be building it up as an exciting showdown with Arsenal and questioning whether Brighton can last the pace.

Instead, we have been left with a table which no-one is taking very seriously because of the assumption that, at some point, City will be docked all those points and there will be a reset in the title race.

‌



And at some point, you have to question whether the ongoing City case is affecting the way that the other challengers are approaching games.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Normally, there would be more tension on games. Blimey, Liverpool are nine points behind. But they’re not really, are they?

‌



It’s the same for Chelsea who might end up being surprise title challengers. Are they five points off the top? Or is it eight? Five looks do-able, eight already looks a bit intimidating. Don’t worry, because it will probably soon be five.

Would Arsenal have been more attacking at Nottingham Forest if they really needed to keep up with City? We will never know.

Brighton are proving to be one of the best stories of the season. Fabian Hurzeler has built an exciting, well-coached and attacking team.

They put three past Arsenal, smashed five past Crystal Palace and might push for a top four place. Brighton are getting some coverage and headlines but I can’t help but think they would get a bit more if the table was a reality rather than just a holding pattern.

‌



And the problem is we cannot inject the tension into the title race until we really have a clear picture of what the future holds for City.

It is impossible. What do the games mean? We certainly can’t call City’s games title showdowns.

City boss Maresca is doing brilliantly, has managed to keep his players focused and has also taken over from Pep Guardiola which felt like it would be the impossible job.

View 2 Images Man City manager Enzo Maresca is ignoring outside noise

‌



City look the best team in the Premier League right now, they are playing some of the best football and are providing great entertainment. In any normal season, we’d be building this as an epic fight between City and Arsenal.

City might just be favourites. Instead, bookies are offering odds on them going down and City fans even chanted at Ipswich supporters on Saturday: “Down with the City, you’re going down with the City.”

So, when will we know and when can we start actually looking at the table? There is a set - or recommended - timescale of 12 weeks for City’s appeal to be heard. They have lodged an appeal, they are insistent they will be cleared and they have the evidence to prove it.

The Independent Football Regulator chair David Kogan said this last week: “My understanding is that there is a prescribed process which is 12 weeks and so people are assuming it will be heard by the middle or end of January.

‌



“The Premier League have said they want this resolved within season. I think we’ll know in the early part of next year which is still of course in season.”

The Premier League statement in finding City guilty in the first instance talked about the full process (including appeal) being “concluded as soon as possible” rather than abiding to a set timescale.

The sanctions are actually separate from the appeal and could be decided and announced whenever is appropriate. But there is a feeling among clubs that the sanctions may be imposed at the same time as the appeal verdict is known.

That may mean we will know City’s fate in January. Again, that cannot be set in stone. And City could still challenge the legal process after the sanctions are imposed. So it has the potential to drag on even after the appeal outcome and punishment is delivered.

‌



That scenario would at least offer some clarity and give us back the league. Yes, the original case took too long. But actually the depth and seriousness of the case surely gives more context as to why the Premier League took as long as it did.

There is no quick fix here. And, sadly, that means the title race is well and truly on hold.

Sky Sports great and football fan favourite Chris Kamara has taken on another audacious charity challenge, not long after he collapsed during the Great North Run

Chris Kamara has announced his next great charity endeavour as part of a 500-mile run for Children In Need. That's despite his recent collapse at the Great North Run as he aims to raise money for charity in a growing list of fitness-related challenges.

‌



‌



Kamara, who was diagnosed with speech apraxia and dyspraxia in 2022, gave his wife, Anne, and two sons a scare after falling at the Great North Run. The former Sky Sports Soccer Saturday favourite ran the half marathon alongside one of his sons, Jack, as well as friend and fellow broadcaster Ben Shepherd.

‌



In the wake of his apraxia diagnosis, Kamara had to relearn how to run as the neurological condition affected his speech, balance and movement. Explaining his fall at the finish line, he said his "legs couldn't believe it...and then they collapsed below me."

‌



Barely one month after pulling off that feat, Kamara has now signed up for a Children In Need challenge before the end of the year. He and Olympian Jonny Brownlee will help children at Outwood Primary Academy Lofthouse Gate in Wakefield run 500 miles combined over four hours on November 10.

"Thankfully, it was when I was over the line. If I stay fit, I could possibly do the London [Marathon] and this run with Jonny Brownlee and the kids from Outwood Primary will be another step in my fitness [journey]."

Sports.content:
All the latest news on Manchester City's charges case, including potential points deductions and reaction from their Premier League rivals

Hello and welcome to our live blog covering the Manchester City charges on Monday, October 19.

Last month, the Premier League announced that an independent commission had found City guilty of 114 financial violations. Nevertheless, the case remains ongoing, with the club appealing the guilty verdict. A final decision this season is deemed unlikely, despite a sanctions hearing also being arranged.

The hearing will examine the possible penalties confronting City, spanning from a significant fine to removal from the Premier League. The club have additionally been warned they could be given multiple double-digit points deductions.

The majority of Premier League clubs have come to the same verdict and want City to be hit with a punishment that fits the crime if their appeal fails, and for the sanction to be applied this season.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca confirms huge Man City injury blow and gives Erling Haaland update
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca confirms huge Man City injury blow and gives Erling Haaland update

Erling Haaland came off limping after Manchester City's 3-2 win against Ipswich, making him the latest of several injury concerns for Enzo Maresca before their Champions League clash with AEK Athens

View 2 Images Erling Haaland was in pain after Manchester City beat Ipswich (Image: Neal Simpson/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Enzo Maresca has confirmed that Erling Haaland is available to face AEK Athens - but Manchester City team-mate Antoine Semenyo will be out for around eight weeks. City striker Haaland was seen limping at the end of Saturday's dramatic 3-2 victory over Ipswich.

‌



‌



Before the win, Maresca revealed that he may be forced to take the 26-year-old out of his starting line-up to avoid injury. But Haaland wasn't the only concern from the Ipswich match. Matheus Nunes and Mateo Kovacic both came off injured during the second half, while Semenyo picked up a knock after coming on as a late substitute.

‌



Ahead of City's game at home to Athens on Tuesday, Maresca provided an update by telling a press conference: "He (Haaland) can be available. We will see.

‌



"We have a session now. We have some doubts after Saturday's game. He was quite good yesterday, better. The rest are more or less okay. The only one that will be out for probably eight weeks is Antoine.

"In the first moment we expect an even worse injury so we were more worried but after the scan we are less worried. It could be eight weeks. Now the most important thing is to recover it. When he is back, around December, we have a new player. It's not muscular."

"To lose Antoine, or any player, is not good. In terms of Erling, we said we can use Antoine as a nine but we have different players to try. We will see, at the moment it is Erling, we don't need to think about another one."

Sports.title: Premier League boss already doomed as clear verdict given on first manager to be sacked
Sports.content:
Seven games into the Premier League season, the sound of axes being sharpened is getting louder. From a derby demolitions to stays of executions, the weekend saw plenty of managers' futures come into focus.

There were grumblings at Everton on Saturday as David Moyes' men suffered a 2-0 defeat to Chelsea, before boos up at Newcastle in the late kick-off. In contrast, Alvaro Arbeloa breathed a sigh of relief as he got his first win as Fulham boss.

On Sunday, Pierre Sage had a nightmare experience in his first M23 derby, as his Crystal Palace side were stuffed 5-0 by rivals Brighton. At the same time, Manchester United's draw away to Leeds eased the pressure on Michael Carrick - at least for a few days.

History tells us that when the clocks go back, the first sacking is never far away. We asked the Mirror Football team who'll be the first Premier League manager to get the chop?

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

John Cross

Pierre Sage

Sage is in serious danger as Crystal Palace boss. And I think the Frenchman is most likely to be the first Premier League manager to lose his job.

‌



It is a shame because it is so early in the season - just seven games into the league campaign - and it was undoubtedly a tricky summer with a lot of change at Selhurst Park. But you cannot lose 5-0 to your bitter rivals, and that humiliation at Brighton may ultimately go a long way to sealing his fate.

They have conceded 17 goals which is the most of any team in the Premier League. Palace chairman Steve Parish runs a very good football club and has established them as a mainstay of the Premier League, which is no mean feat considering the mess he inherited.

And he rarely puts a foot wrong. But Sage does not feel as if it is working. The league position isn't actually that bad - but the performances have been seriously lacking.

Sadly, you would have to argue they have been very uninspiring and that is a reflection of the manager. I think Palace are weighing it up and, while a change may not be immediate, Sage is undoubtedly fighting to save his job at this point.

‌



View 4 Images Pierre Sage watched his team wilt (Image: Sebastian Frej/Getty Images)

James Whaling

Alvaro Arbeloa

Arbeloa finally got off the mark for Fulham at the weekend - but it's unlikely to keep the vultures at bay for long. The Cottagers always looked like they could be in for a season of struggle after a chaotic summer, and the opening weeks have done little to dim that view.

Despite a short time as boss of Real Madrid, Arbeloa has no experience of managing in the Premier League and it has shown. They have already suffered defeats to Sunderland, Crystal Palace and Ipswich. Unless the 1-0 win over Hull triggers a change of fortunes, I can't see Arbeloa lasting too much longer.

‌



View 4 Images Alvaro Arbeloa finally got his first win (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

Nathan Ridley

Matthias Jaissle

While the likes of Alvaro Arbeloa, Pierre Sage and Michael Carrick are obvious candidates, I can't look past the full-time reaction at St James' Park on Saturday after Newcastle produced in a limp performance and lost 1-0 to Aston Villa. Jaissle always had a tough act to follow, regardless of how Magpies fans felt about Eddie Howe towards the end of his tenure.

But if Newcastle are serious about wanting to be the world's 'top club' by 2030, as CEO David Hopkinson proclaimed last December, they're running out of time. I can see them pulling the trigger early on the 38-year-old, whom the fanbase is yet to agree on.

‌



Coincidentally, Newcastle face Arbeloa's Fulham and Sage's Palace away from home in their next four games either side of a cup-league double-header against Everton. Favourable, yes, but a recipe for the sack if Jaissle can't pick up at least two wins.

Then come clashes with Arsenal, Brighton, Carrick's United and the big one: Sunderland. The German needs results - and fast.

View 4 Images Matthias Jaissle's Newcastle were booed off (Image: Michael Driver/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Matty Hewitt

Pierre Sage

‌



I think Sage is the first manager likely to be sacked this season and he's under real pressure to deliver results. The humiliation against arch-rivals Brighton at the weekend was disastrous.

The Eagles have lost key players in recent transfer windows and they haven't replaced them with the same quality. It's little surprise Oliver Glasner left the club during the summer, but their former boss is another candidate for the early boot if he doesn't get results at Nottingham Forest.

Evangelos Marinakis doesn't exactly give managers time.

‌



Scott Trotter

Pierre Sage

With the vultures already circling last month, a 5-0 defeat certainly leaves Sage the most vulnerable boss in the Premier League, especially given his strained relationship with decision-makers. While the results are far from unsalvageable at the moment, having a troublesome rapport with your superiors is not the easiest way to pass probation, and Crystal Palace may feel they need to take action.

Roberto De Zerbi's situation should be most vulnerable if Tottenham fail to beat Coventry City on Monday evening, with few excuses to hide behind following a significant summer of spending. The Lilywhites didn't have to do much to improve from two 17th-place finishes and they are sitting in a worse position at the moment.

There could also be trouble in the north east with Matthias Jaissle's Newcastle and Regis Le Bris' Sunderland side looking vulnerable enough to give some supporters twitchy backsides. Both should be afforded more time, however.

‌



Stephen Killen

Regis Le Bris

There are some candidates to be sacked first this season, whether it's Michael Carrick, Alvaro Arbeloa or Pierre Sage. But Sunderland head coach Regis Le Bris will be the first on the chopping block. Nordi Mukiele's comments post-match showed great courage but there is a deeper, underlying issue at play for the Black Cats. While they have European football and Le Bris deserves a huge amount of credit for that, their form isn't being replicated across all competitions.

They sit inside the bottom three, one point a drift of safety and before the next international break in November, he finds himself with some very winnable games against Leeds and Coventry before Chelsea on the eve of the interval. Between that, they have the Carabao Cup and two Europa League matches sandwiched in that run, Sunderland are in desperate need for an injection of inspiration. It is a critical time for the Frenchman to catapult them up the table and make a giant stride toward solidifying their Premier League status for another season. Undoubtedly, Le Bris has credit in the bank for leading Sunderland to the unthinkable and making supporters on Wearside dream again. But if form doesn't pick up, it could spell the end of the 50-year-old.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi reveals he banned phones in an effort to change Tottenham's fortunes
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi reveals he banned phones in an effort to change Tottenham's fortunes

Tottenham go into Monday's clash with Coventry looking for their first win of the Premier League season, and Roberto De Zerbi is leaving no stone unturned in his bid to lift Spurs off the bottom

View 3 Images Roberto De Zerbi laid down the law to his players (Image: Hayters TV)

Roberto De Zerbi has revealed that he put a ban on mobile phones during Tottenham's warm-weather training camp. The Spurs boss took his squad to Marbella, Spain in his latest effort to change their fortunes.

‌



‌



Tottenham are languihsing rock bottom of the Premier League table ahead of facing newly promoted Coventry in a crunch match on Monday. De Zerbi's side have mustered just three points from their opening six games, and they're now the only team still waiting for their first Premier League win of the season after Fulham beat Hull on Saturday.

‌



Spurs shelled out more than £380million in the summer transfer window, making 10 new signings after narrowly avoiding relegation last season. But after their dire start this term, De Zerbi is searching for 'solutions' that can change his side's fortunes.

‌



"We worked on the pitch, we stayed together - we removed phones from breakfast, lunch and dinner to stay together because now it is like (being on phones) all the time," the Italian told a press conference.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"We had two or three important meetings speaking about football, our situation and how everyone has to take responsibility. And nothing more.

"There were some dinners just for the players, some dinners just for the staff. As a coach you understand you have to improve, you have to change the situation and you try to find all solutions.

"I already did this type of training camp two times with Marseille and it was a good solution. I spoke with the club, with Vinai (Venkatesham), with Johan (Lange), with the owner and together we took the decision, but it's nothing special.

‌



Will Tottenham beat Coventry? Give us your score prediction in the comments section.

View 3 Images Roberto De Zerbi wanted his players to connect (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

"It's just to spend more time together because in pre-season we couldn't. We had many new players and players who came back from the World Cup. Three or four days together without family, putting the club at the top of their priorities, is normal and is good."

‌



With all eyes on Coventry, De Zerbi has been boosted by the long-awaited return of Dejan Kulusevski. The winger has been out of action for 526 days due to complications with a serious knee injury, but he's expected to be on the bench at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Meanwhile, James Maddison could start for the first time in 2026 after a long-term layoff of his own. Xavi Simons, however, will remain sidelined until the new year.

View 3 Images Dejan Kulusevski hasn't played since May 2025 (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

‌



"I am very close with Xavi Simons, for example, in this moment," De Zerbi explained. "I follow him step by step in his journey as an injured player. Like Maddison, because the management of Maddison is totally different. He is another special player and now is available to play.

"Kulusevski was a very important player, even last season when he was injured. It is a part of this job for the players, but at the same time can be a crucial moment to become better, to become stronger.

"You need to play many games to reach the best physical condition but there are players able to be important, even if they play 10, 15 or 20 minutes and James is one player like this. Right now he is ready to start the game, but I don't know if we will start with him. I'm waiting for that moment."

Sports.title: Man Utd players claim they have been banned from interviews by club after Martinez outburst
Sports.content:
Man Utd players claim they have been banned from interviews by club after Martinez outburst

It comes after Lisandro Martinez's explosive interview in the wake of United's defeat by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League last week

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes was among the players who declined to speak to media after the Leeds game (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United players claimed they had been gagged by the club following Sunday's 1-1 draw at Leeds United. It is common for United players to speak to members of the written press in the mixed zone after games, especially after a positive performance.

‌



‌



However, after the match at Elland Road, despite being asked by reporters to stop, Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha said they weren't allowed to speak.

‌



It follows Lisandro Martinez's explosive TV interview after United's 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid, in which he tore into the club's hierarchy, including director of football Jason Wilcox, for the club's perceived lack of summer transfer business.

‌



Martinez, who was fined for the outburst, subsequently apologised after clear-the-air talks with the club and played against Leeds. He received support from travelling United fans, who chanted "Argentina, Argentina, Argentina" from the away section, only to have to come off at half-time with an injury.

Man Utd may be rushed to appoint Michael Carrick's successor as new twist emerges READ MORE :

The silence from United players after the Leeds game suggests they have been asked by the club not to speak for fear of more Martinez-style tirades. However, it is understood that there had been no direct order from the club's media team for players to refrain from engaging with written reporters after the match.

Harry Maguire spoke to the club's official website after the game. He said: "You can't question the togetherness, the spirit and the fight. This is a tough place to come. Leeds have been flying in the league.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"We can be better. We have to show more quality with the ball. When you come to places like this, you can't be beaten on set-plays and we conceded a set-play which got them back in the game.

"Throughout, we felt comfortable in our shape. They didn't create too many chances. To concede a set-piece after half-time is disappointing. We had to dig in. We got a foothold at about 70 minutes and probably looked the more likely to go and win it, but a draw is probably fair."

‌



View 3 Images The silence from the players followed Lisandro Martinez's explosive interview (Image: Florencia Tan Jun - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Meanwhile, Michael Carrick claims the performance felt like a "fresh start." The United boss said: "We're not getting too carried away because we haven't won the game. I think if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons, then you get what you deserve in the end."

The draw extended United's winless Premier League run to five matches – their only win was against newly-promoted Ipswich in August – while they have won just two of their 10 games in all competitions.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Carrick was satisfied with the performance (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Not since the end of the 2018-19 season have United gone six games in all competitions without a win and it is 40 years since they won only one of their first seven top-flight games at the start of a season.

Carrick's side travel to Italy to face Cesc Fabregas's Como on Wednesday in their third Champions League game of the season before returning to Premier League action on Sunday against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Brook wants to be captain 'England fans can rely on'
Sports.content:
Harry Brook insists he wants to be a captain that "England fans and the team rely on" as we near the one-year anniversary of his altercation with a bouncer at a nightclub in New Zealand.

Brook was overlooked for the Test captaincy after Ben Stokes' international retirement this summer, while he's previously admitted that he could have been sacked as white-ball skipper for the incident in Wellington that occured just hours before an ODI against the Black Caps on Halloween last year.

Since then, Brook has stabilised an ailing 50-over side, with England winning their last three series - having lost seven of eight prior - while his T20 team currently top the world rankings.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of England against Sri Lanka in the third ODI at The Oval as Harry Brook's side clinched a series win

With just under a year to go until the 50-over World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, Brook's ODI average has also enjoyed a sizeable bump as skipper, scoring 51.3 per innings with the captaincy compared to 25.2 without.

"I've learnt a lot as a captain, I've learnt a lot as a person," Brook told the Press Association ahead of England's ODI against Pakistan on Tuesday - live on Sky Sports Cricket from 8.30am (first ball 9am) - to open their tri-series which also involves Sri Lanka.

"I know it wasn't an ideal situation [in Wellington] to put myself in, but I feel as a captain and a leader I've learnt a lot.

Image: Harry Brook was fined approximately £30,000 and given a formal warning after his altercation with a nightclub bouncer in New Zealand last year

"Responsibilities and leadership aren't just on the field, they're more so off the field as well, and actions speak louder than words.

"I enjoy the extra responsibility. I like the extra little bit of added pressure.

"I'm not going to go out there and score runs every time I bat, but I want to be the man that is in that match-winning situation who can get us over the line.

"I know there have been a few innings where I haven't managed to do that, but hopefully I've turned that corner and I can really be the man England fans and the team rely on."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England managing director Rob Key explains why it was 'the right thing to do' in giving Joe Root the Test captaincy over vice-captain Harry Brook

Brook's Test average of 53.08 is also the highest among any England batter to have played at least 20-plus matches in more than 50 years, but former captain Stokes revealed recently he told the Yorkshireman it should be as high as 65 or 70.

Asked what his reaction was to Stokes' comments, Brook replied with a laugh: "I mean, 65 or 70 is a massive average, isn't it, wow!

"Personally I'm not that bothered about the stats, I've always said I think there should be a match-winning column in your stats - that's not there.

"I write stuff down and I try and judge myself on whether I've had a match-winning performance or match-winning impact in that specific game and I try and tally it up at the end of the year and see how well I've done."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook shares his thoughts on Kevin Pietersen's impact on England's white-ball side

Brook's immediate focus is on England's tri-series against hosts Pakistan, who they open their campaign against on Tuesday in Rawalpindi, and Sri Lanka, who were beaten by the hosts in the opening match on Sunday.

Every team plays each other twice, with the top two finishers contesting the final on Halloween.

The injured Jos Buttler and rested Jofra Archer are missing from England's 16-strong squad, while Rehan Ahmed was overlooked for fellow leg-spinner Mason Crane, more than eight years after his last appearance for England.

Image: Jofra Archer is being rested for England's ODI tri-series with Pakistan and Sri Lanka

Brook added: "It's a great experience for us and with the potential of getting to a final, it gives us even more experience in those games where it's do-or-die. It's going to be one hell of a series.

"In the last six to eight months and we're certainly trending in the right direction as a squad. I think we're really building towards the make-up of the side that we want [for the 2027 World Cup].

"Me and Baz [head coach Brendon McCullum] feel like we've got a squad where if someone does go down five minutes before the toss, we're in a position where someone else can come in and fill that role perfectly well."

Sports.title: Littler to face O'Connor in European Championship Darts opener
Sports.content:
Luke Littler will face William O'Connor in his European Championship Darts opener, while Gian van Veen will start his title defence against Andrew Gilding on Thursday in Dortmund.

World champion Littler, who won two of the three European Tour events he played in this year, will seek to arrest a poor run of form which has seen him lose in the quarter-finals of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam, in the first round at the World Grand Prix and the semi-finals of the World Youth Championship.

Littler had been hoping to add the World Series of Darts, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals trophies to complete a historic clean sweep of the year. But his bid was derailed by Jonny Clayton in the Netherlands.

Dutch No 1 Van Veen - who set a new record average on the European Tour this weekend - has fond memories of Dortmund as he secured his maiden Premier title 12 months ago before his run to the World Championship final in January.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Matt Edgar discusses why Luke Littler played in the World Youth Championships and what's next for him

The 24-year-old has enjoyed a successful year on the European Tour, making the final of the season opener in Poland as well as three consecutive semi-final runs in the last three events.

Following the conclusion of the Dutch Darts Championship on Sunday, which saw Niels Zonneveld secure his first-ever European Tour title, the 32-player field for the European Championship was confirmed, with seedings based on the one-year European Tour rankings.

That victory means Zonneveld will now start his hunt for a Premier title as fourth seed and will take on Cameron Menzies.

Image: Dutchman Gian van Veen broke the European Tour record average on Saturday, and defends his title at the European Championship

World No 2 and last year's runner-up Luke Humphries kicks off his campaign as the 12th seed and will face Ryan Searle.

Ross Smith - a winner of two European Tour titles this year - enters as the top seed and will take on Karel Sedlacek.

Wessel Nijman will compete as second seed after also boasting two titles on the circuit this year and he will meet Germany's Martin Schindler.

Other notable ties include 2019 runner-up Gerwyn Price vs two-time champion Rob Cross, Kevin Doets against four-time champion Michael van Gerwen and 2018 winner James Wade against Damon Heta.
