Sports.title: England Women boss Wiegman signs new deal through to Euro 2029
Sports.content:
England Women boss Sarina Wiegman will lead the Lionesses through to the end of Euro 2029 after signing a new two-year contract extension.

The 56-year-old's previous deal was set to expire at the end of the 2027 World Cup.

The new deal gives Wiegman the chance to guide England to a third straight European Championship title after earning the Lionesses' first major trophy with Euro 2022 victory, followed by a successful defence three years later.

Under Wiegman, England also finished as World Cup runners-up in 2023 after a final defeat by Spain.

Image: Wiegman will be aiming for World Cup glory next summer

The new contract extension is set to see Wiegman's time in charge as England Women boss reach eight years after her first game in 2021.

Wiegman, who also won the 2017 Euros with her native Netherlands, said: "I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football. Working for a world-class organisation like The FA, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day.

"I am grateful to Mark Bullingham, Debbie Hewitt and the FA Board for the incredible way they have backed me, my coaches and support team and, of course, the players.

"I am honoured by their trust, which I never take for granted and want to keep this great partnership going. I have such a strong desire to see what more we can achieve together with our amazing fans.

"I also want to keep supporting the wonderful collaborative work being led by The FA across the women's game, particularly in developing young players and coaches.

"Of course, anyone who knows me will understand that my main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come. We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year."

'No one better to lead Lionesses into next two tournaments'

Image: Wiegman has won the Women's Euros three years on the bounce

Wiegman will aim to guide the Lionesses to the 2027 World Cup as England take on Ukraine over two legs in the final play-off round in December, with the winners of the tie progressing to the tournament in Brazil.

Last year, Wiegman, who has also won two Arnold Clark Cups and the first Women's Finalissima against Brazil, was voted as the Best FIFA Women's Coach for a record-extending fifth time.

FA chief executive Mark Bullingham said: "Sarina is an incredible coach, with an unparalleled record in major tournaments and I am so happy to continue to work with her for the next EURO cycle.

"While we will all remember the trophies and thrilling moments she has given us, I know she is only looking forward. There is no one better to lead the Lionesses into the next two tournaments.

"Sarina's impact on English football has been immense, and she continues to inspire so many throughout the game. We have so much more to do in the women's game and she will be instrumental in helping us to achieve that."

Wiegman's new deal will also encompass the 2027 Nations League, which serves as a qualifying tournament for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.

FA Chief Football Officer Dan Ashworth added: "We have been aware for a long time now that this is a golden age for women's football in this country, and Sarina has played a significant part.

"In Sarina, we have an elite coach who has won consistently while operating at the highest tactical level, embracing innovation and never standing still. Her record is remarkable.

"While Sarina is fuelled by a determination to keep on winning and to support the growth of the game, her humility also shines through. It is never about her but always about a desire to maximise the potential within players to be the best they can be."

'New Wiegman deal comes as a surprise'

Image: Wiegman has been in charge of England since 2021

Sky Sports' Laura Hunter:



"News of Sarina Wiegman's contract extension comes as something of a surprise. The assumption was that she would lead England into next summer's World Cup and that would likely be her fourth and final major tournament cycle.

"England have reached the final of every tournament under her charge, her record close to flawless.

"But the Dutchwoman has had to field more scrutiny over the past 12 months, much of it surrounding what many believe to be a stagnation of England's development. The bar for the Lionesses is extremely high. They are the two-time European champions and must be judged against the world's best.

"So when they fell 4-0 to Spain recently and failed to qualify automatically for Brazil 2027, it drew criticism. But it was also a necessary reality check, and an opportunity for Wiegman to embrace the change she had resisted within her squad of champions.

"There are some young, exciting talents coming through England's ranks. That much was demonstrated by 20-year-old Lexi Potter during the most recent international window.

"Wiegman must see the potential in the next generation. And there is perhaps no better coach on the international scene to help them realise that potential. Now she can focus fully on how England might go about winning their first women's World Cup - and what can be achieved beyond."

Sports.title: Merson: Brighton defeat scared Arsenal – they won’t beat Bayern
Sports.content:
The defeat to Brighton has scared Arsenal. After winning the league, they came out and played some entertaining football, but then that result happened and they’ve gone back to being an efficient machine.

It frightened them and they've reverted to type. And the type is that they won't let in any goals, and they'll make an opportunity to score a goal, and that's exactly what they did at Nottingham Forest.

I don't think I've ever seen a game where a team has that much possession and still doesn't look like scoring a goal in a month of Sundays. It was as bad as it gets.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Nottingham Forest and Arsenal.

It's unbelievable how you can have that much of the ball and not look like scoring. I used to watch Arsene Wenger's teams and they would have 30 shots from that amount of play.

Other teams have seen the blueprint to play against Arsenal: sit back and defend. It's not hard. It's not like they're going to make 20, 30 chances. The wingers don't go past anybody. No one runs beyond the ball. The ball isn't being held up. There's no real movement.

I was blown away watching their performance against Forest. I know they won by not playing well, and that's a great sign, but at the same time I thought the shackles would be off this season and they would really start playing. Bruno Guimaraes has got to play in every game. He's the one who can pass the ball.

Arsenal won't beat Bayern

I just can't see how they beat Bayern Munich this week. If I was Bayern, I'd just open the game up and just say you have a shot, we have a shot because there'll only be one winner. Can Arsenal outscore teams?

This is a massive football match. This gives you a marker for where you are in the Champions League, because you just don't know how strong these leagues are.

I like Kai Havertz. He's a good footballer. But when the Bayern Munich centre-halves go to bed, is he giving them a sleepless night? Are they awake worrying that they're playing against Havertz?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Bundesliga match between Bayern Munich and RB Leipzig.

X factor is what wins a Champions League and I don't see that at Arsenal. I don't see Havertz or Viktor Gyokeres as the difference-maker.

It's fine when you're playing against lesser teams, but it's different when you're playing against Europe's big boys. I still see Arsenal winning the league because I just think they just need one goal. I feel Manchester City need two goals every football game to win. Arsenal just need one and they'll win.

Eze might not make it at Arsenal

I've played for big teams and I've played for teams that weren't big - it's a different game. Eberechi Eze is a prime example. It's so, so different.

He was substituted at half-time against Forest, but if he played like that for Crystal Palace, he would still be on the pitch.

You've got to perform at Arsenal. You've got to play in a shape. You can't just play your own game. You can't be a free spirit at big clubs anymore.

At Palace, the team talk is 'give the ball to Eze, everything goes through him and then we'll work from there'. You go to Arsenal, there are four of them. Give the ball to Bruno. Give the ball to Bukayo Saka. Give the ball to Martin Odegaard. Give the ball to Declan Rice.

At Arsenal, he gets on the ball, and he's got to make things happen in the 25, 30 times he's touched the ball instead of the 100 times he touches the ball at Palace.

Image: Eberechi Eze has scored 11 goals in 61 appearances for Arsenal

I've seen him try to nutmeg people on the edge of his own box at Crystal Palace and lose the ball, but it's alright. That's no disrespect to Palace, but it's just different playing for a big team.

The pressure is on week in, week out at Arsenal. They can win at Forest and they'll still get criticised by people like me. That's the difference.

I remember Aston Villa away last year. Eze falls asleep at the far post, Matty Cash scores and he gets subbed at half-time. He started only one league game in the next two months.

The lad can play. He's a lovely player, but I don't know if he'll be lovely for Arsenal. I don't know if he'll get the chance because as soon as he doesn't do well, he's off.

Arsenal have too many players on the bench, so it's easy to take him off. That's the problem.

Sports.title: Spin, Crocombe and Curran: Questions for England in ODI tri-series
Sports.content:
As ever, there is little rest for the England men's cricket team.

Having completed an ODI series victory over Sri Lanka on September 27, they return to that format in the subcontinent from Tuesday as they take on Pakistan in Rawalpindi - live on Sky Sports (9am first ball) - in a tri-series that also includes Sri Lanka.

It marks the start of a packed winter schedule that goes on to feature a white-ball tour of Australia, Test trips to South Africa and Bangladesh and then a return to Australia for the pink-ball, 150th-anniversary Test match in March.

Here we look at the questions for England in this tri-series and what knock-on effects they could have for the Test challenges to come…

Will spinners press claims for Test call-ups?

Image: Will Jacks (right) may be eyeing up the Test tour of South Africa this winter

When it comes to spin bowling in white-ball cricket, England have struck on a decent formula. Adil Rashid as the main man - something he has been for well over a decade now - supported by a number of all-rounders, including Will Jacks and Liam Dawson.

In Test cricket, though, spin is a real issue. Dan Lawrence is the first-choice option for now, principally because of his batting prowess, and while Shoaib Bashir has received another central contract, he has only played two Tests in the last year.

So, this white-ball series in the subcontinent offers the chance for England's younger spinners - Jacks, James Coles and the recalled Mason Crane - to push for squad places on the Test tour of South Africa from December 17, also live on Sky Sports.

England squad for ODI tri-series Harry Brook (captain), Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker, Tom Banton, James Coles, Jordan Cox, Mason Crane, Henry Crocombe, Sam Curran, Liam Dawson, Ben Duckett, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Adil Rashid, Joe Root, Josh Tongue.

Jacks, who played in four Ashes Tests last winter, and Coles could appeal because they, like Lawrence, bring much with the bat. Crane is the only out-and-out bowler in that trio but has advanced his batting with two Championship tons for Glamorgan last term.

At the very least, Crane, in line for his first England appearance since 2018, will be keen to prove he should be Rashid's leg-spin back-up in ODI cricket and perhaps his long-term successor, too, having leapfrogged Rehan Ahmed in the white-ball pecking order.

Will we see what the fuss is about with Crocombe?

Seam bowler Henry Crocombe was awarded a two-year central contact last week despite not yet having made a senior appearance for his country. That shows the regard England hold him in and you sense he will be unleased sooner or later.

Image: Henry Crocombe was recently awarded a two-year England central contract

The 25-year-old, who will join Surrey from Sussex ahead of the 2027 domestic season, has enjoyed most success in red-ball cricket to date, with his 125 wickets in 51 matches including back-to-back hat-tricks against Somerset and Essex this campaign.

Crocombe's 50-over stats are not too shabby, though - 49 wickets in 36 matches - and the length of his central contract would suggest England view him as a multi-format bowler, alongside Jofra Archer, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson.

The Eastbourne-born quick is set to make his T20I debut in Australia in November, while he must have an excellent shout of making that Test trip to South Africa as well.

Big few months coming up for Duckett?

Another talking point from England's updated central-contract list last week was Ben Duckett missing out on a two-year extension. The batter's deal runs until 2027 so he probably shouldn't be fretting about his spot too much, although he could do with some runs.

Image: Ben Duckett could do with some big scores in this tri-series

To be fair, the 31-year-old has scored runs in ODIs since a lean time in that format towards the end of 2025 when he registered a top-score of 31 at home to South Africa and then managed only 11 in three games away to New Zealand.

But with Jacob Bethell soon to return from injury and Tom Banton having just hit his maiden ODI hundred, perhaps Duckett's opening berth is not quite as secure as it was.

If the Nottinghamshire man endures a tough time in this tri-series and then in the one-day internationals in Australia next month, chat will inevitably turn to the surety of his Test place, too.

Duckett is averaging only 23.42 across his last 11 Tests with a solitary hundred and a second-highest score of 42. His name has not really been mentioned when it comes to who will drop out of the XI when Bethell is back. He will want to keep it that way...

Will Curran audition to be the new Stokes?

Sam Curran has not played a Test match in over five years, mainly because England had Ben Stokes fulfilling the pace-bowling all-rounder job but with Stokes bowing out from international cricket this summer, in typically eye-catching style, there is a spot available.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sam Curran took three wickets in the space of six balls, including the huge scalp of Virat Kohli, as England beat India in the series-deciding third ODI at Lord's this summer

Curran would probably have been involved in the 3-0 red-ball rout of Pakistan if not for a groin injury ending his home summer early and he has surely been earmarked for a place in South Africa this winter, in the squad at least, if not the XI.

England don't need a reminder of the Surrey player's talent before he returns to the Test arena - he is whip-smart and tenacious, has variations with the ball and class with the bat, and having captained domestically, would add much-needed leadership to the group.

It's probably just a case of where his body is at after that injury.

Will England continue ODI upturn?

If you rewind to around this time last year, when England were whumped 3-0 in New Zealand, we were beginning to wonder whether the 2019 World Cup winners would have to go through the ignominy of a qualifying tournament to reach the 2027 edition in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, such was their lowly ranking.

However, back-to-back series wins in Sri Lanka and at home to India - Harry Brook's side coming from behind to win both of those assignments - assuaged any fears and they then made it three ODI series victories on the trot when they beat - no, thrashed - Sri Lanka in a decider at The Kia Oval last month.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the series-deciding third ODI at The Kia Oval on September 2027 as England hammered Sri Lanka

England will be expected to make the tri-series final as the teams ranked fifth (Pakistan), sixth (England) and seventh (Sri Lanka) meet over the next week and a bit, especially with their 50-over success against Sri Lanka already this year.

They should face a stronger Pakistan than the one they crushed in the Test arena this summer - the tri-series hosts started with a victory over Sri Lanka and have won their last three bilateral ODI series at home, including against Australia and South Africa.

If England can continue their 50-over resurgence here, it will only add to the notion that they could be genuine contenders at the 2017 World Cup, a competition they were once scrambling to qualify for.

Sports.title: NBA on Sky Sports: Live matches and big moments in 2026/27
Sports.content:
The 2026/27 NBA season is here and Sky Sports viewers have lots to look forward to.

With up to 130 live regular season games, plus matches from the playoffs including the Conference Finals and NBA Finals, there is a feast of live action heading your way.

All bases are covered with five live games on Christmas Day, plus coverage of All-Star Weekend and MLK Day, so with no further ado, here's your guide to some of the biggest moments this season…

Opening Night

The most immediate - and perhaps the most unmissable - instalment of NBA on Sky is the league's opening night on Tuesday.

The Detroit Pistons - who topped the Eastern Conference last year with an impressive 60-22 record - play host to the 2024 champions Boston Celtics at 8pm on Sky Sports Mix. The Celtics are sporting a new-look side featuring Paul George after his arrival in a high-profile trade that facilitated the departure of last year's leading scorer Jaylen Brown.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player LeBron James got 10 points, five assists and four rebounds in the first half in Philadelphia 76ers debut in preseason match against Brooklyn Nets

Later that evening, Brown joins up with LeBron James, Joel Embiid, and the rest of his new Philadelphia 76ers team-mates as they travel to Madison Square Garden to face the reigning champion New York Knicks.

The slate ends with yet another fascinating match-up: a rematch of last year's seven-game epic Western Conference Finals series between reigning MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's Oklahoma City Thunder and Victor Wembanyama's San Antonio Spurs.

Christmas Day

Christmas Day is already a staple in the NBA calendar - but this year in particular is a feast for UK fans, with five games across 12 hours of live basketball on Sky.

The day kicks off with a rematch of the 2026 Finals - Wembanyama's Spurs will look to exact their revenge on Jalen Brunson's Knicks in New York at 5pm, before Giannis Antetokounmpo's Miami Heat visit the Celtics in Boston.

Later, LeBron returns to Los Angeles as an opposing player for the first time in eight years to take on the Lakers at Staples Center, with the Thunder playing Anthony Edwards' Minnesota Timberwolves and the Denver Nuggets taking a trip to San Francisco to face Steph Curry's Golden State Warriors in the early hours of the morning.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the NBA Finals Game 5 match-up between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs

All-Star Weekend

All-Star weekend - the NBA's mid-season showpiece - will once again be shown live on Sky.

The NBA All-Star game on Sunday night headlines the weekend - but there are five other events for fans to get stuck into across the three-day event

The All-Star weekend kicks off with the Rising Stars game on Friday, with its own round robin featuring a draft selected by a plethora of honorary coaches and NBA legends to be selected closer to the time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nikola Jokic reminded everyone of his extraordinary playmaking ability in Sunday's preseason opener, whipping a sensational behind-the-back crosscourt assist to Cameron Johnson for three

The four teams are made up of players in their first and second years in the NBA - last year, the field was headlined by Mavericks No 1 pick Cooper Flagg, bar one team, which is made up entirely of players from the NBA's development affiliate, the G-League.

Saturday features the Shooting Stars contest, the three-point contest and the dunk contest.

If that wasn't enough, Friday's action finishes with the NBA All-Star Celebrity Game, before the Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU) classic takes place early on the next day.

Play-in tournament

The play-in tournament at the beginning of April - taking place just after the end of the regular season, but before the playoffs - represents one of the most emotional and consequential weekends of the NBA season.

While the teams that finish Nos. 1-6 in the standings of each conference are guaranteed a playoff spot, the teams that finish Nos. 7-10 in the standings are entered into the play-in. These teams will battle for the seventh and eighth playoff seeds.

Here is the NBA's overview of how it works:

Each conference's No. 7 team in the standings will host the No. 8 team. The winners secure the No. 7 seed in the playoffs. The losers will get another chance to earn a playoff spot.

E ach conference's No. 9 team in the standings will host the No. 10 team. The winners will advance to the final stage of the Play-In Tournament. The losers are eliminated.

The losers of the No. 7 vs. No. 8 matchups will host the winners of the No. 9 vs. No. 10 matchups. The winners secure the No. 8 seed in the NBA playoffs for its conference. The losing teams are eliminated.



2027 NBA Finals

After 1,230 regular season games and a potential 98 playoff games - it will all come down to the 2027 NBA finals, which will be live on Sky Sports.

Last season's finals saw the Knicks only require five games to beat the Spurs and secure their first NBA championship in 54 years, prompting frenzied celebrations in America's biggest city that New York will be keen to recreate in 2026.

Sports.title: US GP talking points: How will Hamilton, Norris move on from woes?
Sports.content:
Formula 1 returns to Austin's Circuit of The Americas for the United States Grand Prix with a historic championship crowning potentially in the offing, along with several other hot topics on the agenda.

All eyes on Antonelli as history beckons

The event in Texas kicks off the second of three triple-headers to end the season, with races in Mexico and Brazil immediately following this one.

There is every chance that Antonelli will become F1's youngest ever world champion on one of the next three Sundays, but it would require something quite dramatic for that to be in Austin.

Antonelli would need to win the United States Grand Prix and for his Mercedes team-mate George Russell to finish ninth or lower, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton also finishing fifth or lower.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell takes over from Kimi Antonelli's engineer during the Sprint rain delay in Singapore.

However the weekend plays out, it will be fascinating to see how Antonelli handles the pressure of the title being attainable for the first time.

Ultimately, there has been little evidence to suggest the 20-year-old will back far away from the aggressive approach that has served him so well this season, and why should he?

Will Mercedes' upgrades work better?

A key factor in determining when Antonelli seals the title could be the performance of his Mercedes car, and more specifically the upgrades that have been brought to it in recent weeks.

The Silver Arrows had projected plenty of confidence over the major package they added to the W17 at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, but it appeared to have a negative impact as they delivered arguably their least performative weekend of the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff explains Mercedes issues after big upgrade package at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia.

That led to the team taking the quite extreme step of running a full test of the upgrades the following weekend in Singapore as Antonelli drove with the new parts on his car and Russell drove with the pre-Sepang specification.

The extreme heat and nature of the surface in Malaysia made it tricky for all the teams to analyse their performance, while Singapore's Marina Bay Street Circuit is also something of an outlier on the calendar.

A return to a more traditional circuit in Austin therefore makes it a crucial weekend for Mercedes, whose plans for the development of their 2027 car will be significantly impacted if this package simply doesn't work.

Can Verstappen make it a hat-trick?

There is no longer any doubt that Max Verstappen and Red Bull are well and truly back.

The four-time world champion had to wait until the 16th round of the season for his first Grand Prix victory of 2026, but it was then just seven days before his second came along.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen wins his first ever Singapore Grand Prix.

There's no doubt that the upgrades Red Bull have gradually added to the car are working, with Verstappen having been in a league of his own over the past two weekends.

Antonelli might be on the brink of glory, but there is already a growing sense in the paddock that Verstappen could end this year and start next season as the driver to beat.

Antonelli himself admitted that it would be "very scary" if Verstappen was challenging him for the title in this form.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Sky Sports F1 Show Podcast, Bernie Collins gave huge flowers to Red Bull and their strategy after Max Verstappen's clean sweep in Singapore.

Verstappen is just eight points behind third-placed Lewis Hamilton and 17 points behind second-placed Russell in the drivers' standings, with both at major risk of being overhauled by the Dutchman in the coming weeks.

While the positions below first in the Drivers' Championship count for little, Verstappen appears as though he may be in the process of laying down a major psychological marker for next year.

How will Hamilton handle strategy error?

In contrast to the late-season momentum that Verstappen is building, his old rival Hamilton's campaign is fizzling out.

The latest downturn came in Singapore when the seven-time world champion made an inexplicable decision to ignore Ferrari's call for him to come into the pits during a Virtual Safety Car period.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's Karun Chadhok dissects Lewis Hamilton's Singapore GP race.

While stopping would have almost certainly condemned him to finishing behind team-mate Charles Leclerc, getting rid of his already worn tyres would have likely sealed a podium finish, or at worst, fourth place.

Instead, he took the chequered flag in sixth, before not showing up for his post-race interviews amid concern over his physical condition following the gruelling race.

The saga has led to speculation over a possible breakdown of trust between Hamilton and the Ferrari pit wall, with the 41-year-old having been unhappy with their choices on several other occasions this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins considers whether Lewis Hamilton has lost trust in Ferrari after overriding a team strategy call in Singapore.

Given the fact he didn't speak after the race in Singapore, there will be extra attention on his press briefings on Thursday in Austin.

While that might be intriguing, the more pressing issue is that Ferrari need to sort their act out for 2027 with the threat of Verstappen looming.

Repercussions for Norris?

If Red Bull need a warning against taking anything for granted after Verstappen's successive wins, it's glaring at them in the form of the papaya McLarens.

Either side of the summer break, it was Lando Norris who claimed his first two victories of the season in successive races in Hungary and the Netherlands.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri make contact on the final lap of the Singapore Grand Prix Sprint race.

He should have had a third in Madrid soon after, with his hugely impressive pace at each of those events leading many to believe McLaren were going to be the team to beat for the remainder of the season.

Instead, the last triple-header saw them drop painfully backwards. Norris didn't qualify higher than fifth at the three events and his best result was fourth in Singapore.

The Brit was also guilty of creating negative headlines for the team by attempting a late overtake in the Singapore Sprint on his team-mate Oscar Piastri that resulted in the pair crashing and cost them both points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok dissects who was at fault for the collision between the two McLaren's which saw Oscar Piastri crash out of the Singapore GP Sprint race.

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella and chief executive Zak Brown made it clear they were extremely unhappy with the collision, but opted against publicly criticising Norris.

Now that the team have had more time to review the incident, it will be interesting to see if Norris feels the need to make further apologies, or whether there are firmer words from the top.

Sports.title: Bayern and Luis Díaz warm up for Arsenal revenge mission with furious rout of Leipzig | Andy Brassell
Sports.content:
When Bayern Munich fail to win for two games in a row, you know what is coming next. Particularly on a Saturday night showcase, against the sort of good domestic opposition that tend to bring the best out of the champions. It had been a frustrating week, domestically and continentally, in two games on the road. On both occasions they had been caught cold, conceding the Bundesliga’s fastest goal at Augsburg and going 1-0 down in less than 90 seconds in Stavanger.

Vincent Kompany’s low profile on the Allianz Arena touchline, sat almost motionless in his seat on the bench as his team rattled a flurry of goals past poor RB Leipzig, had nothing to do with any lingering chagrin connected to those slow starts from his team. The sporting director, Max Eberl, who stood in for his coach in the post-match press conference, explained that the Belgian had been ill, not to mention Kompany’s current hip problem that had made the move from dressing room to pitch side slow and uncomfortable.

It was good he did not attempt to get up from his vantage point every time his team scored, or he would have been extremely sore in the morning. This was what Kicker referred to as a “Trainingsspiel in der Allianz Arena”. Had it not been for the goalkeeper Maarten Vandevoordt performing creditably, Leipzig’s club record defeat – a 7-0 loss to Manchester City three and a half years ago – would have been comfortably surpassed. This was carnage.

For Leipzig and their coach, the former Bayern man Martin Demichelis, this 6-1 defeat was the starkest of reality checks. The media reaction was the same, a sense of disappointment that a supposed competitor to Bayern could offer so little in terms of resistance. Yet there needed to be a recognition too that this was Bayern being their brilliant best; piqued, prickly and poked into action by a potential challenge that they felt compelled to prove wasn’t much of one.

This was a furious clearing of frustration on a number of levels; the need to defend Manuel Neuer after his early error at Augsburg, the industrial scale of chances frittered away in that game, the first-half punking by Viking in midweek, the concession of a late equaliser having come back and the red card for Michael Olise (Eberl had memorably called Viking’s captain, Zlatko Tripic, a “scumbag” for systematically winding up the France midfielder to the point at which he picked up two bookings in the blink of an eye, the second for gently lobbing the ball in Tripic’s face, forcing the latter to throw himself to the ground).

And how that feeling was expelled from the very beginning. Harry Kane called Vandevoordt into action in the opening seconds, but it was only a temporary let-off for the visitors. Luis Díaz steamed on to a Joshua Kimmich pass to fly through the centre of the Leipzig defence and give Bayern the lead in the 12th minute. The Colombian created a second with a delicious pass for the onrushing Aleksandar Pavlovic just before the half-hour, and just after a stunning collective move finished with Kane carving a chance for Olise to finish imperiously.

View image in fullscreen Michael Olise scores against RB Leipzig but he will miss the Champions League match against Arsenal on Wednesday through suspension. Photograph: Xinhua/Shutterstock

It was a recital. The move that led to the Pavlovic goal began with Kane steering the ball left from a quarter-back position, maybe 10 to 15 metres in front of his own penalty area. In the second half Díaz fully took centre stage, gathering a Kane pass to chop inside and curl a shot into the far corner, then scurrying the long way around to finish from a central area and complete his hat-trick – not the perfect hat-trick perhaps, but maybe the perfect Luis Díaz hat-trick of centre, from the left and long run around to finish. His first Bundesliga goals since August were scoffed with the demeanour of a famished man.

This version of Díaz will be needed against Arsenal with Olise suspended, and the score settling version of Bayern will be the default too, with this the perfect warm up in that sense, even if Leipzig were more compliant than might have been expected. Nobody in Munich has forgotten their first defeat of last season, 11 months ago, when Arsenal stepped up a gear and showed just how good they had become in a comprehensive second-half display at the Emirates Stadium that led to a 3-1 win. “We have memories of that game,” said Eberl, “and we want to translate those memories into energy this Wednesday.”

There is a sense of this all just being shadow-boxing, of course, in a league stage that Bayern and Arsenal will be expected to graduate from safely in the top eight. Yet any measure of where they are and where they are headed is useful. Even if this was not a win or go home situation, Saturday’s game could be the season kickstarter for Díaz who, as Kimmich said, is extremely valuable to his team in that he is the most likely to make runs behind the defence; more so than Kane, Olise, or any of their midfielders.

“He delivered incredible numbers for us last season,” Kimmich continued (22 goals and 17 assists in Bundesliga and Champions League combined) – and here it was, starting again. Even at this early stage, markers are needed and after Leipzig, Arsenal are Bayern’s next.

Talking points

Bayern ended the weekend on top of the table – ahead of Borussia Dortmund courtesy of, already, a vastly superior goal difference – thanks to previous leader Freiburg’s first loss of the season, on Sunday afternoon at Bayer Leverkusen. Julian Schuster’s side had taken an early lead at BayArena, with the in-form Derry Scherhant concluding a flowing team move but Leverkusen hit back in arguably their first proper test at home. The brilliant Ibrahim Maza quickly equalised and then laid on the second-half winner for Patrick Schick – who has now scored in each of the opening six games of the season – with a sublime assist. Maza explained to DAZN how his escape from a clutch of Freiburg defenders was straight out of his Berlin childhood. “Just playing in the cage, just improvising and going for it.”

View image in fullscreen Ibrahim Maza draws Bayer Leverkusen level against the previous Bundesliga leaders Freiburg. Photograph: Thilo Schmülgen/Reuters

Level with Schick at the top of the scoring charts is one Niclas Füllkrug, who scored for a fifth game in a row as his brace brought Werder Bremen back from 2-0 down to draw with Paderborn – the third straight game in which Werder have recovered from a two-goal deficit to take a point or more. Daniel Thioune spoke afterwards about how the (maybe soon-to-be-again?) Germany striker is raising the standards of those around him – including the coach himself. “Niclas expects a lot from a coach,” he said. “It’s not just what he does on the pitch, but also what happens in the locker room. Niclas is never too proud to go the extra mile.”

Dortmund’s tired performance in a goalless draw with Union in Berlin was a second straight scoreless game but their fellow Champions League participants Stuttgart are in a worse state, glued into the bottom six by a defeat in Hamburg in which they missed a raft of chances. “We’re not a top team right now,” bemoaned Deniz Undav.

Sports.title: Sarina Wiegman signs contract extension to stay as England women head coach until 2029
Sports.content:
Sarina Wiegman has extended her contract to continue as the head coach of England women for Euro 2029. Her deal was due to expire after next summer’s World Cup and this gives her the chance to lead the Lionesses to three European championship titles in a row.

Wiegman, who took on the role in September 2021, also led her native Netherlands to Euros glory in 2017 and has reached the final of the past five major tournaments, twice finishing as a World Cup runner-up.

“I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football,” Wiegman said. “Working for a world-class organisation like the FA, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day.”

Quick Guide How do I 

England will reach the World Cup finals, which are being in held in Brazil in June and July, if they come through a two-leg playoff against Ukraine for which they are heavy favourites. “My main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come,” Wiegman said.

This is Wiegman’s second contract extension with England and opens the possibility that she could coach Team GB at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles should the team qualify. Wiegman, who turns 57 next Monday, will continue to be assisted by Janneke Bijl, Arvid Smit and Darren Ward.

“Sarina is an incredible coach with an unparalleled record in major tournaments and I am so happy to continue to work with her for the next Euro cycle,” said the Football Association’s chief executive, Mark Bullingham.

Wiegman had refused to be drawn on questions over her future before England’s two games against Greece during the recent international break, but the Chelsea midfielder Keira Walsh last week said “obviously I’d want her to stay” when asked about the head coach’s future.

Sports.title: Konsa bullish about Arsenal’s Champions League hopes as Bayern clash looms
Sports.content:
For Ezri Konsa, it was just a wonderfully satisfying challenge. The Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap had stolen in behind him up the inside left channel on Sunday. There were 93 minutes gone, Arsenal were 1-0 up and it was now or never for Forest. Konsa decreed that it would be never, curving his covering run back, matching Delap for pace and stretching into the perfect block tackle.

So, another win for Arsenal: their 10th in 11 matches this season. Another clean sheet. And for Konsa, a continuation of what has been a dreamlike couple of months. Do points-saving last-minute challenges mean more when the defender is actually a fan of the club, too? Basically, yes.

“I’ve been asked this a lot,” Konsa says with a smile, when the subject of his boyhood allegiance is raised. “And, yes, I was [an Arsenal supporter]. I had a lot of Arsenal kits when I was younger. You dream of playing for big clubs like this. When you’re a kid, you see the likes of Arsenal, growing up, and the amount of quality players they’ve had throughout the years and to be here – and not only to be here but to be here with close friends – makes it even more special.”

Konsa is talking about Eberechi Eze, in particular; another boyhood Arsenal fan, with whom he is especially tight. Everybody has seen the clip of Eze greeting Konsa at the training ground after the latter had completed his £51m move from Aston Villa and how they crack up with laughter before embracing. It is infectious. But Konsa knows a clutch of other Arsenal players from England duty – Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ben White – and he credits them with helping him to settle in.

Konsa’s adaptation has been quick and it has needed to be with William Saliba injured. After making his Arsenal debut as a substitute at Villa – Konsa’s scriptwriters have been hard at work – he has played in every minute of the club’s Premier League and Champions League matches. The victory at Forest, where Arsenal had drawn 0-0 in each of the previous two seasons, was significant. It was not a performance of any attacking pace or spark. Perhaps it made the points feel more precious.

“We hadn’t won here in two seasons, the boss was going on about it,” Konsa says. “It’s something we wanted to change as players and these are the games you have to win. If you want to win titles, you have to come away to tough places like this and get three points.”

View image in fullscreen Konsa does battle with Liam Delap during Arsenal’s 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Things are about to get even more interesting for Konsa and Arsenal because on Wednesday they face Bayern Munich at the Allianz Arena in the Champions League. “It’s against my international teammate as well,” Konsa says, and he is straight into an appreciation of Harry Kane, the England captain, who has been on fire since joining Bayern from Tottenham in 2023. Kane’s scoring record for the club bears repeating: 155 goals in 157 appearances.

Konsa has a good record against Kane, having faced him seven times, six of them for Villa against Spurs. The seventh and most recent came in October 2024 when Konsa was in the Villa team that beat Kane’s Bayern 1-0 at Villa Park in the Champions League. It was Villa’s first home match in the competition for 41 years. Konsa has four wins against Kane’s teams and three losses. Kane has only scored twice against him, both from penalties.

“The Villa-Bayern game … to beat them at home and keep a clean sheet … it was very special for the players and the fans,” Konsa says. “I don’t really look much at those kind of stats [against individual players] but I am relishing the challenge.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The dynamics against Bayern appear different for Konsa this time. It was a famous victory for Villa that night, in part because of the tie’s history; the club beat Bayern 1-0 in the 1982 European Cup final. Villa were underdogs as they felt their way back into Europe’s elite competition. Arsenal will kick off as Bayern’s equals and among the favourites to win the tournament, having lost on penalties to Paris Saint-Germain in last season’s final.

Konsa won the first trophy of his career a week before that when he was in the Villa team that defeated Freiburg in the Europa League final. He says he has felt the determination of the Arsenal squad to go one step further in Europe.

“One hundred per cent,” Konsa says. “As players, the standards we have, the goals we have … we want to win everything – the Champions League, the Prem. Whatever trophies are in front of us. When I came to Arsenal, I wanted to win. I was hungry to win. Last season I got my hands on the Europa League and this season I want more.”

Sports.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
Sports.content:
1 Arsenal earn no respite from troubles

There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey

2 London City extend winning run

London City’s impressive start to the season continued as they extended their winning run to four games with a 2-1 victory against Everton. If the match against Tottenham before the break had been an illustration of their attacking power, this was a much grittier performance. The Toffees, who have the joint second-meanest defence in the league (shared with Eder Maestre’s team), proved tough to break down with London City managing just five shots on target despite creating 16 opportunities. Their two first-half goals, however, once again came on transition and were a sign of the deep quality they possess. Plenty has been made of London City’s attack this season but it was their out-of-possession work that shone through. They have now faced the fewest shots on target in the division (12) and the way they handled the slight change of momentum in the second half when Everton switched things up and gained belief was an indication of their growing defensive mettle. SD

View image in fullscreen London City’s Grace Geyoro protects the ball from and Everton’s Rion Ishikawa. Photograph: Jonathan Brady/PA

3 Silver linings in latest Charlton loss

Charlton may still be pointless six games in, but their second-half performance against Manchester United impressed their manager, Karen Hills. After a rough first half an hour, in which the final score of 3-1 to United was established, the home team held firm. “When we talk about bravery, I thought we took the second half to Manchester United,” said Hills. “If we can do that against a very, very top team like United, then I’m hoping that we can continue on that run. I think you saw that in the first half as well, when we actually got the ball we played some really nice football. It’s a team that’s very aggressive and on the front foot. It was just the moments when we didn’t have the ball that probably cost us today.” Given Charlton only had 23.8% possession in the match, those moments without the ball were many, but finding silver linings when you’re down is important. Suzanne Wrack

4 Growing pains for Spurs

The 6-2 scoreline looked an unlikely one when Tottenham went into their dressing room at Stamford Bridge at half-time with the score level at 1-1. It had been an assertive first half from the visiting team against an increasingly impressive Chelsea. The Blues did put their foot on the gas in the second half but the Tottenham head coach, Martin Ho, said his team had to do better to not collapse after conceding. “We conceded three goals in nine minutes and then two in six. We can’t completely collapse in those moments. That’s individual responsibility and accountability to defend,” he said. Tottenham have not won in 20 games against top-four opponents. “You can see that, as a young team, we lack a little bit of maturity in these big games. That will come with time.” SW

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Martin Ho says Tottenham ‘can’t completely collapse’ after they concede. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images

5 Hemp edges closer to assist record

Lauren Hemp closed in on the WSL all-time assist record after setting up two goals in Sunday’s 3-2 win against Brighton. The 26-year-old recorded numbers 50 and 51 within the opening 16 minutes of the game by setting up Khadija Shaw twice. She now sits just three assists behind record holder and teammate Beth Mead, who has 54 in total. Hemp, who has eight goal contributions for the season, said: “I want to keep improving and I want my whole performance across the game to be good and I thought I lost the ball too many times today. So I want to keep pushing for more, keep striving and I still think my best is yet to come. But I’m happy with the contributions I’ve done in games recently.” Emillia Hawkins

6 Villa finally off the mark

Aston Villa finally got their first win of the season after a second-half comeback for a 2-1 victory against Liverpool. Villa had managed just three draws from their opening five games before the international break, but doubled their points tally thanks to a second-half strike from Chasity Grant and an own goal from the Reds defender Grace Fisk. It was a positive result for Brian Sørensen, who took over from Natalia Arroyo last month and was this week confirmed as the interim head coach until the end of the season. Sørensen said: “Incredible. Also the manner that we did it in, we were really struggling in that first half and Liverpool were so good, but we made changes tactically but also personnel at half-time and that flipped the game around. Credit to the girls … best day ever!” EH

7 Gago gives West Ham first away win

Kelly Gago’s second league goal of the season secured West Ham a 1-0 victory over Crystal Palace and their first away win of the campaign. The French international’s goal came from an assist from Oona Siren who capitalised on a defensive error, and Gago fired home a left-footed finish, proving the difference in the contest. Gago joined the Hammers from Everton at the start of the season and is beginning to make her mark in east London. Her contribution offers a boost for a West Ham side looking to build momentum and move away from the bottom end of the table following three consecutive losses prior to the international break. Réshma Rao

Sports.title: Semenyo’s eight-week injury absence leaves Manchester City short on cover for Haaland
Sports.content:
Antoine Semenyo has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury, leaving Enzo Maresca short of alternatives to Erling Haaland, who is a doubt for Manchester City’s Champions League game at home to AEK Athens on Tuesday.

Semenyo limped off against Ipswich on Saturday and Haaland hobbled off at full time with a foot injury. City are eager to get their European campaign back on track after losing to Paris Saint-Germain last Wednesday. Maresca has said he will make changes and has previously admitted Haaland will require resting at some point. Semenyo would have been the most obvious replacement but Phil Foden and Iliman Ndiaye could be utilised.

“To replace Erling it’s always difficult but we have some different options; we’ll see tomorrow,” Maresca said. “To lose Antoine or any player for us is not good. Then in terms of Erling, we said that we can use Antoine as a 9 but also we have different players that we are going to try and to find new solutions.”

Maresca witnessed a number of his players limp away from the win over Ipswich: Haaland, Semenyo, Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O’Reilly, who all featured at the World Cup. Maresca had made six changes, showing the need to rotate amid a hectic schedule of seven games in 21 days in October for City, many of whose players also had international commitments at the start of the month.

“We try to manage all the players in the best way, try to keep them fit,” Maresca said. “Even sometimes things happen that you cannot control, like Antoine’s injury. We try to save him, we try to keep him fresh.”
