Sports.title: Russell and Leclerc are the joint ‘sprint race champions’ of 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli can clinch the drivers’ championship at the next round – but three of his rivals out-scored him over the course of Formula 1’s six sprint races this year.

Singapore played host to F1’s sixth and final sprint race of 2026 last weekend. The sprint races were won by four different drivers: George Russell won three (Shanghai, Montreal and Zandvoort), while his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli triumphed at Silverstone, Lando Norris won in Miami and it was Max Verstappen’s turn in Singapore.

Russell could have beaten Verstappen last weekend, of course, having taken the lead off him at the start. But his crash at the end of lap one ended his chances of winning a fourth sprint race.

It also meant he ended the year with as many sprint race points as a driver who didn’t win any of these races. Charles Leclerc collected 34 points from sprint races, the same as Russell. This was made possible by the single-point gaps between finishing positions in sprint races, which are much closer than those used in grands prix.

After Russell’s retirement, Norris was on course to end the year as the top sprint race points-scorer. But his last-lap tangle with his team mate cost him three points and left him third.

As points are only awarded to the top eight finishers in sprint races, the drivers from the top four teams tended to monopolise them, with one exception: Isack Hadjar did not score a single point in a sprint race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Liam Lawson scored points for both Red Bull (while substituting for Hadjar at Zandvoort) and Racing Bulls in sprint races. His regular team mate Arvid Lindblad also took sprint race points, as did Alpine’s Pierre Gasly and Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg.

But for almost half the grid, the sprint races offered nothing. The addition of four more sprint races next year could further increase the gap between the leading teams and the midfield.

Sports.title: Singapore victory leaves Verstappen one win away from a full set – but not for long | 2026 Singapore Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen’s 73rd career victory was surely one of the most overdue of his career. At his 10th attempt, the Red Bull driver finally won the Singapore Grand Prix.

He’d come close several times before. Verstappen had started second four times and converted three of those into second-place finishes. On the other occasion he was wiped out by the Ferrari drivers as they sprinted to turn one.

But after finally claiming his first pole position at the Marina Bay circuit, Verstappen never let go of his advantage, leading every lap of the race. However with other drivers switching to the preferred soft tyres over the final stint, Verstappen did not set the fastest lap, so he did not collect his seventh ‘grand slam’.

He has now won at 27 different circuits, a feat only bettered by Lewis Hamilton on 31. Verstappen has won on every track on the calendar with a single exception: the Madring, which held its first grand prix this year.

However in order to complete a clean sweep of victories at every track on the calendar, Verstappen will have to win at three new rounds next year. Two venues where he has raced in F1, but not previously won at, will return on the 2027 F1 calendar.

What’s more, another driver will be in the same position as Verstappen. This is Hamilton, the last driver to have achieved a clean sweep:

Track Verstappen’s best result Hamilton’s best result Bahrain International Circuit 1st 1st Jeddah Corniche Circuit 1st 1st Albert Park 1st 1st Suzuka 1st 1st Shanghai International Circuit 1st 1st Miami International Autodrome 1st 6th Circuit Gilles Villeneuve 1st 1st Monaco 1st 1st Autodromo do Algarve 2nd 1st Silverstone 1st 1st Red Bull Ring 1st 1st Spa-Francorchamps 1st 1st Hungaroring 1st 1st Monza 1st 1st Madring 2nd DNF Baku City Circuit 1st 1st Istanbul Park 2nd 1st Singapore 1st 1st Circuit of the Americas 1st 1st Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez 1st 1st Interlagos 1st 1st Las Vegas Strip Circuit 1st 2nd Losail International Circuit 1st 1st Yas Marina 1st 1st

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hamilton last achieved a clean sweep when he won the French Grand Prix in 2018. He kept up the achievement over the next two seasons – even as the Covid-19 pandemic added new races to the schedule in 2020 – but his run ended when he failed to win at Zandvoort in 2021.

Achieving a clean sweep next year would arguably be a greater feat for either driver. There were 21 circuits on the calendar when Hamilton achieved it in 2018, but there are 24 on next year’s schedule.

Verstappen became the fifth driver to achieve 50 pole positions last weekend. He did so in his 250th race start and joins Ayrton Senna, who took 108 races to do the same, Hamilton (168), Michael Schumacher (177) and Sebastian Vettel (196).

This was the fourth year in a row the Singapore Grand Prix has been won from pole position. Verstappen led every lap on his way to victory, which is the fourth ‘lights-to-flag’ victory at the circuit in the last five years, along with Sergio Perez’s win in 2022 (from second on the grid), Carlos Sainz Jnr’s in 2023 and Lando Norris’s from 2024.

Red Bull was only one win behind Mercedes when the season began. However Mercedes has enjoyed such a strong season that Red Bull’s victories in the last two rounds means its is now 10 behind. However Red Bull did end Mercedes’ streak of leading at least one lap in every race this year.

Racing Bulls reached 100 points, which is more than they scored last year and their best score since 2021, when they competed as AlphaTauri.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

But Alpine’s season has decidedly hit the skids as they failed to score for the third round in a row. It was a particularly frustrating weekend for Pierre Gasly, who finished one place outside the points in both the sprint race and grand prix.

Williams left Singapore point-less, too. Carlos Sainz Jnr got his car into the top 10 early on in his 250th appearance in a grand prix weekend, but slipped to 14th at the flag.

Sports.title: On This Day: Stroll wins final race before becoming a Formula 1 driver | Brief
Sports.content:
10 years ago today Lance Stroll scored his most recent victory to date, in his final race before he became a Formula 1 driver.

Just two weeks shy of his 18th birthday, Stroll’s promotion to F1 with Williams the following year had already been announced. He had clinched the European Formula 3 championship earlier in the season and won both of the preceding two races in the season-ending triple-header at the Hockenheimring.

For his last race at Prema, Stroll lined up fourth on the grid behind Joel Eriksson, Jake Hughes and Callum Ilott. Stroll wasn’t the only future F1 driver on the grid: others included Nikita Mazepin (10th), Zhou Guanyu (13th) and George Russell (15th). Anthoine Hubert, who tragically died in a Formula 2 crash in 2019, lined up seventh.

Sports.title: Oscar Collazo Faces Mandatory Order After Flyweight Setback
Sports.content:
The WBO is not doing Oscar Collazo any favors. Just as the Puerto Rican minimumweight champion was preparing to walk away from 105 pounds, the sanctioning body stepped in to complicate matters, ordering him to defend his strap against interim titleholder Ryusei Matsumoto within a 15-day negotiating window.

The timing could hardly be worse for Collazo. He had already set his sights on bigger game, skipping right past light flyweight to challenge Ricardo Sandoval for two flyweight belts on October 10 in Chicago.

That two-division title run was ruined when a painful rib injury in training camp knocked him off the card. Instead of resting up and rescheduling his run at 112, Collazo now finds the WBO knocking on his door, insisting he settle business at the minimumweight limit.

WBO representative Gustavo Olivieri laid down the law on social media, making it clear that both camps have two weeks to hammer out terms or the fight goes straight to purse bids. The organization is leaning on its rule of keeping only one champion per division, which puts an end to Matsumoto’s interim status one way or another.

The order simply covers the paperwork, not a fight date. Nobody expects Collazo in the ring tomorrow, especially with bruised or broken ribs needing time to heal. The real issue is the weight. Making 105 pounds is brutal for any fighter growing into his prime, and Collazo had already mentally and physically started the transition to flyweight. Asking his body to drop back down for Matsumoto is a grueling chore that risks stalling his career.

Collazo holds the cards, but neither option is simple. Walking away from the belt leaves him empty-handed with nothing guaranteed at 112, while taking the Matsumoto fight delays his move up for several months.

Matsumoto’s team is in a great position, knowing they either get a shot at the real belt or pick it up by default. Collazo has to decide if keeping the hardware is worth the torture of making 105 one more time.

For Collazo, the risk-to-reward ratio is completely upside down. If he wins, what does he get? A small purse and the privilege of holding a belt that does not move the needle commercially. If he enters the ring drained from making weight and gets caught or looks sluggish against Matsumoto, his entire stock drops before he ever gets to cash in at flyweight.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Still Has Plenty Of Paydays Available
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley can still bag massive paydays below elite title level. Calls for him to hang up the gloves after getting stopped by Daniel Dubois completely miss that reality. Falling short against Dubois does not strip him of his ability to top domestic bills.

Derek Chisora wrote the playbook here. Chisora never had to conquer top-tier heavyweights to fill arenas or generate huge paychecks. British fans recognize him, know the entertainment they are paying for, and show up. Wardley can mirror that blueprint without wasting years fruitlessly chasing a rematch with Dubois.

Domestic dust-ups against Dave Allen, Johnny Fisher, or Chisora himself offer immediate box-office appeal. Efe Ajagba or Tony Yoka provide solid international flavor. None of those are walkovers, but none require beating a pound-for-pound monster to pack out a venue.

The draw remains unchanged. Fans know Wardley hits like a truck, and they know he can get hurt in return. Put Wardley in the ring with Fisher, and nobody cares if a world belt is on the line; they are tuning in because someone is going to sleep.

That leaves Queensberry holding plenty of cards. A routine bounce-back victory followed by a massive domestic main event puts him right back in the money without pretending he solved the Dubois riddle.

Down the line, reaching the end of his Queensberry deal might even open up a fresh bidding war. Zuffa could easily see value in an action-heavy British brawler. While nothing is on the table right now, it highlights how many avenues exist beyond this single loss.

Wardley’s physical condition must always come first. From a purely business perspective, the path is clear. Chisora proved you can remain a massive ticket seller without beating the division’s champions.

Wardley does not need another belt around his waist to get paid. Pick the right matchups, and he can laugh all the way to the bank for years to come.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Seeks Stamina Help From Team Usyk
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez is working alongside Oleksandr Usyk’s conditioning team ahead of his October 31 bout against Christian Mbilli in Riyadh. The meeting will thoroughly test his gas tank across twelve rounds.

Base camp is Gandia, Spain, where Canelo brought in outside fitness specialists while Eddy Reynoso directs the boxing work. Against Mbilli, the payoff must show when fatigue sets in, especially since the younger contender never stops pressing forward.

“In strength and conditioning, I am learning new things,” Canelo told The Ring. “I appreciate them because they put all of their energy into me and are doing everything based on what [my head coach] Eddy Reynoso needs for boxing.”

Mbilli’s relentless tempo explains the sudden shift in preparation. Canelo punishes opponents who march directly into his range, yet he needs steady volume to win rounds. Landing occasional sharp counters leaves far too much clock open for an aggressive challenger throwing nonstop leather.

The main question is whether Canelo can sustain his offense once the fight pushes past the midway mark. Now 36, Canelo returns following his defeat against Terence Crawford and subsequent surgery on his left elbow, with over a year of inactivity behind him. He expects peak execution from a heavily taxed body.

A fresh training philosophy provides something new, yet genuine output down the stretch remains unproven. Cardiovascular endurance does not magically appear in the twilight of a twenty-year career. You cannot rebuild an engine with that much mileage, especially after serious elbow surgery and more than a year out of the ring.

Usyk’s training methods work for Usyk because he has spent a lifetime developing an engine built for movement, bounce, and non-stop output. Transplanting those drills onto a flat-footed counterpuncher who relies on heavy torso rotations and planted feet makes zero sense mechanically.

Mbilli is a nightmare style for an aging fighter who needs scheduled rest breaks. He throws upwards of 80 punches a round, does not care about taking shots to give three back, and smothers distance

The mental comfort of working with Usyk’s crew might give him a temporary psychological lift in camp, but once round seven arrives, and Mbilli is still in his chest, those new drills will not buy him the oxygen his legs and lungs can no longer produce.

Training in Spain softens the time shift into Saudi Arabia. Canelo described feeling “really weird” during his early morning bout with William Scull and stated he has requested that Turki Alalshikh schedule a ring walk no later than midnight or 1 a.m.

Better timing can sharpen his entrance. Once the bell rings, though, Mbilli brings intense pressure that travel logistics cannot solve. Canelo needs the work with Usyk’s camp to translate into steady output when fatigue threatens to stall him.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Drops Canelo Chase Three Years Late
Sports.content:
David Benavidez has finally conceded that a fight with Canelo Alvarez will never happen, admitting that reality years after his climb up the divisions settled the question.

Benavidez currently fights at cruiserweight, two full divisions above super middleweight, while openly discussing a future heavyweight jump against Oleksandr Usyk. He has not made 168 pounds since 2023. Any realistic window to face Canelo closed several weight classes ago.

“I think honestly I could say with confidence that that fight is never going to happen,” Benavidez told Brian Custer.

When Brian asked if he had permanently moved on, Benavidez praised Canelo, yet still claimed the Mexican star simply refused to face him.

“I don’t want to keep disrespecting somebody … not even disrespecting, but just calling somebody out that doesn’t want to fight,” he said.

That rationale ignores the massive physical gap separating them today. Critics can reasonably argue Canelo should have met Benavidez when both shared the 168-pound division. That complaint loses all weight with Benavidez now preparing for Michal Cieslak at 200 pounds.

His prospective roadmap includes Jai Opetaia, Artur Beterbiev, and eventual heavyweight tests. None of those plans lead anywhere near Canelo.

A logical alternative after Canelo fell to Terence Crawford would have been targeting Crawford directly. Crawford had talked of entering boxing’s Mount Rushmore. The public intrigue around him was at an all-time peak, and Turki Alalshikh held the purse strings to fund virtually any blockbuster Crawford wanted next.

If Benavidez truly wanted to settle the score on the belts Canelo kept out of reach, Crawford was the obvious lever to pull. Instead of shifting his crosshairs to the newly crowned undisputed champion, Benavidez let the moment disappear.

“He’s a great fighter. He’s a legend,” Benavidez said. “I would like to be a great Mexican legend like him one day.”

Calling yourself a future Mexican legend sounds nice in an interview, but looking at the actual resume tells a different story. Canelo earned that status by taking on the toughest challenges available from junior middleweight all the way to light heavyweight, facing elite operators like Floyd Mayweather Jr., Gennadiy Golovkin, Miguel Cotto, and Dmitry Bivol.

Benavidez is nowhere near that neighborhood. Instead of securing defining legacy bouts, he is lining up voluntary defenses against Michal Cieslak at 200 pounds. While Cieslak is a capable European contender, nobody outside of hard-core circles is paying to see that fight. It does nothing to elevate Benavidez to the pantheon of Mexican greats.

If Benavidez genuinely wanted to close the gap on Canelo, he needed to make real waves. Taking out Gilberto Ramirez was a solid win, but sitting on belts and scheduling low-demand opponents like Cieslak keeps him in neutral. Fighting fringe contenders at cruiserweight only proves that while he talks about chasing history, his matchmaking still trails far behind the standard Canelo set.

Sports.title: Frank Martin Wants Shakur Stevenson Or Tank Rematch
Sports.content:
Frank Martin is calling for bouts with Shakur Stevenson, Gervonta Davis, or Isaac Pitbull Cruz. Still, his recent ring activity shows he has serious ground to cover before getting those marquee fights.

The 31-year-old light welterweight contender welcomed every major challenge, targeting Davis in particular.

“Man, I love that rematch,” Martin said to Fight Hub TV. He also acknowledged that facing Cruz or Lamont Roach could build momentum toward a second Davis meeting.

Martin pointed to weight issues during his initial loss to Davis without detailing what went wrong. Vague explanations will not convince the public to buy a sequel. He must deliver clear proof inside the ropes that a second meeting would end differently.

The inactivity is killing whatever marketability he had left from the Tank pay-per-view. Since the lucrative 2024 bout with Davis, Martin has made only two ring appearances. His sole win since 2023 was a decision over veteran Rances Barthelemy, followed by a ten-round draw against Nahir Albright earlier this year.

Albright was supposed to be a routine showcase to get him winning, and instead, Martin escaped with a gift draw in a fight that many observers thought he dropped. When you look shaky against Albright, you have zero leverage to demand dates with elite champions.

Martin steps into the ring against Tarik Zaina on October 24 for a rebuilding fight. Winning is essential, yet vanishing into inactivity afterward would erase any progress.

“We ain’t chasing nobody,” Martin stated. “I just want to put on a dominant performance,” noting he is ready for whatever comes next.

Waiting for top fighters to call him rarely works. Neither Stevenson nor Davis has an incentive to pick him when Martin carries minimal buzz. Cruz offers the most practical path forward. The aggressive style Cruz brings could create an explosive contest, giving Martin a platform to secure a defining victory.

Joining Zuffa could also solve his scheduling problems if the promotion delivers active fight dates. Constant ring time will do far more for his career than calling out superstars he cannot book.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Reveals Three Fight Roadmap: Opetaia, Beterbiev, And Usyk
Sports.content:
David Benavidez is mapping out an ambitious three-fight wishlist once he handles Michal Cieslak on December 5. Benavidez laid out three massive targets: Jai Opetaia, Artur Beterbiev, plus Oleksandr Usyk.

That roadmap keeps him focused on cruiserweight, along with an eventual leap to heavyweight for Usyk. It also leaves Dmitry Bivol completely on the sidelines for the foreseeable future.

“We’re talking about Opetaia. We’re talking about Beterbiev. And then we’re maybe talking about Usyk,” Benavidez said to Brian Custer’s channel.

Opetaia sits at the top of the queue. If Benavidez gets past Cieslak, he wants the Australian champion on Cinco de Mayo weekend in May 2027.

“The fight that I got to honor first is the fight with Opetaia because I told him I’d fight him Cinco de Mayo next year,” he explained.

Beterbiev comes next in the plan, specifically at cruiserweight. Benavidez figures the Russian puncher would benefit from skipping the brutal drain down to 175 pounds. That choice sets up a fresher, more dangerous rival to conquer.

“I think it’s a better fight for both of us at cruiserweight,” Benavidez said. “It’d be a bigger challenge for me.”

Trading shots in the pocket against Beterbiev without weight drain presents a massive test. If Benavidez stays inside to let his punches fly, he must survive lethal return fire right back.

A meeting with Usyk remains the most ambitious idea on the board. Benavidez mentioned taking that bout at cruiserweight or heavyweight, saying he would take the chance immediately.

Keep in mind, these names represent Benavidez’s personal target list rather than finalized contracts. He plans on staying with PBC while working across promotional boundaries to secure them.

A bout with Bivol could happen down the line, but it will not happen anytime soon.

“In the next three fights, probably not,” Benavidez said regarding Bivol.

Gold fever completely clouds judgment, and Benavidez sounds like an old prospector who spotted a glitter in the stream and started spending millions in his head before he even picked up a shovel.

Counting Opetaia as an automatic win to reach massive paydays against an aging Artur Beterbiev and Oleksandr Usyk shows how disconnected Benavidez has become from reality. If Opetaia clips him, that entire fantasy sequence turns to smoke. The Usyk dream evaporates, the cruiserweight belts vanish, and the massive Saudi checks dry up overnight.

Benavidez is so fixated on cashing in on three giant events that he forgets the brutal toll the very first hurdle demands.

Sports.title: Robert Garcia Questions Unequal Protection On Canelo Alvarez Card
Sports.content:
Robert Garcia wants assurances about his camp’s safety before Lindolfo Delgado’s October 31 vacant IBF light welterweight title fight in Riyadh. He expects Canelo Alvarez to receive royal treatment ahead of his fight with Christian Mbilli, but fears his own team will be left traveling without the same protection.

The veteran trainer sounded uneasy rather than defiant when speaking on his team’s travel logistics. His issue is not whether the bout takes place, but the wide gulf between how the headliner travels and how the undercard talent gets moved into Saudi Arabia.

Canelo operates in an entirely different financial stratosphere. Garcia expects him to arrive by private plane with security handling his trip to the arena. His fear is that Delgado and his corner will have to fly commercial and pass through a public airport without comparable protection.

“They’ll f***ing fly private. They’ll go into a private airport where nobody knows where they’re at. They’ll have security driving them to the arena,” Garcia told Elie Seckbach.

Garcia wants similar protection for his group, but his tone sounded more resigned than demanding. He knows how big-money boxing operates. Promoters spare no expense for the box-office anchor, while supporting fighters are left to fend for themselves on standard itineraries.

“Canelo’s fight might happen because, like I told you, he’s secured. Not us. We’re not secured,” Garcia admitted.

The idea of Delgado’s camp joining Canelo on a private charter is wishful thinking, and Garcia practically acknowledged it in the same breath.

“If they tell us, ‘You guys are all traveling together,’ then we’re fine, but I don’t think that’s the case.”

Garcia doesn’t sound hopeful. Delgado is fighting Artur Biyarslanov for the vacant IBF light welterweight title, but that doesn’t buy him Canelo’s treatment. Canelo headlines the event. Delgado fills a spot underneath him, even with a world championship at stake.

Robert can vent to reporters, but walking away could cost his fighter the opportunity he’s been working toward. If Garcia refuses to travel without better security, organizers could look for a replacement. Delgado would then be watching somebody else fight for the belt.

That’s what makes Garcia’s position so uncomfortable. He has every reason to ask how his team will be protected, yet Delgado could be the one paying for it if they refuse to go. A world title shot is a powerful incentive to board the plane, even when your trainer has serious doubts about the trip.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley’s Defeats Overshadow His Finest Boxing Year
Sports.content:
A back-and-forth heavyweight fight captures the public’s collective imagination like few other sporting events. Countless expressions originating or popularized in heavyweight boxing describe competitive sporting events. “A knockdown drag-out contest”, “teams throwing haymakers”, “a slugfest”, “a heavyweight fight”, and many other such phrases regularly feature on football, baseball and basketball broadcasts.

The first fight between Daniel Dubois (24-3, 23 KO) and Fabio Wardley (20-2-1, 19 KO) in May illustrated the fantasy of what many envision in a heavyweight clash. Knockdowns, temerity, mettle, blood, violence. In the end, Daniel Dubois prevailed via technical knockout in the eleventh round. Fabio Wardley lost his championship, but gained the respect of anyone watching. It instantly entered the “fight of the year” conversation and was hailed as a heavyweight classic.

…

This past Saturday, just over five months later, Dubois and Wardley met again. The rematch was anticlimactic by comparison. The fight featured an early knockdown like the first encounter, though this time Daniel Dubois delivered it. Though Wardley tried to resist Dubois’ onslaught, it proved to be futile. Dubois nearly ended the bout inside the first round. But Wardley survived long enough to hear the bell to conclude round one. Ultimately, Wardley’s doggedness just lengthened his suffering.

Sixty seconds later, as round two began, Dubois was patient, waiting to find openings to pound away at Wardley. Dubois did it in short order. In the final minute of round two, Dubois peppered a winded and wounded Wardley with clean, powerful punches. The fight got stopped 2:21 into the second round; it was undoubtedly a fair stoppage. Referee Steve Gray stopped the contest just as Wardley’s trainer Ben Davidson threw in the towel from the corner.

Dubois obliterated Fabio Wardley and extinguished any doubt from fans and media, at least for now.

…

Fabio Wardley was a latecomer to boxing, turning professional at 22 years old with no amateur fights on his resume. Both his age and lack of amateur experience are considered rarities. Four fights into his pro career, Wardley agreed to be managed by Dillian Whyte, a fellow British heavyweight and former sparring partner. Wardley was born in Ipswich, England, and naturally is a lifelong supporter of Ipswich Town Football Club. He attained a dream by fighting at Ipswich Town’s stadium, Portman Road, in June 2025. His knockout win there over Justis Huni helped propel Wardley to recognition as 2025’s British Boxer of the Year, according to multiple outlets. An upset victory over former world champion Joseph Parker earned Wardley the WBO’s interim heavyweight championship. Wardley’s banner year of 2025 set him up to challenge Daniel Dubois in May for the vacant WBO heavyweight title.

…

On Saturday, Fabio Wardley was walloped. This year, Wardley has zero wins and two losses, both by technical knockout. But boxing fans will always remember the slugfest Wardley and Dubois had in May. While 2025 was Wardley’s most successful year in boxing, he will inevitably be associated with Daniel Dubois and their classic fight five months ago. In a career in which he has beaten former world champions and scored devastating knockouts, boxing fans will most fondly remember Fabio Wardley for a fight he lost.

It might not be fair, but it is reality. In a way, it is endearing, though. Even if Fabio Wardley never competes for a heavyweight championship again, the Ipswichian has forever earned a place in heavyweight boxing lore for his performance on May 9, 2026.

…

Sports and society at large are infatuated with analytics and data. Decades from now, when a young boxing fan asks their personalized robot about Fabio Wardley, they will be unimpressed by consecutive knockout losses. But if that young fan finds an old head and mentions Fabio Wardley, they will hear about his toughness, how he could have won a title in a different era, who Wardley reminds them of, and whatever else. Wardley and Dubois have earned remembrance in highlight reels and recollections, the greatest accolade of all.

Ghana News.title: Godfred Dame welcomes stay of Hanan’s trial, cites unfair charge sheet
Ghana News.content:
Lawyer for former National Food and Buffer Stock Company (NAFCO) Chief Executive Officer Hanan Abdul-Wahab Aludiba, Godfred Yeboah Dame, has welcomed the Court of Appeal’s decision to halt the trial, insisting the charge sheet lacks sufficient detail on the allegations against his client.

The Court of Appeal on Monday, October 19, 2026, suspended proceedings at the High Court pending the determination of Hanan’s appeal challenging alleged defects in the charge sheet.

Speaking to the media after the ruling, Mr Dame said the trial had been unfair to his client because the charges allegedly lumped together sums said to have been stolen without specifying the individual acts and transactions involved.

“We thank God for this,” he said, welcoming the court’s decision to suspend the proceedings.

"I am not surprised that today the Court of Appeal has halted it because the charges really have been unfair to the accused person. The trial so far has been very unfair to the accused person in the sense that it is more or less like having your hands tied to your back, your eyes blind folded and being asked to fight in a boxing ring,” he said.

He argued that the prosecution had failed to provide sufficient particulars explaining which specific acts and payments formed the basis of the allegations and how the alleged offences occurred.

“That cannot be a fair trial. That is not the kind of criminal justice system our Republic is supposed to have,” he added.

He added that the Constitution envisages a fair criminal justice system in which an accused person is given sufficient details of the acts for which they are standing trial.

The Court of Appeal granted the stay after finding that the issues raised by the defence constituted exceptional circumstances warranting the suspension of the trial.

The decision does not determine the merits of the charges against Hanan and his wife, Faiza Seidu Wuni, but pauses the High Court proceedings until the appeal is determined.

Ghana News.title: GPL Week 7: Hearts of Oak’s Kelvin Osei Asibey, 8 others win NASCO MoM awards
Ghana News.content:
Hearts of Oak defender Kelvin Osei Asibey was adjudged NASCO Man of the Match following his solid display as the Phobians defeated Vision FC 1-0 at the Nii Adjei Kraku Complex on Saturday. Substitute Kwesi Asmah scored the winner in the 86th minute after pouncing on a poor clearance.

At the Kpando Stadium, Berekum Chelsea defender Fuseini Zachariah won the Man of the Match award as his side stunned Heart of Lions FC 2-0 for their first away win of the season. Dramani Awuah opened the scoring in the 39th minute before Paul Attah Agyei doubled the lead in the 69th minute.

At the Swedru Sports Stadium, Eric Wiafe Darkwah was named Man of the Match as Swedru All Blacks FC beat Karela United FC 2-0. Darkwah converted a 9th-minute Panenka penalty and then provided the assist for Faisal Charwetey who doubled the lead in the 59th minute.

At the AAK II Park, Lawrence Gadeseh claimed the Man of the Match accolade as Basake Holy Stars FC edged Bechem United FC 1-0 to maintain their perfect home record. Bismark Teye Tetteh scored the only goal of the game in the second half.

At the Debibi Presby Park, Richard Owusu was adjudged Man of the Match as Debibi United FC defeated Goldstars SC 1-0. Maxwell Agyemang struck just before half-time to secure all three points for the newly-promoted side.

At the Nana Agyeman Badu I Park, Abubakar Adams was the Man of the Match as Aduana FC returned to winning ways with a 1-0 win over FC AshantiGold 04. Adams reacted quickest to fire home a rebound in the 40th minute after Seidu Saana's free-kick was parried.

At the Baba Yara Stadium, Hubert Gyau won the award as Asante Kotoko SC beat Young Apostles FC 2-1. Gyau broke the deadlock in the 70th minute before Solomon Nsor Asaah doubled the lead in the 82nd minute, while Huziaf Iddrisu pulled one back for the visitors with a late direct free-kick.

At the Nsenkyire Arena, Akwasi Sarpong was named Man of the Match as FC Samartex 1996 beat defending champions Medeama SC 2-1. Joshuah Fuseini gave Samartex the lead in the 54th minute, Dominic Amponsah equalised for Medeama in the 79th minute, before Christian Agyenim snatched the winner three minutes into injury time.

At the Daasebre Boamah Darko II Park, Samuel Aryee Baabu was adjudged Man of the Match as Port City FC were held 1-1 by Dreams FC. Baabu thundered home the opener from the edge of the box two minutes after the restart, but Kelvin Ahiable struck in stoppage time to rescue a point for Dreams.

Each NASCO Man of the Match winner will take home a 32-inch NASCO television set courtesy of sponsors Electroland Ghana Limited.

Ghana News.title: Zelenskiy says Ukraine got no warning as Russia launches major attack
Ghana News.content:
Ukraine received no advance warning from its ‌partners of a Russian ballistic missile strike overnight, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said, after Moscow launched one of its broadest air assaults in months, cutting power to more than half a million households.

Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and the surrounding region and more than 200 drones ​across the country in attacks stretching from Kharkiv and Dnipro in the east to Odesa in the south ​and Volyn and Rivne in the west. More than 10 energy facilities were damaged, Zelenskiy ⁠said.

The strikes killed a woman in Kyiv and two more people in the industrial city of Kryvyi Rih, officials said.

Zelenskiy's ​complaint about intelligence sharing comes amid growing friction between Zelenskiy and President Donald Trump's administration over US support for Ukraine and ​Washington's approach to Russia.

"Another Russian ballistic missile attack came in several waves overnight, and once again, there was no early warning from our partners," Zelenskiy said on the Telegram app.

"When deliveries of missiles for Ukraine's air defence are blocked while Russia is granted relief or delays ​in sanctions, this is, unfortunately, a denial of reality on the part of our partners."

Throughout the nearly five-year war, Ukraine ​has relied on US intelligence to detect Russian ballistic missile launches and provide early warning of incoming strikes.

Yurii Ihnat, a spokesman for the ‌Ukrainian air ⁠force, said Kyiv received no warning ahead of the first ballistic missile strike overnight but did receive information ahead of a second attack.

"For some reason, no information was received the first time, a matter our experts are investigating together with our partners, as this is not the first time such a situation has occurred," Ihnat told Ukrainian television.

Secretary of State Marco ​Rubio denied that the United States ​had paused some intelligence sharing ⁠with Ukraine, contradicting Zelenskiy, who has said the United States briefly curtailed such cooperation.

ROLLING BLACKOUTS

Ukrainian air defences downed 247 targets - four cruise missiles and 243 drones, the air force said.

Russia's ​Defence Ministry said its forces carried out a "massive strike" using precision weapons and attack drones ​against Ukrainian defence ⁠industry facilities, drone and cruise missile storage sites, and a data centre.

Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said the energy sector was the main target of the attacks, with damage reported across the country. Ukraine's energy ministry said rolling blackouts were introduced for households ⁠and businesses ​as crews worked to restore supplies.

Railway stations, pharmaceutical warehouses, commercial properties and ​residential buildings were also damaged, Koretskyi said.

In Kyiv a subway station on the left bank of the capital was hit, and a 25-storey residential building ​was damaged, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Telegram.

Ghana News.title: Ghana Stammering Association calls for inclusion and an end to stigma
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Stammering Association (GSA) has called for greater understanding and inclusion of people who stammer, urging Ghanaians to create spaces where everyone can communicate without fear of ridicule or discrimination.

In a statement marking International Stammering Awareness Day 2026, the association said the varied experiences of people who stammer must be recognised rather than reduced to a single narrative.

The association is joining the global stammering community in awareness activities throughout October under the theme, “Shades of Stuttering — What’s Yours?”

According to GSA, the theme highlights that stammering does not look or sound the same for everyone, and that some experiences may be less visible than others.

“Some people may openly repeat sounds, words or phrases, stretch sounds, or get stuck when speaking — this is often described as overt stammering,” the statement explained.

Others, it noted, may conceal their stammering by substituting words, avoiding particular situations, pretending not to know an answer or choosing to remain silent. These experiences are often described as covert stammering.

The association said people also adopt different approaches to navigating their speech. While some use speech techniques, others focus on accepting their stammering, with many experiencing a combination of approaches.

“These are all different shades of stammering, and every experience is valid,” GSA stated.

The association said the observance offered an opportunity to acknowledge both the difficulties people who stammer face and the positive experiences that can emerge from their lives.

It identified stigma, bullying, discrimination, communication barriers and pressure to speak fluently as challenges that people who stammer may encounter.

At the same time, GSA noted that many develop greater self-awareness, resilience, empathy and advocacy skills, while building meaningful connections with others through their experiences.

The association encouraged people who stammer to share their stories to deepen public understanding and demonstrate that there is no single way to stammer or to experience life as someone who stammers.

“We encourage people who stammer to share their experiences and help others understand that there is no single way to stammer and no single way to experience life as a person who stammers,” it said.

GSA also appealed to parents, teachers, employers, speech and language therapists, researchers, policymakers and the wider public to listen to people who stammer and consider how to make their environments more inclusive.

The call places emphasis on enabling people to participate and express themselves without facing judgement about how they speak.

As part of the observance, the association invited reflection on individual experiences, the lessons people have learnt and the collective action needed to improve inclusion.

“What is your shade of stammering? What have you experienced? What have you learned? And what can we do together to create a more inclusive world for people who stammer?” the statement asked.

Ghana News.title: Akosua Manu calls on Vice President to intervene in Obuasi SHTS abuse case
Ghana News.content:
The Advisor on Gender and Social Protection to Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, Akosua Manu, has called on Vice President Prof. Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang to use her office and influence to ensure justice for students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) following allegations of sexual abuse.

She said the Vice President’s position as a woman in a historic leadership role carried significant meaning for Ghanaian girls; hence, it must produce tangible improvements in their safety and welfare.

In an op-ed titled “A Party Card Is Not a Certificate of Immunity,” published on her social media platforms on Monday, October 19, 2026, Akosua Manu challenged the Vice President to translate her advocacy for girls into practical measures that protect them from abuse.

“Your voice and influence must help secure an impartial response, even where it requires uncomfortable questions within your own political circles,” she said.

She noted that the allegations at Obuasi SHTS raised broader concerns about the handling of sexual misconduct complaints in schools, particularly reports that earlier complaints had been made but apparently remained unresolved.

“According to investigative reporting, students raised complaints, teachers expressed concerns, and petitions reached the relevant authorities. Each was an opportunity to establish the facts and protect the girls. Yet the complaints apparently remained unresolved,” she noted

She said the circumstances demanded answers about what authorities knew, when they became aware of the complaints and what steps they took to protect the students.

She urged the Vice President to ensure that the allegations were investigated without political interference, emphasising that political affiliation should neither determine how complaints are treated nor shield anyone from accountability.

The gender advocate also called on the Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, to provide clear answers on the support being offered to the alleged victims and their families.

She asked the Ministry to outline measures to prevent intimidation, protect the students’ privacy and education, and guarantee their access to justice.

“Representation must translate into protection,” she stressed, arguing that the responsibility to safeguard children rested with the entire government, particularly institutions mandated to protect vulnerable people.

Beyond the immediate case, Akosua Manu called for an independent review of how allegations of sexual misconduct were handled across schools, insisting that students needed confidential reporting channels outside the authority of the persons they accused.

Akosua Manu commended investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni and other journalists who brought the allegations to national attention, but warned that investigative journalism should not become a substitute for effective child-protection institutions.

She concluded by advocating for the protection of victims against retaliation, prompt referral of suspected criminal offences to the appropriate investigative authorities and professional support for affected students.

Ghana News.title: World Bank President warns 1.2bn young people will compete for 400m jobs in next 15 years
Ghana News.content:
Over the next 10 to 15 years, 1.2 billion young people will arrive at a job market projected to offer only about 400 million jobs, the World Bank President, Ajay Banga, has warned.

Making remarks at the 2026 World Bank/International Monetary Fund Annual Meetings Plenary in Bangkok, Thailand, he said this generation will shape the next century. Therefore, “the choices we make today will help determine how”.

“Those are the twin challenges we have been working to address: Making scarce resources go further… while helping countries create jobs at scale. They must be addressed together”, he mentioned.

Over the past three years, he said the World Bank has used these Annual Meetings to lay out the work it is undertaking, changes it is making, and the ambition behind them.

“This year, I want to focus on our progress—and where it is taking us. The future of development will depend on bringing public finance, private investment, philanthropy, and technology together around what each country needs”, he added.

World Bank on Reforms

Furthermore, Ajay Banga said the World Bank has begun reforms, cutting project preparation from 19 months to nine. “Replaced 153 scorecard measures with 22 focused on impact. Increased pay-for-results financing from about one-third to half. Brought our public and private sector teams together around country-led strategies. And reengineered our balance sheet—creating more than $100 billion in additional IBRD lending capacity over a decade”.

The World Bank Boss said the number of projects on its digital co-financing platform has tripled in two years to about 250 projects, seeking $138 billion in financing.

“We are cutting duplication by relying on each other’s work with the Asian Development Bank, Inter-American Development Bank and EBRD—and expanding that model”.

“Taken together, these changes give us greater capacity. Our jobs strategy gives it direction”, he explained.

He pointed out that the Jobs Council drew on experience across countries and sectors to identify policies and programmes that create more and better jobs. The strategy that emerged rests on three pillars.

First, he mentioned physical and human infrastructure.

According to him, employers need electricity, water, transport, and digital connections, while people need health, education, and skills. Last year, the World Bank committed $40 billion—nearly one-third of its financing—to these foundations.

Second, regulatory and policy certainty.

Third, scale, he added.

“That is how we bring more private capital into development”, he explained.

In 2022, the year before its work plan began, the World Bank mobilised roughly $35 billion in private capital.

Last year, it raised $112 billion, a threefold increase.

Alongside its own financing, total financing exceeded $230 billion.

Ghana News.title: Obuasi Agrifair promotes agribusiness, food security and youth employment
Ghana News.content:
Stakeholders in the agriculture sector in Obuasi and two local municipal assemblies are forging ahead to transform the town from its known status as a gold mining community to a rich agricultural hub to feed the country.

In collaboration with AngloGold Ashanti’s Obuasi Mine, the maiden Agrifair is organised to promote agribusiness, create employment opportunities for young people and strengthen agricultural production in the Adansi area and beyond.

The maiden fair assembled agricultural producers, processors, buyers, financial institutions, government agencies and other stakeholders to explore partnerships to expand farming businesses and improve productivity.

The initiative forms part of activities to commemorate the 2026 World Food Day and reflects the AGA’s 10-year socioeconomic development plan (SEDP), prioritizing sustainable livelihoods, agriculture, enterprise development, skills development and local economic growth.

The initiative aimed at creating market opportunities for locally produced agricultural goods while promoting agriculture, agro-processing and local enterprise development.

Managing Director of AngloGold Ashanti’s Obuasi Mine, Samuel Pobi, noted that the fair was crucial to strengthening agriculture, promoting local enterprise and creating sustainable economic opportunities.

“Our support for agriculture is not new. Through our community development and livelihood interventions, we continue to support initiatives that strengthen agricultural productivity, improve processing capacity and create opportunities for income generation,” he said.

The event is expected to provide a platform for farmers and other stakeholders to explore business opportunities, share ideas and identify ways to make agriculture more productive and attractive to young people.

Mr. Pobi added that creating opportunities within the agricultural sector could contribute to improved livelihoods and encourage more people, particularly the youth, to consider farming and related businesses as viable sources of income.

The program also saw the handover of some agricultural inputs and modern processing equipment to selected farmers and processing groups.

Obuasi MCE, Faustilove Appiah Kennin, shared that the town cannot rely on its mineral resources alone for sustainable growth but must also turn to other ventures to promote economic growth.

“Obuasi is recognized for its rich mineral resources as the contributory of mining to local and national economy, however, you’d realize that sustainable and economic development requires us to diversify our economic activities and create additional source of employment,” she said.

Deputy Minister for Food and Agriculture, John Dumelo, reaffirmed the government’s commitment to supporting farmers with agricultural equipment and inputs to improve productivity and increase food production.

He stressed that farmers needed access to the necessary resources to expand their operations and contribute more effectively to the growth of Ghana’s agricultural sector.

The fair was held on the theme: “Building Sustainable Agriculture for Food Security and Economic Growth in Obuasi”.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod must be commended for successes chalked up – Mahama
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama has commended the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) for its contribution to the growth of gold exports, increased foreign exchange earnings and efforts to promote responsible small-scale mining.

Speaking at the Mining in Motion Conference, the President highlighted an increase in gold exports from the artisanal and small-scale mining sector, alongside measures to reclaim lands destroyed by illegal mining and improve monitoring of mining equipment.

“I wish to commend the Gold Board for the successes that it has chalked,” he said.

President Mahama said Ghana exported 64 tonnes of gold from the artisanal and small-scale mining sector in 2024. In 2025, the country exported 104 tonnes from the sector between April and December, following the establishment of GoldBod in April.

He said the regulation of small-scale gold exports had also contributed to a significant increase in foreign exchange earnings.

“And I'm happy to note that the Gold Board in 2025 alone, with the regulation of export of small-scale gold, brought into this country $10.8 billion, which is an almost 100% increase over the $4.66 billion that came into the country in 2024,” he said.

The President's remarks come as the government seeks to strengthen the regulation of gold trading, increase the economic benefits of the mining sector and address the environmental damage associated with illegal mining.

President Mahama said the government had made progress in removing illegal miners from nine designated high-risk areas, with work now underway to prepare the affected forest reserves for reclamation.

“I'm happy to note that of those nine red zones, we have cleared all of them of illegal miners and are currently preparing those forest reserves for reclamation,” he said.

He said that illegal mining had destroyed approximately 12,000 acres of land across Ghana, making the restoration of affected areas a key priority.

The President commended mining company Newmont for its reclamation work, saying it had restored almost 800 acres of mined-out land and planted useful crops.

He also praised GoldBod for awarding the Ghana Armed Forces a contract to reclaim 253 acres of land damaged by mining activities in the Tano-Nimiri Forest.

“The Gold Board has awarded the Ghana Armed Forces a contract to reclaim 253 acres of land destroyed in the famous Tano-Nimiri Forest. That work is ongoing,” he said.

President Mahama further commended the Ministers of Lands and Natural Resources and Finance for allocating GH¢200 million towards the reclamation of 5,000 acres of degraded land, with the work expected to begin in 2027.

The planned restoration forms part of broader efforts to repair environmental damage caused by illegal mining and protect forest reserves from further degradation.

The President also outlined measures to strengthen monitoring of excavators and improve oversight of mining activities across the country.

He said 6,060 excavators had been registered and detained at the ports, while 2,059 had been fitted with tracking devices to help authorities monitor their locations and use.

The tracking system is intended to help the authorities identify where the equipment is being deployed and strengthen efforts to prevent its use in illegal mining operations.

President Mahama also said 11 cooperatives had been trained in new mining methods and were now operational.

He added that GoldBod was financing small-scale artisanal mining operations to adopt technologies designed to reduce environmental destruction.

The initiative is intended to support miners in adopting improved methods while reducing the damage associated with mining activities.

President Mahama said the government was also allocating funds to strengthen efforts to tackle illegal mining and protect the country's water bodies.

He announced that GH¢200 million had been allocated in the 2027 Budget to support the activities of the National Inter-Ministerial Coordinating Committee on Illegal Mining (NIMOS) and the Blue Water Guards.

The funding is expected to support enforcement measures aimed at curbing illegal mining and protecting water resources from pollution and degradation.

The President also announced plans for a major reafforestation initiative involving the Ministry of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation and the REDD+ programme.

The initiative is expected to cover various parts of the country, including the savannah regions, as part of efforts to restore degraded landscapes and increase tree cover.

Beyond GoldBod's activities and the fight against illegal mining, President Mahama highlighted the government's local content policy, which seeks to increase the participation of indigenous Ghanaian companies in the mining industry.

He said the policy would encourage a transition from owner mining to contract mining by indigenous companies, creating more opportunities for local businesses to provide services to mining operations.

“We have also introduced a local content policy that transitions our mining companies from owner mining to contract mining by indigenous companies, so that we can have more indigenous participation in our mining industries,” he said.

The policy is intended to expand the role of Ghanaian-owned businesses in the mining value chain and increase local participation in the industry.

However, the President assured workers employed by existing gold mining companies that the transition would not affect their salaries or conditions of service.

“I want to reassure the workers who currently work for operating gold mines that the transfer to contract mining will not affect their remuneration or their conditions of service,” he said.

“They will be paid the same way as they were paid under their current administrations,” he added.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
