On the persistent brain drain in the health sector, the NMA president said doctors should not be expected to remain in Nigeria solely out of patriotism.

“Patriotism should be supported by decent working conditions, professional dignity, security, competitive remuneration, opportunities for career development and a health system in which doctors can see a future for themselves and their families,” he said.

He warned against a healthcare system that continually demands sacrifices from doctors without adequately addressing their welfare, noting that exhausted and stressed physicians could struggle to deliver quality care.

Omoti called for improved staffing levels, adequate rest, regular medical examinations and confidential psychological support for doctors.

On the future of medical practice, he advocated the integration of digital health, artificial intelligence and telemedicine into medical education and service delivery.

He, however, cautioned that technological advancements should complement rather than replace the human connection between doctors and patients.

Meanwhile, Arohunmolase disclosed that Ondo State had lost more than 400 doctors to migration and other forms of attrition in the past five years, leaving about 500 doctors in public health institutions.

He said the situation had worsened the doctor-to-patient ratio in the state to approximately one doctor for every 6,000 patients, placing enormous pressure on the remaining workforce.

“There was a time when we had about 900 to 1,000 doctors in the system. About 400 have exited. This has placed an enormous burden on the sector,” he said.

The state NMA chairman appealed to the Ondo State Government to improve doctors’ remuneration and working conditions to attract and retain medical personnel and reduce burnout.

He commended Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa for approving the new circular on doctors’ remuneration issued by the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, but noted that some states offered remuneration above the national rate to retain their doctors.

Arohunmolase also attributed the high rate of medical tourism among wealthy Nigerians and politicians to inadequate healthcare infrastructure and a shortage of essential medical equipment.

He lamented that Ondo State might not have up to four defibrillators, devices used to restore normal heart rhythm in certain life-threatening emergencies.

According to him, many Nigerian doctors practising abroad received their training locally and possess the competence required to deliver quality healthcare, but are driven away by systemic inadequacies.

He called for increased government investment in the health sector, noting that Nigeria’s estimated two to three per cent budgetary allocation to health remained far below the 15 per cent commitment under the Abuja Declaration.

World.title: Alleged Rights Violation: Court dismisses El-Rufai’s N120m suit
World.content:
Nasir El-Rufai

By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja

A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) sitting at Maitama, Abuja, on Monday dismissed a fundamental rights enforcement suit brought before it by the detained former governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai.

Listed as respondents in the legal action were the Department of State Services (DSS), the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), and the Attorney General of the Federation (AGF).

El-Rufai, who served as governor from 2015 to 2023 and as minister of the FCT under former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration, had accused the respondents in the suit of violating his rights.

He further urged the court to invalidate letters of invitation extended to him by both the ICPC and the EFCC and demanded N120 million in damages from the respondents.

Delivering judgment in the matter, Justice Sylvanus Oriji held that the legal action was without merit and dismissed it.

The court held that the letters of invitation, which requested the former governor to appear before the federal agencies investigating allegations against him, met constitutional requirements and did not infringe his fundamental rights.

The court held that the agencies acted within their mandates by inviting him to shed light on issues raised against him.

Besides, the court declined to declare that the DSS’s attempt to arrest the applicant at Nnamdi Azikiwe Airport amounted to a violation of his rights.

It held that the DSS has a statutory responsibility to maintain a watchlist and to arrest persons of interest.

Justice Oriji held that the former governor could not use the court to stop government agencies from performing their legitimate duties.

The court held that, contrary to El-Rufai’s contention, the agencies did not need a warrant to effect such an arrest.

On whether the confiscation of the applicant’s international passport by the DSS was a violation of his rights, the court said it was satisfied that the seizure was lawful and carried out pursuant to the powers of the DSS.

It held that the applicant failed to adduce evidence to establish that the seizure was continuous, permanent and unlawful.

Consequently, aside from dismissing the case, the court awarded costs of N200,000 against the applicant in favour of each of the four respondents.

It will be recalled that El-Rufai also filed another N1 billion fundamental rights enforcement suit, which is pending before the Federal High Court in Abuja.

Listed as respondents in the suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/345/2026, are the ICPC, the AGF and the Inspector-General of Police.

He specifically challenged the legality of the warrant the ICPC relied on to search his Abuja residence.

El-Rufai is praying the court to declare that the search warrant dated February 4, which the Chief Magistrate of the Magistrate’s Court of the FCT signed to authorise the search and seizure of items from his residence, is invalid, null and void.

He also sought a declaration that the search warrant was legally defective for lacking particularity and for “material drafting errors, ambiguity in execution parameters, overbreadth, and absence of probable cause, thereby constituting an unlawful and unreasonable search in violation of Section 37 of the Constitution.”

Other reliefs he sought include a declaration that the invasion and search of his residence at House 12, Mambilla Street, Aso Drive, Abuja, on February 19 at about 2 p.m., executed by agents of the ICPC and the Inspector-General of Police under the invalid warrant, “amounts to a gross violation of the applicant’s fundamental rights to dignity of the human person, personal liberty, fair hearing, and privacy under Sections 34, 35, 36, and 37 of the Constitution.”

The chief magistrate, who was initially listed as the 2nd respondent, was subsequently delisted from the case by the applicant.

All the respondents have since urged the court to dismiss the case as lacking in merit.

World.title: Sokoto ADC, APC clash over Tinubu’s INEC nominee
World.content:
President Tinubu

By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

SOKOTO — The African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Sokoto State and the state government have disagreed over President Bola Tinubu’s nomination of Professor Mustapha Aliyu as an Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) National Commissioner representing the North-West, with the opposition demanding closer scrutiny of his political neutrality and the government defending his credentials.

The disagreement has renewed debate over the independence of the electoral body and the need to sustain public confidence in its officials ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State, Hon. Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, called on Tinubu to reconsider the nomination and urged the Senate to conduct a thorough screening of Aliyu before confirming his appointment.

Dan’iya, in a statement issued by his media aide, Aminu Abdullahi, cited the nominee’s reported family relationship with Governor Ahmed Aliyu and raised questions about his alleged political affiliations.

He argued that appointments into INEC required transparent scrutiny to prevent doubts about the impartiality of officials responsible for conducting elections.

“The independence of INEC is too important to be treated as a routine political appointment. Nigerians must have confidence that those entrusted with managing our elections will act without fear, favour or political pressure,” Dan’iya said.

The ADC candidate, however, acknowledged that family ties alone did not establish wrongdoing or automatically disqualify a nominee.

He said the reported relationship between the nominee and the governor made it necessary for the Senate to verify whether Aliyu met the constitutional requirements for the position.

Dan’iya specifically cited Section 156(1)(a) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides that a person appointed as a member of INEC must not belong to a political party.

He urged the Senate to verify the nominee’s political affiliations, eligibility and ability to discharge his responsibilities without partisan influence.

The ADC candidate also called on senators representing Sokoto State and the North-West to seek relevant disclosures during the screening process, insisting that the credibility of the electoral commission should take precedence over political considerations.

“If credible evidence establishes that the nominee is constitutionally disqualified, the Senate should refuse confirmation, and the President should nominate a qualified alternative,” Dan’iya said.

He maintained that no nominee should be exempted from scrutiny because of political connections or relationships with public officeholders.

Government defends nomination

The Sokoto State Government rejected the ADC candidate’s concerns, describing them as an attempt to politicise what it considers a merit-based appointment.

The governor’s Special Adviser on Political Matters, Faruku Labbo, said Dan’iya should provide evidence that Aliyu belonged to the All Progressives Congress (APC) or held a party position that could constitute a constitutional impediment to his nomination.

In a statement on Sunday, Labbo maintained that the nominee’s family relationship with Governor Ahmed Aliyu was insufficient, on its own, to establish constitutional disqualification.

“Although Professor Mustapha Aliyu remains a brother to Governor Ahmed Aliyu Sokoto, he is not holding any position in the All Progressives Congress at any level,” Labbo said.

He described Aliyu as a distinguished academic qualified for national service and urged the public and the Senate to assess the nomination based on the professor’s professional credentials, constitutional eligibility and capacity to perform the role impartially.

Labbo also argued that the nomination was intended to fill vacancies arising from the expiration of the tenures of serving electoral commissioners, and should not be interpreted as an attempt to advance the political interests of the Sokoto State Government or any individual.

The government’s response followed the Presidency’s announcement on October 16, 2026, of Aliyu’s nomination alongside those of other national commissioners and resident electoral commissioners.

The nominations are subject to the applicable constitutional procedures, including Senate confirmation where required.

The disagreement has brought renewed attention to the standards of transparency, political neutrality and accountability expected of officials appointed to oversee Nigeria’s elections.

As political parties intensify preparations for the 2027 general elections, the Senate’s screening process is expected to attract public scrutiny, with the ADC insisting that the nominee’s eligibility and political neutrality must be established and the state government maintaining that his nomination should not be discredited solely on the basis of family ties.

The nominee’s eligibility and the applicable constitutional requirements remain matters for assessment through the appropriate procedures.

World.title: United Nigeria Airlines builds health centre in Ekiti
World.content:
…Oyebanji promises equipment, medical personnel

By Rotimi Ojomoyela

ADO-EKITI — United Nigeria Airlines has constructed and handed over a community health centre, a solar-powered borehole and a perimeter fence to the Ekiti State Government as part of its corporate social responsibility initiative.

The facilities, located in Aso-Ayegunle, Ado-Ekiti, were commissioned by Governor Biodun Oyebanji, who pledged that the state government would equip the centre, provide medical personnel and integrate it into the state’s primary healthcare system.

Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Prof. Obiora Okonkwo, said the intervention was designed to ensure that communities benefited directly from the airline’s presence and business operations in the state.

He said the project demonstrated the importance of public-private partnerships in addressing community needs, particularly where government resources alone might not be sufficient to provide essential infrastructure.

Okonkwo commended Oyebanji for creating an enabling environment for private-sector participation in the state’s development, describing the governor’s approach to collaboration with businesses as a key factor behind the initiative.

He explained that the Ekiti State Government had selected United Nigeria Airlines as its preferred carrier after assessing its operational capacity and services.

According to him, the company decided to reciprocate the confidence reposed in it by investing in the welfare of residents rather than simply operating its business without making a meaningful contribution to the host community.

The airline chairman said the company had undertaken similar interventions in other parts of the country, including providing relief to communities affected by flooding in Bayelsa State and supporting projects in Anambra State.

He described the Aso-Ayegunle project as particularly significant because of its connection with the airline’s relationship with the Ekiti State Government and the development opportunities associated with the state’s aviation sector.

“As a matter of fact, most communities where we operate have benefited from our presence. We have carried out interventions in different locations and at various stations. Some of these communities have experienced calamities.

“I remember when there was flooding in Bayelsa State; we were there to provide relief. In Anambra State, we have also undertaken several projects, and we have done similar things in other places. More interventions are still in the pipeline for areas we have not yet covered,” Okonkwo said.

He said the project reflected the state government’s commitment to working with private businesses to deliver development.

“This project is special. It is special because of what we found when we came to this community. It is also special because the governor of this state has demonstrated extraordinary commitment to public-private partnerships. His support has been amazing. He has a vision of defining the role of government while allowing the private sector to do business,” he said.

Okonkwo explained that the airline was approached by the state government after it conducted due diligence on the company’s operations and fleet.

“There was no application and no interview. They conducted their due diligence and reached out to us. They were satisfied that the services we offer and the fleet we have could meet their needs. We were touched by the confidence they reposed in us, and we felt we should show the world that this kind of partnership works. That is why we have come here with this special intervention,” he said.

He also highlighted the airline’s support for tourism in Ekiti, disclosing that members of its delegation visited Ikogosi Warm Springs during their stay in the state.

The airline chairman expressed optimism that the partnership would create further opportunities, particularly as Ekiti develops its capacity to export agricultural products.

“Our mission and commitment to this state do not end with this commissioning. I believe this is just the beginning of the good things that will come out of this relationship. We have made a commitment, and as the state develops, particularly in the area of exporting agricultural products, I will be ready to provide the necessary support when the opportunity arises,” he said.

In his remarks, Oyebanji thanked the airline’s management and staff for the investment, describing the project as a valuable contribution to the government’s efforts to expand access to primary healthcare.

The governor explained that the arrangement required the airline to construct the facility, while the state government would be responsible for equipping and operating it.

He promised that the Ministry of Health would ensure that the centre was adequately staffed, supplied and integrated into the existing primary healthcare system.

Oyebanji also urged residents to take ownership of the facility, protect the infrastructure and ensure that it served its intended purpose.

He said the centre would reduce the burden on residents who previously had to travel considerable distances to access medical services, particularly pregnant women, nursing mothers and children.

The Ewi of Ado-Ekiti, Oba Rufus Adejugbe, described the commissioning as a significant development for Aso-Ayegunle.

The monarch recalled the initial resistance that greeted the acquisition of land for the airport and urged residents to protect the health centre and prevent the facility from deteriorating.

He stressed that the community had a collective responsibility to preserve infrastructure provided for its welfare.

Also speaking, a community representative, Fajuyi Olumide, described the project as a major development for Aso-Ayegunle and thanked the airline and the state government for the intervention.

Olumide said the facility had raised hopes among residents who, according to him, had waited for greater development and government presence in the community.

He expressed optimism that the project would be followed by other interventions capable of improving residents’ living conditions.

World.title: CAS verdict on Senegal AFCON title appeal ‘expected end November’
World.content:
AFCON

The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced Monday that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco is expected at the end of November.

CAS said in a statement that a hearing of the case took place behind closed doors at its headquarters in Lausanne on October 8.

“The panel have begun and continue their deliberations,” the organisation which resolves international sports disputes explained.

“The CAS arbitrators have decided to issue a complete ruling which includes legal grounds, known as a CAS Award. This process will require several weeks, with the CAS Award expected at the end of November 2026.”

At the January 18 final in Rabat, Senegal won 1-0 thanks to Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal, but the occasion was marred by chaotic scenes near the end of normal time when many Senegal players walked off the pitch in protest at the decision to award Morocco a penalty with the match still goalless.

Some Senegalese supporters also attempted a pitch invasion, and the game was held up for almost 20 minutes before the Senegal players returned.

In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title.

World.title: Flood kills two, submerges 18 communities in Nasarawa
World.content:
By Edwin Philip, Lafia

The Nasarawa State Government has urged residents of flood-prone communities to heed evacuation warnings and move to higher ground following flooding that submerged 18 communities in the Doma Local Government Area, killing two people and displacing several others.

The Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr Nawani Aboki, made the appeal on Monday while briefing journalists in Lafia on the impact of the disaster in the affected communities.

Aboki said Governor Abdullahi Sule had directed the Director-General of the Nasarawa State Emergency Management Agency to visit the affected communities to assess the damage and determine the necessary interventions.

He said the government was working towards providing assistance to residents affected by the disaster.

“We are hoping that anytime this week concrete actions will be taken by government. Yesterday, when I was returning, I was there with the chairman of the local government to sympathise with the people and condole with them,” the commissioner said.

According to him, two people have died as a result of the flooding, while several others have been displaced. Buildings and farmlands were also reportedly destroyed.

Describing the incident as massive flooding, Aboki said residents had been advised against returning to their homes until the floodwaters receded.

“It is not just normal flooding, but massive flooding that took place. We are hoping that the flooding will end and the waters dry up so that people can resume their normal activities,” he said.

“But we have asked them not to go back yet. Let them wait until we see the water actually receding back to the River Benue. We are not sure if more water will be coming in from the Lagdo Dam in Cameroon; it will even be worse than it is currently,” he added.

The commissioner said the government was also prepared to provide support and relief supplies to affected residents to reduce the risk of disease outbreaks following the flooding.

He explained that several smaller communities were clustered within larger settlements, complicating efforts to assess the full extent of the damage and the number of people affected.

Aboki cited Agyma, where more than eight communities were reportedly affected, and Rukubi and Akpanaja, where several communities were also said to be experiencing the impact of the flooding.

The government urged residents in vulnerable areas to prioritise their safety and remain in safer locations until the floodwaters had sufficiently receded.

World.title: 40 years after Dele Giwa’s killing, MRA demands justice
World.content:
Dele Giwa

By Elizabeth Osayande

Media Rights Agenda (MRA) has called on the Federal Government to implement a court order directing it to investigate the assassination of renowned journalist and founding Editor-in-Chief of Newswatch magazine, Dele Giwa, and prosecute those found responsible.

The call came on Monday, October 19, 2026, as Nigeria marked the 40th anniversary of Giwa’s death. He was killed on October 19, 1986, by a parcel bomb delivered to his residence in Ikeja, Lagos.

In a statement issued in Lagos, the media rights organisation described the failure to resolve the case four decades later as a “shameful reminder of the entrenched culture of impunity for attacks against journalists in Nigeria.”

MRA’s Deputy Executive Director, Ayode Longe, said the anniversary should go beyond remembering Giwa’s contributions to journalism and should prompt renewed scrutiny of the failure to deliver justice.

“Forty years is far too long for the assassination of a journalist of Dele Giwa’s stature to remain unresolved. His killing must not be reduced to a recurring anniversary in Nigeria’s media calendar, accompanied by tributes and expressions of outrage but without meaningful progress towards accountability,” Longe said.

He recalled that on February 16, 2024, MRA secured a judgment at the Federal High Court in Abuja in a suit against the Attorney-General of the Federation.

According to him, the court ordered the Federal Government to investigate Giwa’s murder and other unresolved killings of journalists, and ensure the prosecution of those responsible.

Longe said the government had yet to demonstrate progress or report concrete steps taken to establish the facts surrounding the killings, identify those responsible and pursue accountability in accordance with the law.

He described the lack of visible action as a disregard for a valid and subsisting judicial order.

The MRA official urged the Attorney-General of the Federation, the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant authorities to provide a clear account of the steps taken to implement the judgment.

He said the report should include the status of the investigation, measures already undertaken and plans for prosecution where supported by the available evidence and applicable law.

Longe argued that the passage of time did not extinguish the state’s responsibility to pursue accountability for an unlawful killing. He urged investigators to explore all lawful avenues, including reviewing historical case files, witness accounts, documentary evidence and other materials that could help establish the circumstances of Giwa’s assassination.

He also called for the use of modern forensic and investigative techniques where appropriate and feasible.

According to him, the failure to resolve the case sends a damaging message about the safety of journalists in Nigeria and the consequences of violence against people exercising their right to freedom of expression.

He warned that leaving such a high-profile killing unresolved could signal to those inclined to attack journalists that they might do so without facing consequences.

Longe said MRA’s campaign for justice in Giwa’s case formed part of its broader efforts to secure accountability for the killings of journalists in Nigeria.

He called on the Federal Government to establish mechanisms to protect journalists, ensure law enforcement agencies respond effectively to threats and attacks, and demonstrate through concrete action that violence against media professionals would not be tolerated.

He noted that Giwa’s legacy included his contribution to the development of a media sector committed to investigating public affairs, holding those in power accountable and providing citizens with information needed to participate in public life.

According to him, a meaningful commemoration of Giwa’s life and work requires renewed commitment to truth, accountability, professional courage and the public’s right to know.

“As Nigeria marks four decades since his assassination, the most fitting tribute to Dele Giwa would be demonstrable progress towards justice for him and his family, stronger guarantees for the safety of journalists, and a national commitment to ending impunity for crimes against journalists and other media professionals,” Longe said.

World.title: Alleged Ogu PDP Aspirant Denies Contesting Party’s Guber Race
World.content:
James Sowole in Abeokuta

As the Peoples Democratic Party(PDP) in Ogun State continues to drag the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) over the omission of its governorship candidate, Ladi Adebutu, from the list of contestants, a chieftain of the party, Topa Olusegun Peter, has raised the alarm over the alleged unauthorised use of his name as a governorship aspirant ahead of the 2027 electionS.

Peter, who is the Baale Olorunsogo, Ilara in Imeko Afon Local Government Area of the state, insisted that he never purchased a nomination form or authorised anyone to represent him in the purported political race.

He also alleged that the Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the council area, Ramoni Adebolu, and some other APC chieftains approached him with a political offer before his name allegedly surfaced in newspaper publications as a PDP governorship aspirant.

The traditional titleholder, who addressed journalists in Abeokuta, claimed that Adebolu subsequently urged him to remain calm and allegedly promised him financial benefits, a car and a major political appointment after the emergence of the APC governorship candidate, Senator Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi.

Peter, however, said he rejected the initial political offer and had no knowledge of any arrangement to make him a governorship aspirant in the PDP.

The development took a more serious turn when Peter expressed concern over a purported petition allegedly written to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) by a lawyer, Anderson Asemota of Neplus Ultra Attorneys, demanding that the commission publish his client’s name as a governorship aspirant within 48 hours.

Peter denied knowing or authorising the lawyer to act on his behalf, calling for an investigation into how his name was allegedly used in the reported correspondence.

He also raised concerns about the safety of his family, appealing to security agencies and other relevant authorities to intervene and ensure their protection.

Narrating his experience, Peter said: “I was shocked and deeply surprised to discover that my name had appeared in newspaper publications as a governorship aspirant on the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) platform, an aspiration I know absolutely nothing about.”

The PDP chieftain insisted that he had neither expressed an intention to contest the governorship election nor signed any document to that effect.

“I wish to emphasise here, again, that I never purchased a governorship nomination form, signed any document expressing an intention to contest the governorship election, or authorised anyone to act on my behalf in this regard,” he said.

Explaining how the controversy allegedly began, Peter said Adebolu and some other APC chieftains contacted him, claiming they had a political position to offer him.

According to him, the meeting took place in Ilara, his hometown, where the politicians informed him that the proposed position was in the PDP but did not explain its precise nature.

He said he immediately rejected the offer, stressing that he was not interested in the arrangement.

“We met in my hometown, Ilara, and they informed me that the position was in the PDP but did not explain its exact nature. But I told them there and then that I was not interested because such could only come from my party, the PDP,” Peter stated.

He said he was subsequently taken aback when newspaper publications identified him as a PDP governorship aspirant.

According to him, he immediately contacted Adebolu to seek clarification after discovering the publications.

Peter alleged that the APC chairman told him to remain calm and promised him financial benefits and a car.

He further claimed that Adebolu assured him of a major political position after the emergence of Adeola as the APC’s governorship candidate.

Peter also denied receiving money from Adebolu or any of the other individuals he mentioned.

“For the avoidance of doubt, I did not collect any money from the individuals mentioned in this statement,” he said.

Peter’s concerns, however, extended beyond the newspaper publications to the reported petition allegedly submitted to INEC in his name.

He said he was deeply troubled by reports that a lawyer had written to the electoral commission on his behalf without his knowledge or authorisation.

The baale specifically denied any relationship with Asemota, the lawyer alleged to have demanded that INEC publish his name as a governorship aspirant within 48 hours.

“I have never spoken with or met the lawyer, Anderson Asemota of Neplus Ultra Attorneys, alleged to have written the petition on my behalf,” he said.

The PDP chieftain questioned how documents could have been submitted in his name without his consent, urging the electoral commission to investigate the matter.

He called for a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the reported petition, including the identity of those who initiated the correspondence and the basis on which his name was allegedly used.

“I therefore call for a thorough investigation into how my name came to be used in this manner and how documents were submitted in my name without my knowledge,” Peter said.

Amid the unfolding controversy, Peter expressed fears over his safety and his family, calling on security agencies and other relevant authorities to intervene.

He appealed to Nigerians and well-meaning individuals to help ensure their protection, while urging the authorities to establish the facts surrounding the alleged unauthorised use of his name.

“I am appealing to Nigerians, relevant authorities, security agencies, and all well-meaning individuals to come to my aid and help ensure the safety of my life and every member of my family,” he said.

Although Peter did not provide specific details of any direct threat against him or his family, he said the circumstances surrounding the alleged use of his name had caused him serious concern.

He urged the relevant authorities to investigate the matter and bring anyone found culpable to justice.

The allegations, if substantiated, could raise questions about the use of individuals’ identities in political correspondence and the processes for verifying claims made in the names of prospective candidates.

Peter also used the briefing to reaffirm his loyalty to the PDP, insisting that he had remained a member of the party since its formation in 1998 and had never defected to another political platform.

He said his political allegiance had remained consistent over the years and that he had no knowledge of, or involvement in, the purported governorship aspiration.

“I have been a loyal member of the PDP since 1998, the year the party was formed, and I have never defected to another political party. My commitment to the party has remained consistent throughout the years,” he said.

Peter further stated that Hon. Ladi Adebutu emerged as the sole candidate of the PDP in the Ogun State governorship primary election held on May 24, 2026, an exercise he said he supervised in his ward.

He said the development was another reason he wanted the circumstances surrounding the reported governorship aspiration clarified.

The PDP urged INEC to disregard any document purportedly submitted by him or on his behalf.

“I also urge INEC to disregard any document purportedly submitted by me or on my behalf, establish the circumstances surrounding the fraudulent use of my name, and bring the perpetrators to book,” he said.

The controversy comes as political activities and alignments ahead of the 2027 general elections gather momentum in Ogun State.

World.title: RMB Nigeria Wins AIHN M&A Deal of the Year Award
World.content:
RMB Nigeria has been awarded M&A Deal of the Year 2025 by the Association of Issuing Houses of Nigeria (AIHN), recognising its role as exclusive financial adviser to Helios Investment Partners on the US$583 million acquisition of Axxela Limited.

RMB Nigeria advised Helios on the landmark acquisition of Axxela, a leading energy infrastructure company in West Africa, by BlueCore Gas InfraCo Limited.

The transaction involved Helios Investment Partners’ divestment of its 75 per cent equity interest in Axxela and Sojitz Corporation’s sale of its remaining 25 per cent stake through the exercise of its tag-along rights, resulting in the transfer of full ownership to BlueCore.

As one of the significant private equity exits in Nigeria’s midstream energy sector in recent years, the transaction highlights the role of strategic capital and investor participation in supporting the development of critical energy infrastructure.

Commenting on the recognition, Chief Executive Officer of RMB Nigeria, Bayo Ajayi, said: “Transactions of this scale demonstrate the value of sophisticated financial advice, deep market understanding and disciplined execution in bringing strategic opportunities to fruition. This

recognition reflects our commitment to working alongside clients to navigate complex transactions and deliver solutions aligned with their long-term objectives.’’

“We remain focused on bringing together the expertise, perspective and execution capabilities required to support businesses and investors as they pursue strategic opportunities across Africa.”

Executive Director and Head of Investment Banking, Broader Africa,

RMB Nigeria, Chidi Iwuchukwu, added: “The Axxela transaction required a clear understanding of the deal dynamics, the interests of the parties involved and the strategic considerations underpinning the transaction. Our role as exclusive financial adviser was to bring the financial expertise and execution discipline required to support Helios Investment Partners through this important milestone.’’

“This recognition from AIHN underscores the depth of our investment banking capabilities and our continued focus on delivering value through complex, strategically significant transactions.”

RMB Nigeria continues to support corporate and institutional clients across Africa with financial advisory, funding and investment banking solutions. By combining deep market insight, sector expertise and execution capabilities with the reach of the broader RMB network, the bank supports clients in navigating complex transactions, deploying capital and pursuing strategic growth opportunities.

World.title: CRMI Seeks Mandatory Risk Reporting, Management Units in MDAs
World.content:
Oluchi Chibuzor

The Chartered Risk Management Institute of Nigeria (CRMI) has called for mandatory risk management reporting by organisations registered in Nigeria and the establishment of dedicated risk management functions across ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs) to strengthen institutional resilience, safeguard public trust and promote sustainable national development.

Speaking at the 25th anniversary and annual international conference held in Lagos recently, the President of CRMI, Mr. Kevin §ºUgwuoke, said that risks don’t arrive one at a time, but they connect, and a failure in one place could diffuse through an entire organisation.

The event, with the theme: ‘The Resilience Edge’, he affirmed, means that identifying risks and writing controls is no longer enough.

“Resilience is the ability to make sound decisions under pressure, to keep essential activities working, to adapt as circumstances change, and to recover, while continuing to create value. That is the edge,” he stated.

However, looking ahead, Ugwuoke said: “Our vision is a Nigeria in which risk management is not the preserve of banks, but part of the daily life of the nation: in every boardroom and every small business; in every ministry, department and agency; in agriculture and energy, health and education, manufacturing and technology; and wherever public trust is held.

“That is why we are advocating. We are pressing for organisations registered in Nigeria to report on how they manage risk, and for a risk management function in every ministry, department and agency. A more professional approach to risk, across all sectors, is the foundation of national resilience.

“But advocacy alone will not carry us. The Institute is a bridge between the private sector, the public sector and academia, and a bridge needs people at both ends. So, I call on every one of you, regulators, executives, entrepreneurs, public servants, academics and students to connect with this Institute.”

He stressed that as they celebrate their “Chartered status, conferred by Act No. 39 of 2022, it’s our most important milestone. It is also a responsibility to uphold professional competence, and to earn public trust through the quality of our advice and our conduct.

“We have made our contributions along the way. CRMI contributed to the national conversation on credit bureaus from as early as 2002, leading up to the CBN’s introduction of credit bureaus in Nigeria. “With the CIBN, we launched the Chartered Risk Manager certification, now in its tenth set. On that note, we are happy to announce the commencement of Executive Risk Management Certification in collaboration with the prestigious Lagos Business School.”

Also, the Director, Risk Management, CBN, Dr. Blaise Ijebor, urged risk professionals to always look at fiscal and monetary policies after their operations to ensure compliance.

“Then you need to look at operations and compliance. And the risk duty, therefore, is to monitor the implementation and see how that affects your cash flow timing,” Ijebor said.

The keynote speaker, and Chairman of the Board of PENCOM, Mr. Opeyemi Agbaje, said that 25 years represent a remarkable journey of vision, perseverance, professional commitment, institution building and the collective determination to establish risk management as an essential pillar of sound organisational governance and sustainable development.

He noted that the theme, ‘The Resilience Edge’, speaks directly to the realities of time and the responsibility they share as risk management professionals.

He explained that resilience edge is the ability to anticipate change, absorb disruption, adapt effectively, recover responsibly, and transform challenges into opportunities for sustainable growth.

“It goes beyond the traditional understanding of risk management as a function concerned primarily with identifying threats and preventing losses. It positions risk management as a strategic instrument for protecting value, creating opportunities, enabling innovation, and strengthening decision-making.

“We operate in a world where uncertainty has become a defining feature of business, governance, and national development. Economic volatility, geopolitical tensions, technological disruption, cyber threats, climate -related challenges, regulatory changes, health pandemics, and evolving stakeholder expectations continue to test the strength of organisations across every sector,” he stated.

World.title: Oyebanji Unveils Industrialisation Blueprint, Targets Small Businesses Growth
World.content:
Gbenga Sodeinde in Ado-Ekiti

Ekiti State Governor, Mr. Biodun Oyebanji, has unveiled an ambitious industrialisation blueprint for his second term in office, declaring that his administration will shift from building infrastructure to driving industrial growth, expanding local value addition and supporting small businesses as part of efforts to transform the state’s economy.

The governor said the next phase of his administration would focus on ensuring that agricultural produce grown in Ekiti is processed locally into finished products capable of generating higher economic value, creating jobs and stimulating private sector-led development.

Speaking on his second-term agenda during an interview in Ado Ekiti, Oyebanji said the foundation for economic expansion had already been laid through massive investments in roads, electricity, agriculture and other critical infrastructure during his first term.

According to him, the priority now is to convert those investments into productivity and shared prosperity through industrialisation.

“Our next major focus is industrialisation and support for small businesses. That is the only way we can deepen our shared prosperity agenda,” the governor said.

He explained that while infrastructure development would continue, greater attention would now be devoted to empowering small and medium-scale enterprises by improving access to affordable financing for welders, tailors, hairdressers, barbers, artisans and other entrepreneurs to expand their businesses and create employment.

Oyebanji said his administration would also strengthen agricultural value chains by ensuring that farmers produce at scale and are linked to reliable off-takers and processing companies that would convert raw agricultural products into finished goods for local consumption and export.

To attract investment into the state, the governor said the government was implementing reforms to improve the ease of doing business through simplified approval processes, streamlined taxation, reforms in land administration and the establishment of a one-stop investment centre for investors.

The governor noted that these initiatives had already begun attracting significant private investment into the state’s agriculture sector, particularly within the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zone, where investors have committed billions of naira to agribusiness projects.

Oyebanji cited Agbeyewa Farms, described as one of the world’s largest cassava farms, alongside Arog Agro-Allied and other agribusinesses as evidence of growing investor confidence in Ekiti’s economy.

He added that the African Development Bank’s selection of Ekiti as a Tier-2 State under the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zone Programme would further strengthen the state’s industrial ambitions through irrigation development and expanded agricultural production.

The governor stressed that the government’s responsibility was not to establish industries but to create the right environment for businesses to flourish.

“Capital flows to places where it is treated well. Our responsibility is to provide infrastructure, guarantee security, improve the business environment and create policies that encourage investors to establish industries and create jobs,” he said.

Beyond industrialisation, Oyebanji disclosed that his administration was accelerating efforts to position the Ekiti Agro-Allied International Cargo Airport as a 24-hour facility through the installation of an Instrument Landing System, airfield lighting and a privately developed aviation fuel depot.

According to him, the airport would become a strategic hub for investment, cargo movement and agricultural exports once the ongoing projects are completed.

He also revealed plans to expand the state’s transportation system through the deployment of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered and electric vehicles, saying the initiative would reduce transportation costs, improve mobility and support economic activities without disrupting existing transport operators.

Oyebanji said the industrialisation agenda would be reflected prominently in the 2027 budget, expressing confidence that the strategy would accelerate productivity, create sustainable jobs and position Ekiti State as the leading destination for investment, agro-processing and manufacturing in Nigeria.

“Our central objective in this second term is to catalyse productivity and ensure that our economy becomes more productive. Everything we are doing is geared towards creating opportunities for businesses to thrive and for our people to enjoy greater prosperity,” the governor said.

World.title: Kwankwasiyya Movement Kicks against Proposed N55bn  LGA Loan in Kano
World.content:
Ahmad Sorondinki in Kano

The Kwankwasiyya Movement has questioned the reported plan by the Kano State Government to compel the 44 local government councils in the state to take a combined loan of about N55 billion from a commercial bank.

In a statement issued last Saturday and signed by its spokesperson, Dr. Habibu Mohammed, the movement said each council may be required to assume a debt of about N1.3 billion to fund Computer-Based Test (CBT) centres, an unspecified project and an empowerment programme.

According to the movement, the proposed breakdown includes about N632.57 million per council for CBT centres; N500 million for an undisclosed project, and N117.41 million for empowerment.

While supporting educational infrastructure and empowerment, the group said such projects must be pursued transparently and lawfully, and asked why councils should borrow for projects reportedly to be controlled by the state.

The movement queried the timing of the loan ahead of the electoral cycle, and asked the government to disclose its revenue position and why existing allocations cannot fund the projects. It said that, though it was not alleging the loan was meant for election financing, safeguards must be in place to prevent diversion to partisan activities.

It also demanded full details of the projects, including locations of the CBT centres, feasibility studies, the nature of the N500 million project, and the selection criteria for empowerment beneficiaries.

The statement further demanded an account of the previous joint empowerment programme, particularly the monthly women empowerment initiative, asking how much each council contributed, the total amount received by the state, the amount disbursed, administrative costs and remaining balance, and why the programme lasted less than ten months.

The Movement called on the Kano State House of Assembly to clarify whether it approved the loan, and to publish relevant resolutions, insisting that repayment terms and legal basis must be scrutinised in line with the Supreme Court’s July 2024 judgment on local government autonomy.

It also urged the commercial bank linked to the facility to conduct thorough due diligence on the legality, repayment capacity and purpose of the loan, warning that public sector lending carries legal and reputational responsibilities.

The group noted that while a change of government does not nullify a valid loan, a future administration has the right to review inherited financial commitments where illegality is found.

It urged the state government, local government chairmen, the Assembly, and the bank to ensure that public borrowing serves public interest and not political convenience.

World.title: PDP Demands Answer from Gov Alia over Wike’s N30bn Monthly FAAC Revelation
World.content:
Says no accountability in Benue since May 29, 2023

George Okoh in Makurdi

The People Democratic Party (PDP), Benue State chapter, has challenged the state Governor, Hyacinth Alia, to explain his administration’s silence following the disclosure by the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, that Benue State now receives as much as N30 billion monthly from the Federation Account.

According to the PDP state Publicity Secretary, Bright Yima Antyo, the allegation is a weighty statement from a serving federal minister, and he wondered why the Benue State Government has failed to offer a clear public response to the disclosure.

The PDP asked if the governor disputes the figures, “and if he does, why has he not come forward with the actual figures? If he agrees with the minister, why has he not considered it necessary to explain to the people what his administration has done with the enormous resources available to Benue State, following the removal of fuel subsidy,” he asked.

He alleged that since taking office on May 29, 2023, Governor Alia has not delivered a comprehensive public accountability briefing on the revenues received, expenditure incurred, projects executed and results achieved by his administration.

According to him, “Three and a half years in office, the people are still waiting for a transparent and detailed account of how public resources are being managed. Our assessment puts combined FAAC allocations to the state and its 23 local government areas at over ₦1.3 trillion during the period under review. Both tiers of government under the firm grip of Governor Alia owe the Benue people accountability.

“The questions are simple: How much has come in, how much has been spent, and what can the government show for it?

“Where are the functional hospitals, equipped schools, agricultural support programmes, completed roads and other tangible projects across Benue State’s 23 local government areas? In Makurdi, excavated township roads remain unfinished, while the few other projects like the never-ending underpass at High Level in Makurdi continue to raise questions about lack of due process and delivery timelines.”

He added: “The persistent insecurity across the state makes accountability even more urgent. Benue communities continue to suffer attacks, deaths, displacement, and destruction of livelihoods. The government must explain the resources committed to security and demonstrate their impact on protecting lives and restoring peace in the state.”

World.title: Anti-Terrorism: DECAN Honours NSA, Defence Minister, CDS, Service Chiefs, Others
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Defence Correspondents Association of Nigeria (DECAN) has honoured the National Security Adviser (NSA), Mallam Nuhu Ribadu; the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (rtd.); the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Olufemi Oluyede; the Service Chiefs; the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu; and the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Oluwatosin Ajayi, for strengthening Nigeria’s counter-insurgency campaign and recording significant gains in the fight against terrorism.

The heads of the nation’s security institutions received the honours at the third edition of the DECAN Conference and Awards, themed ‘Beyond Kinetic Warfare: Harnessing Technology and Intelligence-Led Operations for Nigeria’s National Security.’

The event brought together senior military and security officials, government representatives, policymakers and journalists to examine emerging security threats and strategies for strengthening Nigeria’s security architecture.

The NSA was represented by the Director of Legal Services at the Office of the NSA, Zakari Mijinyawa, who received the award on his behalf.

Meanwhile, the Special Adviser to the Minister of Defence on Foreign Relations, Air Commodore Adewale Ogunmodede (rtd.), and the Director of Defence Information, Major General Sumaila Uba, received the awards on behalf of the Minister of Defence and the CDS respectively.

According to a statement by DECAN, “The awards are in recognition of their outstanding leadership, strategic coordination and dedicated service in strengthening and managing Nigeria’s national security architecture.”

Nigeria has battled the Boko Haram insurgency for over 15 years, resulting in the loss of lives and the destruction of property worth trillions of naira.

In its fight against terrorism, the Federal Government has arrested thousands of suspects, killed thousands of terrorists and recovered territories previously occupied by insurgents.

In October 2017, the Federal Government commenced the mass trial of terrorism suspects to ensure that justice was served to victims of terrorism across the country.

Since the mass trials began, the Federal Government has secured a total of 1,721 terrorism-related convictions.

The NSA, as coordinator of the counter-terrorism campaign, has continued to provide strategic leadership in efforts to disrupt terrorist logistics and supply networks and dismantle their leadership structures.

In 2026 alone, the Federal Government secured 865 convictions, surpassing the combined total of 856 convictions recorded during the preceding nine years, from 2017 to 2025.

During the ninth phase of the trials at the Federal High Court in Abuja, 386 convictions were secured from 508 cases prosecuted before 10 judges, alongside eight discharges and two acquittals.

Ongoing mass trials in Abuja and at regional military detention facilities, including Kainji, continue to process hundreds of suspects, among them high-profile members of Boko Haram and the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP). Those convicted have received sentences ranging from several years’ imprisonment to life imprisonment and death by hanging.

Approximately 5,000 suspects remain in pre-trial detention facilities across the country as the National Counter-Terrorism Centre and the Ministry of Justice work to review outstanding case files.

These achievements have been made possible through the collaborative efforts of the Armed Forces of Nigeria, the Nigeria Police Force, the DSS, other security agencies, the Ministry of Justice and the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA). These efforts demonstrate the strong inter-agency cooperation among Federal Government institutions working together to end terrorism and insurgency in Nigeria.

Participants at the conference deliberated on the roles of technological innovation, intelligence-sharing, coordinated operations and effective public communication in addressing the country’s evolving security challenges.

DECAN is a professional association of journalists covering defence, security and military affairs in Nigeria. The association promotes accurate and responsible reporting on defence and security matters.

World.title: Breaking: Former Delta Governor Emmanuel Uduaghan is Dead
World.content:
Former Delta State Governor, Dr. Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, is dead.

He was aged 71.

Uduaghan died on Monday morning, according to a statement issued by the family and signed by Toju Anire Uduaghan.

The statement, titled “Announcement of the Passing of His Excellency, Dr. Chief Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, CON,” announced his death with “hearts weighed down by immeasurable grief and profound sorrow.”

“His passing has left us devastated. Words can hardly express the depth of our sorrow at the loss of a man who meant so much to our family and whose life and service touched countless others across Delta State and Nigeria,” the statement said.

Uduaghan served as Commissioner for Health in Delta State from 1999 to 2003 before becoming Secretary to the State Government from 2003 to 2007.

He subsequently served as governor of Delta State from 2007 to 2015.

According to the family, “Throughout his years in public service, he demonstrated a commitment to the human and infrastructural development of Delta State.”

The family described the late former governor as “a source of strength, a father figure, a beloved brother and uncle, and a respected elder,” adding that his presence would be deeply missed.

“His passing is a profound loss to our family, the people of Delta State, and Nigeria at large. We are grateful to Almighty God for his life, his service, and the legacy he leaves behind,” the statement added.

The family also prayed for divine comfort for those mourning his death.

“We pray that Almighty God, in His infinite mercy, will grant his soul eternal rest and comfort our family, friends, associates, former colleagues and all who mourn this painful loss,” it said.

Paying tribute to the former governor, the family said: “Rest well, our beloved Father, Brother, and Uncle. Your memory will forever remain in our hearts, and your legacy will endure in the lives of those you touched. May your gentle soul rest in perfect peace Asamaigor.”

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs’ worrying CAF away record as Da Cruz makes excuses
World.content:
After Kaizer Chiefs suffered a 1-0 defeat to Red Arrows in Zambia, their struggles away from home in the CAF Confederation Cup appear to be far from over.

Amakhosi lost three away matches in the competition last season. Defeats to Egyptian sides Al Masry and Zamalek ultimately contributed to their group-stage exit.

Their latest setback means Kaizer Chiefs have now lost four of their last five away matches in the CAF Confederation Cup, raising concerns about their ability to compete consistently on the continental stage.



Head coach Fernando Da Cruz admitted that his team lacked aggression in the first half against Red Arrows, which made it difficult for them to compete effectively.

“We played a tough first half with no aggression. We were not there inside the duels,” Da Cruz said as per KickOff.

Kaizer Chiefs CAF struggles continue

The French coach acknowledged that his side improved after the break but conceded that they struggled to create enough scoring opportunities.

“In the second half, it was better. We didn’t create a lot of chances, but we made a better second half,” he added.

Da Cruz also pointed to the playing surface as one of the challenges his team faced in Zambia, arguing that the pitch made it difficult for Chiefs to implement their preferred style of play.

“About the field, it was not a field for our advantage. It was not a very good field for us to develop our model game,” he said.



The Amakhosi coach, however, acknowledged that his team needed to adapt to the conditions rather than use them as an excuse for the defeat.

“But we must adapt, we must play with the conditions and the players adapted very well to the conditions,” Da Cruz added.

Kaizer Chiefs must now overturn the 1-0 deficit in the return leg in South Africa if they are to secure a place in the CAF Confederation Cup group stages.

Amakhosi will need to win by at least two clear goals to qualify directly. A one-goal victory would level the aggregate score and send the tie to a penalty shootout if the score remains level after extra time, where applicable.

Can Chiefs make it to the next round?

World.title: PowerBall jackpot resets after R112 million win
World.content:
The PowerBall jackpot has reset after one lucky South African became R112 million richer after scooping the jackpot in the Tuesday, 13 October draw.

The winning ticket was purchased at OK Foods Meyerton, with the player emerging as the sole jackpot winner in PowerBall draw number 1763.

Meyerton is a small industrial and residential town located 18km north of Vereeniging in Gauteng.



Lucky numbers

The five numbers drawn were 3, 15, 24, 30, 31 while the PowerBall bonus ball – which is also required in winning the jackpot – was 7.

Following the win, the PowerBall jackpot now stands at an estimated R12 million for the Tuesday, 20 October draw.

The PowerBall Xtra jackpot, meanwhile, is an estimated R19 million for the next draw on Tuesday evening.



As a reminder, the PowerBall and PowerBall Xtra draws take place every Tuesday and Friday on e.tv (channel 194) and SABC at 21:00 (SA time).

Those wishing to enter have until 20:40 on the night of the draw to do so.

The PowerBall jackpot draw requires players to pick five main numbers from 1 to 50 and one “PowerBall” number from 1 to 16 for an entry fee of R10.00 per board.



Players must be 18 years old.

Urged to come forward

South Africa’s latest PowerBall jackpot winner has been urged to come forward and claim his – or her – life-changing R112 million prize.

The winning ticket holder has yet to come forward as at the time of publishing, with the National Lottery operator encouraging the winner to take the necessary steps to protect their ticket and claim the jackpot.



“We congratulate our latest PowerBall jackpot winner on this extraordinary win. Winning R112-million is a life-changing moment, and we look forward to welcoming the winner when they come forward to claim their prize,” said Kgothatso “KG” Mashile, Head of Marketing at Sizekhaya Holdings.

Advice for the R112 million winner

Mashile urged the winner to complete their personal details on the back of the physical ticket immediately and keep it in a safe place.

Protecting the ticket is an important step towards securing the prize while preparing to claim the jackpot.



Once the winner comes forward, they will also have access to free and confidential professional counselling and financial guidance through Sizekhaya Holdings.

The support is intended to help the winner navigate the significant changes that come with receiving such a large sum of money and make informed decisions about their financial future.

“An extraordinary win like this brings incredible possibilities, but it is important for the winner to approach this new chapter with care and make informed decisions that will help secure their future,” Mashile added.



A life-changing lottery win

The R112 million jackpot could transform the winner’s financial circumstances, but the lottery operator has emphasised the importance of approaching the windfall responsibly.

Professional guidance can help the winner consider their options and plan for the long term rather than make rushed financial decisions.
