World.title: The South African holiday destinations where your money goes furthest
World.content:
From the Eastern Cape to KwaZulu-Natal, these destinations could help stretch your holiday budget this December. Image: canva

South Africans planning a December getaway could save money by looking beyond the country’s biggest holiday destinations.

December is one of the most expensive times of year to travel domestically, with accommodation prices rising sharply in many popular destinations as demand peaks.

But current December 2026 accommodation data shows that there are still destinations where travellers can find relatively better value.



So, where to go on holiday this December?

Gqeberha

Gqeberha is emerging as one of the more affordable holiday destinations for families travelling from Gauteng.

A current December 2026 comparison found that a family of four could get flights from OR Tambo to Gqeberha and 14 nights of accommodation for about R24 600 in total, or roughly R439 per person per night.

The comparison used a two-week stay and flights, making it more useful for holidaymakers than simply comparing nightly room rates. Flights were also substantially cheaper than comparable routes to Durban and Cape Town in the same comparison.



For a family travelling from Johannesburg, that combination can make Gqeberha worth considering even though it is further away.

Jeffrey’s Bay

Just west of Gqeberha, Jeffrey’s Bay is another holiday destination option for travellers looking for a beach holiday without necessarily paying Garden Route hotspot prices.

Current December 2026 hotel data puts the typical nightly price at around R1 204, with available prices ranging from roughly R806 to R2 006.



That does not make every property cheap, particularly during Christmas week, but it provides considerably more choice than simply booking into a luxury resort.

The town also has plenty of beaches and outdoor activities that do not require a large entertainment budget.

Margate and the KZN South Coast

For holidaymakers in KwaZulu-Natal, the South Coast remains one of the most obvious places to look for value.



Margate, Umzumbe, Scottburgh, Pennington and Port Edward all offer self-catering and budget accommodation, giving families the option of spending more of their holiday budget on the actual trip rather than eating out every day.

The KZN South Coast also has the advantage of being within driving distance of Durban and Pietermaritzburg, reducing the cost of flights.

Recent accommodation research found budget options in Umzumbe from around R300 per person per night, while four-person bungalows started at around R1 000 a night. Port Edward also had accommodation options from around R500 a night outside the peak period.



Those are not guaranteed December prices, however, and travellers should check the exact dates before treating them as a holiday budget.

St Helena Bay

Travellers heading to the West Coast could also look at St Helena Bay instead of more expensive destinations around Cape Town.

Current December 2026 hotel data puts the typical nightly price at around R1 584, compared with R1 287 in November.



Available December prices currently range from approximately R1 089 to R2 322.

It is therefore not exactly a bargain-basement destination, but it can offer better value than some of the country’s premium coastal markets.

The big warning about December prices

Holidaymakers should be careful when comparing accommodation prices online.



An August 2026 analysis of more than 5 000 properties found that nearly a third of properties with both September and December rates had increased their cheapest listed December rate.

Among those properties, the median increase was 22.2%.

The same analysis warned that even a December price visible online could still change, while an early-December rate may hide much higher prices around Christmas and New Year. That makes the timing of a trip almost as important as the destination.

World.title: Oil spill warning for motorists on M3 in Cape Town
World.content:
Motorists travelling along the M3 near Wynberg Park in Cape Town are being urged to slow down after an oil spill left the road slippery. Image: Flickr

Motorists travelling along the M3 near Wynberg Park in Cape Town are being urged to slow down after an oil spill left the road slippery and vehicles at risk of losing traction on Monday afternoon.

The warning applies to the M3 northbound near the Wynberg Hill landmark, where drivers are advised to reduce their speed and approach the affected stretch with caution.

Avoid sudden braking

Motorists heading towards Cape Town should remain alert and avoid sudden braking that could cause their vehicles to skid on the slippery surface.



The oil spill poses a potential hazard, particularly for drivers travelling at higher speeds or those who are unaware of the affected section of road.

Motorists are urged to exercise patience and remain vigilant while travelling through the area.

Further details about the spill, including its cause and whether any traffic disruptions or road closures will follow, have not yet been confirmed.



This breaking news story is being updated and more details will be published shortly. Please refresh the page for the fullest version.

World.title: South Africans react to Cyril Ramaphosa’s viral R20 church offering (watch)
World.content:
President Cyril Ramaphosa’s visit to a church in Khayelitsha during the ANC’s Western Cape election campaign has sparked debate on social media. Image: Wikimedia Commons

President Cyril Ramaphosa’s visit to a church in Khayelitsha during the ANC’s Western Cape election campaign has sparked debate on social media, after a post on X claimed he donated just R20 to the church’s offering basket.

The claim quickly attracted reactions from South Africans online, with some mocking the alleged amount while others defended the president, arguing that any donation should be appreciated regardless of its size.

Local government elections

Cyril Ramaphosa visited the Salvation Church of the Revival of Faith at Mew Way Hall in Khayelitsha on Sunday, as part of the ANC’s campaign activities ahead of the local government elections on 4 November.



A post on X claiming that the president placed R20 in the offering basket circulated widely, prompting a mixture of jokes, criticism and support.

However, the R20 figure comes from the social media post and has not been independently verified.

President Ramaphosa donated R20 only for church offering in Khayelitsha . Ankole 🔥🔥🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/dYrTWfI4ov  October 18, 2026

‘He was supposed to circulate the offering basket’

Some users took aim at the president over the alleged donation, with one suggesting he had missed an opportunity to collect more money for the church.

“He ain’t strategic, he was supposed to have circulated the offering basket himself!” the user joked.

Others argued that the amount should not matter, with one commenter writing: “Small or big, its still a donation.”



The discussion also drew comparisons with the cost-of-living pressures facing South Africans.

“I dont blame him, things are tough in this Ramaphosa economy..” another user commented.

Other social media users defended the President, questioning why the alleged amount had become a talking point in the first place.



“He didn’t use your tax money……relax,” one person wrote.

Another asked: “What’s fundamentally wrong with that? Aowa guys. Is giving at church status related?”

The contrasting reactions highlighted how even a brief moment during a political campaign can become a wider discussion about money, leadership and public expectations.



Cyril Ramaphosa steps up ANC campaign in Cape Town

The church visit formed part of a broader ANC campaign push across Cape Town ahead of the 4 November municipal elections.

Cyril Ramaphosa began his Western Cape campaign activities in Athlone with door-to-door visits before travelling to Khayelitsha for the church service. His programme also included further door-to-door campaigning and a public meeting at Monwabisi Park.

The ANC has been encouraging supporters in areas including Khayelitsha, Langa and Mfuleni to turn out in greater numbers on election day.



Voter turnout remains an important factor in the party’s efforts to challenge the DA in Cape Town, where the ANC has struggled to secure control of the metro.

World.title: Does Pitso Mosimane know something about Percy Tau that we don’t?
World.content:
Percy Tau has fuelled speculation about a possible return to football after sharing videos of himself training individually. Image: SAFA website

Percy Tau has fuelled speculation about a possible return to football after sharing videos of himself training individually, prompting a reaction from coach Pitso Mosimane.

The 32-year-old forward remains without a club after leaving Vietnamese side Nam Dinh at the end of last season following a single campaign with the team.

Renewed interest

Tau’s latest training videos have renewed interest in his future, with Mosimane among those seemingly eager to see the former Bafana Bafana star back on the pitch.



Commenting on Tau’s Instagram video, Mosimane wrote: “The return!!!”

The brief message appeared to signal his anticipation of a possible comeback for the attacker, although no club move or return date has been confirmed.

Searching for a club

Percy Tau has been keeping himself in shape while looking for his next opportunity after his departure from Nam Dinh.

The forward attracted attention on social media after posting footage of himself training alone in what appeared to be an open, rural setting. The exact location of the training session was not disclosed.

Despite previous reports linking him with a move to Kaizer Chiefs, no deal materialised, leaving Tau to continue his search for a new club.



His latest posts have sparked renewed discussion among supporters about where he could play next and whether he will return to South African football.

Will Percy Tau make a comeback soon?

Percy Tau’s future remains uncertain, with no official announcement regarding his next destination.

However, his decision to continue training suggests he is working to maintain his fitness and prepare for another opportunity.

The forward has previously represented clubs in South Africa and abroad, building a career that has included spells in European football and appearances for Bafana Bafana.

Mosimane’s reaction has added to the optimism surrounding Tau’s next chapter, although it does not confirm that a deal is imminent or that the coach is directly involved in securing one.

For now, Tau remains a free agent, and the football world will be watching to see where the experienced attacker lands next.

Which club would be the ideal fit for Percy Tau?

Let us know by clicking on the comment banner below …

World.title: Stormers lure Sharks lock back to the Cape
World.content:
Sharks lock Corné Rahl has signed with the Stormers and will join the squad at the end of the current season in July 2027. Image: Stormers website

Imposing Hollywoodbets Sharks lock Corné Rahl has signed with the Stormers and will join the squad at the end of the current season in July 2027.

The powerful 24-year-old hails from the Western Cape town of Montagu and was schooled at Oakdale, where he was one year ahead of his future team-mate Paul de Villiers.

At 2.03 metres tall and 122kg, Rahl brings physicality and intensity to everything he does on the field.



He will add to the depth in the club’s second-row stocks once he makes the move to Cape Town.

Perfect fit

Director of Rugby John Dobson said that Rahl is a perfect fit for what the squad requires.

“Corné is a player who has shown he can stand up to the best in the game and at 24 he has his best years ahead of him. It is important for our players to understand the region and what rugby means here and as a product of Oakdale he certainly fits the bill in that regard.

“He’s a big man who has shown an impressive work-rate and we are looking forward to seeing how he develops his game once he joins us here.

“With Salmaan Moerat and Ruben van Heerden both having moved to France at the end of last season, we wanted to invest in a player who has real long-term potential and we have that in Corné,” he said.

‘Excited’

Rahl said that he is excited to join the fold at the end of the season.



“Right now, I am obviously focused on performing for my current team, before I make the move to Cape Town next year. I am glad that my future is secure and with this announcement done I can focus on playing rugby.

“There is no doubt that the Stormers are building something special, and I am also looking forward to being a part of that once I join next season,” he said.

World.title: SAPS renewal tops agenda as Masemola returns to office
World.content:
PRETORIA - General Fannie Masemola is back at the helm of SAPS, but his return comes at a critical time for the police service, which faces allegations of corruption and criminal infiltration.

A security strategist says the national commissioner must now focus on accountability and rebuilding public trust.

Masemola says unity is paramount within SAPS.

“I return to office determined to unite the organisation, strengthen its institutional integrity and advance our constitutional responsibility to serve and protect the people of South Africa," he said.

"It’s not about an individual; it’s about the responsibility entrusted to the office for leadership continuity, which the organisation SAPS is central to our democracy in the country.”

Security strategist Andy Mashaile says Masemola faces a major challenge in rebuilding the police service and addressing questions of accountability within its ranks.

“He has the responsibility now to single out those who would want to take SAPS to the highest heights and those who do not wish to do so; he has to help them leave the organisation," he said.

As he returns to duty, Masemola says preparing for the upcoming local government elections is his first priority.

World.title: IEC partners with tech giants to fight disinformation
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) has partnered with major technology companies to combat fake news ahead of the 4 November Local Government Elections.

Google, Meta, Microsoft, TikTok and Moxii Africa are expected to sign a cooperation agreement aimed at tackling disinformation and protecting the integrity of the elections.

Google representative Sipho Mtombeni said that, as voters increasingly turn to online platforms to access election information, technology companies have a responsibility to help ensure they receive reliable, high-quality content.

READ | Residents must stay in touch after elections

He said this includes connecting users with trustworthy information while providing strong protection and security for election campaigns and officials.

Mtombeni also highlighted growing concerns about artificial intelligence-generated content.

He said Google was working to help users distinguish between authentic and AI-generated material through a tool called SynthID.

READ | IEC gets to ballot reprinting after Apex ruling on candidate list dispute

Meta representative Thabo Makenete said the company had several measures in place to protect election integrity, including transparency initiatives, efforts to combat misinformation and fact-checking partnerships.

“As the framework is voluntary, we still take it very seriously that we have to live up to the requirements of ensuring that the elections are safe, to ensure that people, when they engage on our platforms, they have to not spread misinformation,” Makenete said.

Moxii Africa director William Bird said threats to election integrity extended beyond misinformation, pointing to individuals, entities and groups he claimed were seeking to undermine democracy and the electoral process.

“And these are very serious things,” Bird said, commending the technology companies participating in the IEC’s cooperation framework to tackle disinformation and protect the integrity of the polls.

World.title: 92 suspected illegal miners arrested in Krugersdorp operation
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Police have arrested 92 suspected illegal miners and seized firearms, ammunition and explosives during an operation in West Village, Krugersdorp.

The operation was conducted on Monday by members of the South African Police Service (SAPS), the South African National Defence Force (SANDF) and the Department of Home Affairs as part of Operation Prosper/Karabo.

Police also confiscated equipment allegedly used in illegal mining, including phendukas and gas cylinders.

Operation Prosper/Karabo is a multidisciplinary law enforcement initiative targeting illegal mining, gangsterism and related criminal activities across Gauteng.

The operation is ongoing.

World.title: After Ethiopia fighting, new Tigray mayor vows elections in 6 months
World.content:
ADDIS ABABA - With rebels abandoning control of Ethiopia's northern Tigray state, a new government-appointed mayor of its capital told AFP on Monday they will hold elections within six months.

Tigrayan rebels, who have run the region for years, launched an offensive against the federal government last month, but were ultimately forced to retreat and lost control of the state.

The fighting raised fears of a regional war, as the rebels had the backing of neighbouring Eritrea, which deployed thousands of troops in Ethiopian territory. But they were also forced to retreat after being pounded by drone attacks.

Some residual clashes were still occurring around the town of Aksum, a spokesman for pro-government forces said.

On Friday, the Ethiopian government of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed established a new interim administration in Tigray, a region of around six million people, with a mandate to hold elections and re-house displaced people.

"Our role is to create the right conditions for elections by ensuring peace and stability across Tigray," Shishay Amare, the new mayor of state capital Mekelle, told AFP.

"I am confident that this will be done within six months, according to our plan," he added.

"We must also make sure humanitarian aid reaches people in need, help people recover from the psychological effects of the conflict, restart economic activities and reopen markets," Shishay said.

Rebel-controlled Tigray did not take part in the nationwide parliamentary elections in June, which saw Abiy and his Prosperity Party returned to power with an overwhelming victory, facing minimal opposition.

Around a million people remain displaced from the last civil war in northern Ethiopia of 2020-2022, which killed an estimated 600,000 people, according to African Union estimates.

The new Mekelle mayor said the sensitive issue of Western Tigray -- which is claimed by both Tigray and neighbouring Amhara state -- would be deferred to a later date.

"Our main task is to help displaced people return with their dignity respected. Questions about territorial integrity will be resolved through constitutional processes," Shishay said.

World.title: Microsoft exits data centre deal in blow to UK AI ambitions
World.content:
NEW YORK - Microsoft confirmed on Monday that it has pulled out of a UK AI data centre deal with British start-up Nscale, in a blow to the country's artificial intelligence ambitions.

The US technology giant agreed last year to lease computing capacity from AI infrastructure provider Nscale, which is backed by chip titan Nvidia, at a planned data centre in Loughton, northeast of London.

A Microsoft spokesperson said "this decision relates to a single site", adding the company remains "committed to our partnership with Nscale".

The deal was announced alongside a flurry of multi-billion-dollar investments from US tech giants during President Donald Trump's state visit to the UK last year, which were touted as helping turn Britain into an AI superpower.

Former Prime Minister Keir Starmer cited the Loughton site as the "largest UK sovereign AI data centre".

But some data centre projects have struggled to get off the ground due to concerns over high electricity prices and lengthy waiting times to connect to Britain's power grid.

"We remain committed to both the Loughton project and the UK and we are exploring alternative power sources for the site, in addition to other expansion sites in the UK," an Nscale spokesperson said Monday.

"Our relationship with Microsoft remains strong and long-term, and this unfortunate London-wide grid issue has no impact on our other contracts," they added.

UK media reported that power grid officials had told Nscale that the site would not have access to power until the 2030s.

-- Wall Street IPO --

It comes as Nscale gears up for an initial public offering on the New York Stock Exchange, reportedly targeting a valuation of up to $35 billion.

In its IPO filing, Nscale noted that "a substantial portion of our committed revenue is driven by a limited number of customers with large contracts", namely Microsoft and US AI giant Anthropic.

The Loughton deal accounted for only a small portion of Microsoft's agreements with Nscale, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Earlier this year, ChatGPT maker OpenAI withdrew from a partnership with Nscale and Nvidia to establish a UK version of Stargate -- a large-scale AI infrastructure initiative.

OpenAI blamed high energy costs and regulatory uncertainty for shelving the project, according to British media.

Meeting the electricity demands of large new data centres often requires major infrastructure upgrades, adding to connection delays.

UK Power Networks, which does not disclose information about individual connections, told AFP on Monday that "many data centres, whilst they can connect to our distribution network, are awaiting works on the national transmission network, which we do not own".

World.title: England women's coach Wiegman signs two-year contract extension
World.content:
LONDON - England women's head coach Sarina Wiegman has signed a two-year contract extension taking her through until the end of the 2029 women's European Championship, the Football Association announced Monday.

Wiegman has led England to tournament triumphs at both the 2022 and 2025 Euros, as well as a first World Cup final in 2023, since taking charge in September 2021.

The 56-year-old Dutchwoman has reached five successive major tournament finals, also winning Euro 2017 with her native Netherlands.

"I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football," Wiegman said Monday.

England, beaten by Spain in the 2023 World Cup final in Australia, will face Ukraine over a two-legged play-off in November and December for a place in next year's tournament in Brazil.

"Of course, anyone who knows me will understand that my main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come," Wiegman added.

"We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year."

Wiegman's new deal will also encompass the 2027 Nations League, which serves as a qualifying tournament for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

She first agreed a contract extension in January 2024.

World.title: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff shot at in Mumbai, three suspects held: police
World.content:
MUMBAI - Indian actor Tiger Shroff was shot at in Mumbai on Sunday, police said, adding that three suspects have been detained.

Shooters opened fire at the 36-year-old actor as he was leaving a private event in the city's upscale Juhu area on Sunday evening, according to Police official Mohit Garg.

Aside from being India's financial capital, Mumbai is also the heart of Bollywood, the country's Hindi-language film industry.

"Tiger Shroff is safe and Mumbai police has deployed different teams to investigate further," Garg told reporters.

Two people were injured in the incident, including the actor's driver, though Shroff did not sustain gunshot wounds, police said.

Three suspects have been rounded up in Rajasthan, another Indian state.

"Preliminary questioning revealed that two of them have one case each against them, one related to theft and the other under the Arms Act," police official Tejaswani Gautam told reporters.

Police have yet to establish a motive for the shooting.

Shroff is known for action films including the "Baaghi" franchise and "War".

World.title: WATCH | Mbeki testifies before TRC cases inquiry
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Former president Thabo Mbeki is expected to testify before the TRC cases inquiry on Monday as it continues its investigation into alleged political interference in the prosecution of apartheid-era crimes.

Former president Jacob Zuma’s testimony has been postponed to a date yet to be confirmed due to ill health. He was scheduled to testify before the inquiry on 22 October.

Both former presidents previously attempted, unsuccessfully, to have inquiry chairperson Sisi Khampepe recuse herself from the proceedings.

The inquiry is investigating allegations that political interference obstructed the prosecution of crimes committed during apartheid.

World.title: Inside Paul Makenzie's fasting regime and 'last days' indoctrination
World.content:
Workers dig the ground to exume bodies as Kenya's Interior Minister Kithure Kindiki visits the mass-grave site in Shakahola, outside the coastal town of Malindi, on April 25, 2023. [AFP]

Controversial preacher Paul Makenzi is this afternoon appearing before Justice Kavedza Mochache as she delivers her verdict over the deadly fast in Shakahola forest.

Justice Kavedza, in her highlights, said the court had established that Makenzi was the overall head of what she termed the ‘fasting regime’, who determined how followers would undertake deadly fasts.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
