World.title: Iraq, World Bank discuss financing strategic projects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari and World Bank Group Vice President for the Middle East and North Africa Ousmane Dione discussed on Thursday financing strategic projects and support for economic reforms in Iraq.

The meeting took place on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, held in Bangkok, Thailand, according to a statement released by the Finance Ministry.

Sari stressed the World Bank’s role in Iraq’s economic and financial transformation. He outlined the country’s desire to use the World Bank’s expertise and financial contributions to carry out significant projects in the energy, education, transportation, and digital transformation sectors.

The step aims to promote sustainable development and improve the efficiency of public services in Iraq, according to Sari.

Dione praised the collaboration with the Iraqi Finance Ministry, indicating that it has efficiently arranged its operational and communication mechanisms with the World Bank.

The World Bank official highlighted that the efforts of the Iraqi government pave the way for additional initiatives to support the country’s economic and financial goals in the upcoming period.

Sari reaffirmed last week Iraq’s commitment to continuing economic and financial reforms, diversifying revenue sources, and strengthening the role of the private sector.

According to Sari, these measures aim to bolster economic stability and enhance the country’s capacity to deal with regional challenges.

Sari noted that the government is addressing the economic consequences of the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz by reprioritizing expenditures, increasing non-oil revenues, and maintaining the state’s essential obligations while pursuing structural reforms.

“Iraq Vision 2050” represents a strategic plan for reducing dependency on oil, broadening production, empowering the private sector, and achieving inclusive and sustainable economic growth, according to Sari.

The minister noted that the reform package includes enhancing public financial management, automating customs and tax operations, boosting the business and investment climate, upgrading the banking sector, and increasing electronic payment systems.

According to Sari, the partnership with the IMF and the World Bank Group supports the economic and financial reform program.

World.title: Chinese oilfield service firm markets Iraq’s oil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – China-based Anton Oilfield Services Group has sold its first Iraqi crude oil shipment as part of a new supply deal with the State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO).

According to Reuters, the unique arrangement with one of a few Chinese independent oil corporations expanding their activities in Iraq enables Baghdad to access cash to pay service suppliers.

Iraq is attempting to bolster oil exports impacted by the military conflict in the Middle East. In the past few months, greater discounts have enticed traders and refiners, leading to a resurgence in its oil shipments.

The Chinese firm said in a statement on Saturday that the agreement intends to improve Basra Oil Company’s (BOC) crude oil sales and cash flow, provide channels for engineering and services, and expedite payment collection for Anton and partners.

An official in the oil sector indicated that Anton struck an agreement with SOMO to market undetermined amounts of Iraqi crude oil, mostly from the Majnoon oilfield managed by BOC.

In late September, Anton marketed one million barrels of Basra Heavy crude to a trading company.

Anton mentioned that the agreement with SOMO allows it to sell oil from the Dhufriya oilfield in eastern Iraq, where it received a license in 2024 to develop the field.

World.title: Iraq inaugurates first satellite ground station
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad inaugurated on Sunday Iraq’s first satellite ground station in Baghdad, a step aiming to bolster digital sovereignty and develop the country’s telecommunications infrastructure.

In a speech he delivered during the inauguration ceremony, Sanad said that Iraq’s acquisition of a satellite would be impossible without a ground station.

The new facility will serve as a cornerstone for the country’s upcoming national space program, with future expansions planned to establish additional ground stations across other Iraqi provinces depending on population density and administrative assessment.

The station also acts as a complete technological hub that includes a satellite communication gateway, a localized data center, and an internet exchange point.

Developed in partnership with the technology group Commercis, the station links incoming satellite communications directly into Iraq’s expanding domestic fiber-optic terrestrial network.

Iraq previously relied on international infrastructure located outside its borders to route satellite traffic. The government is now actively urging ministries, private companies, and security agencies to migrate their traffic to this local gateway to secure sensitive data.

The station is part of a broader economic vision to transform Iraq into a regional data corridor. By leveraging its geographic location, Iraq aims to serve as a high-speed data transit bridge connecting networks across Asia, Africa, and Europe.

The station provides high-speed enterprise internet, secure government communications, live television feeds, and commercial satellite broadcasting.

World.title: Competing narratives emerge over blast at PMF security compound in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Two days after a powerful blast ripped through a Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) security headquarters in eastern Baghdad, an investigative report published by Al Mada newspaper and monithas revealed sharp contradictions surrounding the incident, presenting four competing narratives ranging from a targeted foreign strike to sabotage and munitions mismanagement.

The explosion struck at approximately 6:00 PM on Saturday, October 17, 2026, inside a facility operated by the PMF Security Directorate located along Sadr Al-Qanat near the Saad Al-Watri Hospital.

While the PMF’s official communique attributed the incident to an internal fire that detonated obsolete, deteriorated munitions—resulting in minor injuries to five personnel—field sources cited by Al Mada report over twenty injuries among PMF security personnel and unidentified associates. Strict security cordons accompanied the medical evacuation via PMF ambulances, fueling speculation regarding the potential presence of Iranian technical personnel at the site.

The circumstances have ignited debate over the operational nature of the facility. As an intelligence and security installation, the complex is not designated to warehouse expired ordnance. Security sources cited in the report claimed that newly arrived military consignments from Iran had been transferred into the depot just a week prior to the detonation.

Preliminary forensic findings referenced in the investigation point to the possibility of an incoming projectile initiating the primary blast, though information sharing on the file remains tightly restricted by the PMF Chief of Staff’s office while a specialized investigative committee established by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi conducts its inquiry.

Four Competing Accounts

World.title: Iraq opens public university admissions for international schools’ graduates
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research announced on Monday, October 19, 2026, that the electronic admissions portal for international school graduates applying to public universities will open within the coming days for the 2026–2027 academic year.

According to a ministerial press release obtained by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), admissions processing will be managed through the centralized digital application platform Qaddim.

Eligible candidates graduating from accredited international curricula within Iraq will access the admissions system using their standardized examination sequence number and confidential verification credentials issued directly by their respective school administrations.

The ministry advised prospective students and guardians to monitor its official web portal and recognized digital channels for forthcoming regulatory guidelines, grade-weighting criteria, and precise application submission schedules.

The upcoming portal launch represents an institutional mechanism to integrate international school diploma holders into national university admissions channels alongside graduates of the standard ministerial secondary baccalaureate examinations.

World.title: US dollar edges up to 169,500 IQD in Baghdad and provincial exchanges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged upward across parallel retail and wholesale counters in Baghdad and major commercial hubs on Monday, October 19, 2026.

The capital recorded an increase of 500 dinars per $100 compared to prior trading sessions, while regional desks in Erbil and Basra registered fractional gains of 50 dinars per $100.

In Baghdad, licensed exchange shops and retail desks posted dollar cash selling quotes at 169,500 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 168,500 dinars, reflecting persistent upward pressure in parallel liquidity channels.

In Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, counters listed selling rates at 168,550 dinars per $100 with purchase transactions accepted at 168,000 dinars. Across the southern port province of Basra, foreign exchange desks closed the morning session at a selling price of 168,750 dinars per $100 against buying offers of 168,250 dinars.

The current parallel figures sustain a pronounced gap above the official statutory cash rate mandated by the Central Bank of Iraq, which remains benchmarked at 152,000 dinars per $100.

This continuous premium highlights elevated demand for physical banknotes among local commercial importers navigating foreign trade settlements outside the central electronic clearance window.

World.title: KRG official: Iraq needs 8 billion SCFD of gas for 24-hour electricity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq requires approximately eight billion standard cubic feet per day (scfd) of natural gas to achieve uninterrupted, 24-hour national electricity generation, according to Ahmed Mufti, Deputy Minister of Natural Resources in the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG).

In an analytical op-ed reviewed by the Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Sunday, October 18, 2026, Mufti highlighted that structural inefficiencies and energy waste cost the federal treasury roughly $10 billion annually, urging Baghdad and Erbil to launch a specialized gas licensing round and redirect industrial subsidies toward core infrastructure and upstream extraction.

The KRG energy official pointed out that state-funded fuel subsidies for heavy industries—predominantly cement and steel plants—absorb nearly $8 billion annually. While commending the federal cabinet’s revised pricing mechanism for heavy fuel oil (black oil), which reduced subsidies to sell fuel to industrial plants at $400 per ton against an international benchmark of $650, Mufti emphasized that realized fiscal savings should be channeled directly into natural gas transmission networks.

Transitioning heavy industry clusters, such as those in Sulaymaniyah’s Bazian district consuming 3,000 tons of fuel oil daily, to natural gas would significantly lower production costs, curb emissions, and free up heavy crude volumes for high-value export markets.

Mufti outlined substantial upstream potential across key underdeveloped non-associated gas assets, including Akkas in Anbar and Mansuriya and Khashm Al-Ahmar in Diyala, calling for an investment licensing round backed by robust legal, security, and sovereign payment guarantees.

Highlighting the Kurdistan Region’s foreign-investment model, he noted that output from the Khor Mor gas field surged from 350 million scfd in 2020 to 750 million scfd today, pushing aggregate regional gas production close to one billion scfd. Further development of adjacent fields—such as Chamchamal, Kurdamir, and Topkhana—could elevate regional production to between two and three billion scfd.

To bridge supply shortages, Mufti proposed an integrated “gas-to-power” framework, where gas-fired generation in the north feeds directly into the federal transmission grid, cementing economic alignment between Baghdad and Erbil.

He concluded with strategic recommendations, including the establishment of a joint federal-regional security command to protect critical energy infrastructure, the swift settlement of delayed payments to international oil and gas operators to sustain drilling campaigns, and the formal redesignation of Iraq’s Ministry of Oil as the “Ministry of Oil and Gas” to reflect the fuel’s central role in future industrial strategy.

World.title: Asian stocks start week on back foot, tracking tech-led Wall St losses
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks mostly fell Monday as traders tracked a tech-heavy selloff on Wall Street that was fuelled by growing worries over the AI investment boom.

Chipmakers and other firms linked to artificial intelligence were once again under pressure owing to concerns about surging inflation, rising costs and questions about when the vast sums pumped into the sector in recent years would see a return.

Last week saw wild swings that ended on a largely positive note on Friday, though investors remain on edge heading into a crucial earnings season that sees tech titans Tesla and Meta report this week.

Markets have also been spooked by concerns about “neocloud” firm CoreWeave’s huge debt pile.

The company’s stock price has tanked around 30 percent this month as yields on some of its bonds soared, reflecting heightened angst over its future.

Reassuring comments from Nvidia chief Jensen Huang on CoreWeave’s financial health provided some support to Asia on Friday but that optimism faded as the new week started.

Investors are also looking to next week’s Federal Reserve interest rate decision, with bets on a second successive hike jumping after forecast-topping US inflation data. Higher rates hurt tech firms as many rely on borrowing to fund their huge investments.

All three main indexes on Wall Street ended sharply lower, with the Nasdaq more than two percent down, dragged by giants including Microsoft, Nvidia, AMD and Amazon.

“The US equity sell-off reflected a reassessment of the economics underpinning the AI investment boom rather than a simple downgrade to end-demand,” said National Australia Bank’s Rodrigo Catril.

“Investors are increasingly questioning whether future revenue can justify the capital and financing required for data centers, chips and power infrastructure.”

And the selling rolled over into Asia, where Tokyo was pulled down by tech investment titan SoftBank as well as Advantest and Tokyo Electron.

Seoul followed suit owing to more losses for chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung.

There were also losses in Taipei, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore and Wellington. Hong Kong was closed for a holiday.

There was little immediate reaction to data showing China’s economy grew 4.5 percent in the third quarter, slightly better than forecast in an AFP survey.

Oil prices slipped but both main contracts held above $100 after soaring more than three percent Friday following a big drop in US commercial inventories.

The latest dip came on the back of signs that supplies continue to leave the Middle East despite Iran’s chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz and ongoing attacks by Yemen’s Houthis on key Saudi Arabian crude sites.

On currency markets the euro fell on concerns about the French economy as the country is hit by widespread protests, with President Emmanuel Macron slamming the “unbridled” violence that erupted in cost-of-living demonstrations.

World.content:

He will also flag off a motorcycle rally of about 90 police riders from Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi)Central Armed Police Forces (CRPF, CISF, BSF, SSB, ITBP and NSG) and some Central Police Organisations (RPF, NDRF and NIA). In recognition of the sacrifices made by police personnel and their paramount role in preserving national security and integrity, the Prime Minister dedicated the National Police Memorial (NPM), Chanakyapuri, New Delhi to the nation on Police Commemoration Day 2018.





On October 21, an event will be organised at the National Police Memorial, New Delhi, where a joint parade of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Delhi Police would be held. Why is India witnessing anti-EC protests

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: More than 400 Indian-origin students, researchers and alumni from universities in 27 countries have issued a joint statement condemning the ongoing protests against the Election Commission of India (ECI), describing them as a âplan to sow seeds of doubt in Indiaâs democracyâ.Titled âSpare India from Anarchyâ, the statement criticises the protests against the poll body."An unconscionable and devious plan of sowing seeds of doubt in Indian democracy has been hatched by weaponising sub judice matters, which is then amplified on the streets by leaning on anarchist forces, which have historically and philosophically never believed in constitutional form of governance. All in the name of saving democracy," the statement said."We remain amazed at the irony of all. But more importantly, as informed people who have stakes in the future of this country and travel the world identifying as 'Indians,' we are deeply anguished at this state of affairs," it added.The signatories highlighted the resilience of Indian democracy and the role of constitutional institutions, stating: "In the seven decades since independence, Indian democracy has proved its resilience repeatedly.Institutions have flourished, checks and balances have functioned admirably, and peaceful transition of power has remained an enduring hallmark."They lamented that "a frenzy of election denial, relentless questioning of constitutional institutions, and a preference for 'street over Sansad'" had gripped certain quarters."Unfavourable election outcomes have led to questions of procedural integrity. Adverse judgements have provoked unfortunate commentary on judicial independence. Even the most apolitical institution in the country -- the armed forces -- has been gratuitously and unjustly entangled in partisan discourse," the statement read.While acknowledging that dissent was essential to democracy, the signatories said they refused to remain "silent spectators to the subversion of democratic apparatus in its guise".They urged social and political forces to resolve differences through "debate, discussion, dialogue and dissent" within constitutional institutions.The signatories are based in or have studied at universities across 27 countries, including the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, Germany, France, Japan and Singapore.Their academic affiliations include the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, the universities of Oxford and Cambridge, Harvard University, Stanford University and the London School of Economics, among others. The statement clarified that these affiliations did not imply endorsement by the respective universities.The protests come amid opposition partiesâ allegations of irregularities in elections and questions over the integrity of electoral processes.Last month, The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge, including those related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The report triggered protests by opposition parties and citizensâ groups in several parts of the country, particularly in Delhi, with demonstrators demanding the resignation or removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Kumar, who was appointed an election commissioner in 2024 and became CEC in 2025, has repeatedly faced opposition allegations of electoral irregularities and bias in favour of the ruling BJP.

World.title: Manipur on boil again: 3 killed by militants; locals place bodies in front of CM's house
World.content:
Imphal: Police fire tear gas shells to disperse irate locals who placed the bodies of two victims, allegedly killed in an ambush by armed miscreants at Sunurok Uyok in Imphal East district, in front of the Chief Minister's bungalow, in Imphal. (PTI Photo)

Firewood collectors ambushed in the hills

Bodies placed outside CM's residence

Protests spread, markets and shops shut

Manipur grappling with violence since 2023

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

(With inputs from agencies)

NEW DELHI: Three people were killed and three others injured after suspected militants ambushed firewood collectors along the Imphal East-Kangpokpi district border in Manipur on Monday.The attack triggered protests in Imphal, where locals placed two of the victims' bodies outside Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh's residence.The attack took place around 7am in Khongbal Sunurok Uyok in Kangpokpi district, near Nongshum village in Imphal East. Three people remained missing after the incident, officials said. The protests also led to road blockades and the closure of markets and shops across Imphal.The victims were among 16 people who had gone to the hills near their village to collect firewood when suspected militants opened fire on them, officials said.The deceased were identified as Arubam Ronil, 35, Lairenlakpam Inaobi, 51, and Kshetrimayum Sushil, 32. Ronil and Inaobi died on the spot, while Sushil succumbed to his injuries at a private hospital in Imphal, an official said.The injured were identified as N Suraj, 19, Meisnam Somendro, 53, and K Bosan, 45.They were undergoing treatment. Three people were still unaccounted for, news agency PTI reported, citing officials.An injured survivor, who was taken to a private hospital in Imphal, said, "While we were loading the firewood, we were suddenly fired upon."Angry locals brought two of the deceased's bodies to Imphal and placed them outside the main gate of the chief minister's residence in Babupara to protest the continuing violence in the state.Police fired several rounds of tear gas shells to disperse the protesters. The bodies were subsequently taken to the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences (JNIMS).Security was tightened around the chief minister's bungalow and along the routes leading to it.Following the demonstration, Khemchand Singh visited the injured people receiving treatment at a private hospital in Imphal but did not respond to media queries.The attack triggered demonstrations at several locations in the state capital. Protesters blocked a road at Khurai Lamlong, while a group of women staged a demonstration at Ema Keithel market.Markets and shops across Imphal shut following the incident, as anger grew over the latest attack.The attack on firewood collectors came amid other incidents of violence reported in Manipur over the weekend.In a separate incident, at least 15 houses belonging to the Kuki community were torched in Chassad village in Kamjong district late on Saturday night, officials said on Sunday. Suspected militants allegedly set the houses on fire, forcing several civilians to flee to forest areas and a nearby Army camp.PTI reported that a Kuki civilian was killed and four others sustained bullet injuries when suspected militants attacked the village earlier on Sunday.Deputy chief minister Nemcha Kipgen condemned the violence in Chassad, expressed grief over the death and concern for the injured village leaders and displaced families. She described the burning of houses as an intolerable crime and said she had directed the district administration, state police and security forces to remain vigilant round the clock, protect civilians and their property, and ensure those responsible were brought to justice.Police said a joint team of the Assam Rifles, Border Security Force and Kamjong Police had been deployed in the affected area to bring the situation under control.In another separate incident at Kamjong district headquarters on Saturday night, three Tangkhul Naga civilians sustained bullet injuries when rival armed groups belonging to another community attacked the village.Manipur has been grappling with prolonged violence since May 2023. The latest attack on firewood collectors and the protests that followed came against the backdrop of fresh incidents involving arson, civilian deaths and gunshot injuries in other parts of the state.

World.title: 'O Captain, My Captain': Should Congress make room for Amarinder Singh again?
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Can a party install a new captain, retain the old team and still leave the door open for a former captain who quit the dressing room five years ago? With the leadership chanting 'O Captain! My Captain!' the Punjab Congress seems to be attempting to navigate that question precisely ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.

With

at the helm, Raja Warring and Charanjit Singh Channi 'promised' an active role in the campaign;

has also left the door open to

's possible return. Can Congress accommodate its old captain without unsettling the new captain and the team?

Congress general secretary Sachin Pilot, the party's Punjab in-charge, on October 15 offered a line that will keep speculation alive: "Politics mein 'kuch bhi ho sakta hai' (anything is possible in politics)."

Asked about the possibility of former Punjab chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh returning to Congress, Pilot praised him as a leader who had served Punjab "well" and was "a man of a very tall stature". He clarified, however, that he had not spoken to Captain Amarinder about his political plans.

"I've not spoken to him personally about what his future plans are about joining or leaving any party," Pilot told PTI Videos.





Amarinder Singh on his relationship with Congress leadership.

The remark came less than a fortnight after Congress appointed former India hockey captain Pargat Singh as Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) president, replacing Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on October 2. It also followed Amarinder's public criticism of the BJP, the party he joined in 2022, over its handling of Punjab.

So, is Congress merely acknowledging political speculation, or could the old captain's name return to the party's calculations? And if he does return, where would he fit in a state unit that has just changed leadership and is yet to name a CM face?

The 'Uncle Amarinder' connection

The latest speculation began with an unexpected public greeting.

On August 6, during an Instagram 'Ask Me Anything' session with students, leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi was asked to name his favourite BJP politician.

"Captain Amarinder Singh, definitely. I get along with him, he's cool and he is an expert on military history, so I like him quite a lot," Rahul Gandhi said, before adding: "Hello, Uncle Amarinder!"

The former CM responded that his personal relationship with the Gandhi family would remain, but his political commitment was to the BJP.

In a September interview with The Tribune, he said he remained fond of Rahul, Priyanka and Sonia Gandhi, while distinguishing personal relationships from politics.

"My personal relationship with the Gandhis will always be there, but my political commitment is to the BJP," he said.

"If tomorrow I tell Rahul, Priyanka or Sonia personally that I'll be there for them no matter what, I mean it and I'm happy to help," he added.

The indirect exchange was notable because Amarinder Singh's departure from Congress in September 2021 followed a bitter confrontation with the party's state leadership. "When you've been with somebody for fifty years, they remain your party. I never asked to leave them; they asked me to leave," Captain Amarinder Singh said recently.

Amarinder's BJP discontent

The former chief minister's recent criticism of the BJP has provided the immediate backdrop to the comeback speculation.

In an interview published by The Tribune on September 25, Amarinder said the BJP had not consulted him on Punjab politics or policy despite his long experience in the state.

"I haven't had a single meeting on Punjab policy or politics with them in the last five years," he said.

He was more direct about his decision to join the party: "I have gained nothing by joining BJP."

The political career of Captain Amarinder Singh.

Amarinder also argued that the BJP did not adequately understand Punjab and should consult leaders familiar with the state's political and social realities.

He advocated an alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal, pointing to the BJP's historical position as the junior partner in that relationship.

In the same interview, he described himself as going through "difficult times", without elaborating.

Yet he has also made clear that dissatisfaction does not automatically mean departure. Amarinder Singh said it was his duty to tell the BJP what he thought about Punjab and that criticising the party's approach did not mean he was quitting.

From a 77-seat victory to a bitter exit

Captain Amarinder Singh's record in Congress spans decades, including two terms as Punjab CM, from 2002 to 2007 and from 2017 to 2021.

In the 2017 assembly election, Congress won 77 of Punjab's 117 seats under his leadership, returning to power after a decade. But the relationship between Amarinder Singh and the state leadership deteriorated, particularly amid his prolonged confrontation with Navjot Singh Sidhu.

Sidhu became Punjab Congress president in July 2021. The conflict intensified over leadership and the government's handling of election promises. On September 18, 2021, Amarinder resigned as chief minister after the Congress high command called a meeting of the party's legislators to discuss leadership.

Sachin Pilot kept the door open to Amarinder Singh's return to the Congress.

He subsequently left Congress and launched the Punjab Lok Congress (PLC). In the 2022 assembly election, the PLC allied with the BJP, but the alliance failed to win a seat for Amarinder Singh's party.

AAP swept the election with 92 seats, while Congress was reduced to 18.

Amarinder joined the BJP in September 2022, and his PLC was merged with it.

The electoral record provides the context for the renewed speculation, but it does not establish that bringing Amarinder back would reverse Congress's fortunes. The party's 2022 defeat followed a wider political shift in Punjab, including AAP's rise and Congress's internal divisions.

Pargat Singh's leadership test

Meanwhile, Pargat Singh's appointment has put a new leader at the head of a state unit that has repeatedly struggled with factional disputes. A former India hockey captain and three-time MLA from Jalandhar Cantonment, he was associated with Sidhu during the 2021 confrontation with Amarinder Singh and had publicly questioned the previous government's delivery on election promises.

Pilot called Pargat a "unifying captain", saying the new president has reached out to state leaders and received public support.

He has also invoked the team metaphor to describe Congress's approach to the election.

"You are one captain who's got a fantastic team, and the captain is only as strong as his team," Pilot said he had told Pargat. His appointment, replacing Warring as state chief, was particularly important in the backdrop of an internal tussle between Warring and Channi camps.

Punjab Congress has spent months grappling with a bitter power struggle between the camps of state chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring and former CM Charanjit Singh Channi.

The feud spilled into public view through rival sloganeering, poster wars, clashes at party events and boycotts during visits by then state in-charge Bhupesh Baghel. The high command's July compromise, retaining Warring while appointing Channi to head the campaign committee, failed to end the friction.

After Sachin Pilot replaced Baghel as Punjab in-charge in September, Warring eventually resigned on October 2, and Pargat Singh was appointed the new state chief.

With the Congress leadership now sending the open-door signal to Captain Amarinder, the question is how Pargat's team would accommodate a strong-headed former CM with a history in the party.

Moreover, the issue is not limited to Amarinder Singh. In the upcoming months, Congress must also manage the transition from Warring, who led the state unit from April 2022 until October 2026.

No CM face, but several leadership questions

Congress has also decided against projecting a CM face for the 2027 Punjab election.

Pilot said the party would fight as a team and decide who should lead the state after securing the mandate, following consultations with workers, leaders and MLAs.

"We are fighting together as a team. Let the team win. And then we'll decide who gets to do what job," he said.

In June, Amarinder Singh shared that Rahul Gandhi wished him on his birthday.

The party has several experienced leaders, including Partap Singh Bajwa, Sukhjinder Randhawa, Charanjit Singh Channi and Warring. Pargat's appointment adds a new organisational chief to that mix, while the question of Amarinder's possible return remains unconfirmed.

For the high command, the practical issue would be defining the role of each leader without undermining the other.

What could Captain Amarinder's return mean

Amarinder Singh's long tenure in Punjab politics, his experience as CM and his association with national security and border-state issues are part of his public political profile. A return could give Congress another experienced voice in its campaign, while his criticism of the BJP could offer a new line of political debate.

The Congress may gain from his name, polularity and political history but it is unlikely that he would have any active role owing to his age.

But the political costs would depend on the terms of any return. His 2021 exit followed a major leadership confrontation, and Pargat was part of the state leadership aligned with Sidhu during that period. Reconciliation would therefore involve not just Amarinder Singh and the Gandhi family, but a state unit whose leadership has changed since he left.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It would also raise questions about the position of leaders who remained with Congress through the subsequent elections and organisational changes. Warring's emphasis on youth representation, Pargat's task of consolidating the state unit and Pilot's insistence on collective leadership all point to issues that would need to be addressed.

For now, there is no confirmed proposal to bring Captain Amarinder back, no announced role for him and no indication that talks have taken place or are under way.

Pilot's "anything is possible" may keep the question open, but the party's immediate task remains to get the current team working together before Punjab votes in 2027.

World.title: Polish PM Donald Tusk to visit India from October 21 to 23, hold talks with PM Modi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk will visit India from October 21 to 23 at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with the two leaders set to review bilateral ties and discuss regional and global issues of mutual interest, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Monday.

Tusk will be accompanied by Andrzej DomaÅski, Poland's minister of finance and economy, along with a large business delegation, according to an official statement issued by the government.

During the visit, Tusk will hold bilateral talks with PM Modi in New Delhi on October 22. The discussions will cover the full range of India-Poland relations, which were elevated to a Strategic Partnership during PM Modi's visit to Poland in August 2024.

The two leaders will also exchange views on regional and global developments of mutual interest, the MEA said.

Business forums planned in Delhi and Bengaluru

Tusk will also travel to Bengaluru, where he is scheduled to meet business stakeholders, including representatives from the information technology and space sectors.

An India-Poland Business Forum will be held in New Delhi on October 22 and in Bengaluru on October 23.

The visit is expected to advance cooperation across several areas, including trade and investment, defence, emerging technologies, renewable energy, education, culture and people-to-people ties.





"The visit will provide the opportunity to further strengthen the India-Poland Strategic Partnership and advance cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including trade and investment, defence, emerging technologies, renewable energy, education, culture and people-to-people ties," the MEA said in its statement.

The visit will also provide an opportunity to deepen the strategic partnership between India and the European Union, it added.

Second India visit as Polish prime minister

This will be Tusk's second visit to India in his capacity as Poland's prime minister. His first visit in the role took place in 2010, during his earlier tenure. He also visited New Delhi in 2017 for the India-EU Summit as president of the European Council.

The upcoming visit follows the elevation of India-Poland relations to a Strategic Partnership in August 2024, when PM Modi travelled to Warsaw. The visit marked the first trip by an Indian prime minister to Poland in 45 years.

During that visit, the two countries adopted a comprehensive five-year action plan covering areas such as trade and investment, defence, energy, green technologies, agriculture and infrastructure.

Defence and industrial cooperation on agenda

Ahead of Tusk's visit, Polish finance and economy minister Andrzej DomaÅski outlined plans to expand trade and defence cooperation with India.

Speaking to news agency ANI on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, earlier this month, DomaÅski said Poland wanted to strengthen industrial partnerships and increase defence exports to India.

"We want to develop a strong defence industry. To do this, we would certainly like to maintain good trade relations in defence products with trusted partners like India. Therefore, it is no surprise that we would also like to increase the export of our defence products to India. During the visit, we will bring Polish defence companies to India," DomaÅski said.

The minister's remarks came after his meeting with Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal.

The upcoming visit will provide an opportunity for the two countries to discuss cooperation in defence and other strategic sectors alongside their existing economic and diplomatic engagement.

World.title: 'OIC being misused by Pakistan': India rejects 'malicious' remarks on J&K, flags credibility of agency
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Monday rejected remarks made during the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) Council of foreign ministers' meeting on

, saying the organisation had no locus standi to comment on matters that were strictly internal to India.

In a statement, the ministry said the references to India during the OIC meeting were malicious, biased and false, and had been orchestrated by

.

"We categorically reject the anti-India references in the resolutions of the OIC Council of foreign ministers' meeting held in Baghdad on October 17-18, 2026. The references to India are malicious, biased, and false, and have been orchestrated by Pakistan. We are disappointed that the OIC has once again allowed itself to be misused by Pakistan for its bigoted agenda," the MEA said.

"As we have said in the past, the OIC has no locus standi whatsoever to comment on matters that are strictly internal to India. The Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh are integral and inalienable parts of India. Politically motivated propaganda can never alter this reality. Over the past years since the abrogation of Art 370, Jammu & Kashmir has seen significant economic growth and benefits accruing directly to its people through infrastructure development, tourism and connectivity.





This is in stark contrast to the situation in PoJK, where Pakistan has unleashed violence, repression and brutality on civilian protesters, killing scores of them, including women and children. No amount of media blackout has been able to hide these grave violations of human rights," it added.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The MEA further said that the only issues related to Jammu and Kashmir that remained to be addressed were Pakistan vacating areas under its "illegal and forcible occupation" and ceasing its continued support for cross-border terrorism.

"Other fabricated and hostile references against India in the OIC resolutions, including insinuations related to Islamophobia, are nothing but a desperate attempt by Pakistan to divert international attention from its own appalling record of minority persecution and sectarian violence, apart from governance failure and political instability," it said.

"The OIC's repeated endorsement of patently malicious propaganda and narratives peddled by Pakistan raises serious questions about its credibility and integrity. We hope its members would do better and reform this organisation," it added.

World.title: PSG-Barcelona match in Champions League to go ahead amid shock over France’s violent unrest
World.content:
The showpiece Champions League match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona will go ahead as planned on Tuesday in the French capital city, the French Interior minister confirmed, despite a weekend of protests marred by violence and looting across the country.

Also read | France protest: Prime Minister calls for localised curfews in cities to curb rioting, looting

Many French citizens have been left shocked by the images of violence that have drawn worldwide attention and highlighted the country's tense social climate. On Monday, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said he has instructed prefects to impose “very limited” and “localized” curfews in cities to prevent more rioting and looting.

The violence targeted city halls, other public buildings and hundreds of businesses across the country, leading to more than 2,000 arrests.

Tuesday's (October 20, 2026) match between PSG and Barcelona at the Parc des Princes will require a robust security deployment, with police forces already strained following weeks of student protests. In May, Paris police detained dozens of people after violence disrupted celebrations of PSG's second Champions League title win and a group tried to storm a police station in the French capital.

Speaking after an emergency meeting with top government officials, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the possibility of calling off planned events was discussed, including football matches.

“But this does not apply to tomorrow's match between PSG and FC Barcelona,” he said, adding that other matches planned in European competitions this week would not be affected. Nuñez mentioned the match between Lille and Galatasaray scheduled Wednesday in the northern city, where looters also vandalized shops over the weekend.

Nuñez offered his resignation on Sunday (October 18), but French President Emmanuel Macron asked him to stay to respond to police needs in an emergency situation. Macron instructed Nuñez “to take all necessary steps to ensure full transparency about the failures in planning and intelligence-gathering that led to the violence.”

Lecornu said details of the areas to be placed under curfew will be provided later.

Nuñez acknowledged that authorities had “lost control” in some major cities on Saturday (October 17), with hundreds of businesses looted.

World.title: Shivraj Singh Chouhan launches upgraded agri welfare portal
World.content:
Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Monday (October 19, 2026) launched an upgraded agri welfare portal that will provide farmers with all information about the government schemes and also enable them to submit applications to avail the benefits.

The platform will serve as a single-window gateway to major government initiatives, including PM-KISAN, AgriStack and the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare said in a statement.

Farmers will get authentic information on weather conditions, scientific farming practices, the availability of seeds and fertilisers, and prevailing market prices for agricultural produce. A special training campaign will be conducted through Krishi Vigyan Kendras to help farmers make effective use of the portal and other digital tools.

"The portal aims to provide farmers across the country with direct, easy access to government schemes, financial assistance and reliable agricultural information on their mobile phones, eliminating procedural hurdles and the role of intermediaries," the statement said.

Addressing the launch programme, Mr. Chouhan said the Prime Minister's vision is to ensure that the government remains accessible to citizens and farmers at all times through their mobile phones.

Technology could fulfil its true purpose only when it reached farms and rural communities, he added.

"With the upgraded portal, farmers will no longer need to visit multiple government offices or navigate different websites to obtain information about schemes or submit applications," Mr. Chouhan said.

The portal will also bring together Farmer Producer Organisations, Primary Agricultural Credit Societies, agricultural scientists, researchers and startups, creating a common digital platform for the wider agricultural ecosystem.

Emphasising the importance of reliable information, Mr. Chouhan directed officials to ensure that the portal remained accurate and regularly updated.

He also stressed that the language and processes must be simple enough for small and marginal farmers, including those with limited formal education, to understand and use the platform with ease.

Union Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Secretary Atish Chandra, Additional Secretary Pramod Meherda, senior officials from the Digital Agriculture Division and other officials from the ministry and the National Informatics Centre were present at the launch.

Elaborating on the benefits of the portal, the ministry said all services would be available in one place. "Information on the ministry’s schemes, subsidies, rules and digital services will be available on a single portal, reducing the time and effort farmers spend navigating multiple platforms."

Online eligibility checks, direct application facilities and the transfer of financial assistance through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) will make processes more transparent and reduce the role of intermediaries, he added.

World.title: Karnataka to bring all citizen services online, under Sakala
World.content:
The Karnataka government has issued guidelines for all departments to make citizen services more accessible, transparent and time-bound. The guidelines now make it mandatory that all services, including licences and certificates, be brought online and under the Sakala framework.

An order issued by Harsh Gupta, Principal Secretary, Praja Seva Department, on October 17, requires departments to shorten timelines for Sakala services and issue certificates over the counter wherever possible. Online services should not be restricted to a particular jurisdictional officer where they can be provided by other officers of the equivalent cadre.

The guidelines, approved by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, are based on recommendations of the Karnataka Administrative Reforms Commission-2 (KARC-2). The government said the measures could be implemented immediately without major financial or policy implications.

Facilities for citizens

Government offices must provide seating and drinking water for visitors and introduce token systems for those meeting officials wherever possible. Citizens required to attend verification or inquiries must be informed of their appointment slots in advance.

Departments must offer multi-year renewal options for certificates renewed only on payment of a fee. Approved beneficiaries cannot be removed from schemes without prior intimation and an opportunity to be heard. Property inspections must be conducted through online applications, preferably mobile apps, and based on objective criteria wherever possible.

Online services and digital records

Aadhaar must be the default verification option for online services, with alternatives such as mobile-based verification where Aadhaar cannot be mandated. Departments must link their systems to relevant databases to verify information online and store government-issued certificates and licences in DigiLocker. Relevant fields in Kutumba must be updated in real time so that citizens are not asked to submit documents already held by the government.

Online applications must support OCR-format PDF uploads, digital signatures by officials and e-Hastakshar for applicants. Certificates and licences must follow standard templates prescribed by the Electronics Delivery of Citizen Services (EDCS), display the government logo and carry QR codes.

Departments must address server instability, provide dashboard reports on downtime and ensure websites and applications comply with National e-Governance Service Delivery Assessment standards.

Digital payments and updates

Application fees must be payable online, including through UPI, and manual collection should be stopped as far as possible. Fees collected for rejected applications must be refunded automatically.

Citizens must receive periodic application-status updates through SMS and WhatsApp and be able to track applications online. Portals should provide personal login profiles or integrated authentication to help users track previous applications.

Physical documents must be sent through a centralised postal system, with download options available online or at citizen service kiosks. All formats available only in English must also be provided in Kannada. Departments must prepare short videos explaining their services and upload them on social media.

The order also directs departments to prepare working manuals for officials and examine staff redeployment before creating posts or recruiting against sanctioned vacancies.

Departments must submit compliance reports to the Praja Seva Department. Implementation will be reviewed at the monthly Karnataka Development Programme meeting chaired by the Chief Secretary, the order stated.

World.title: Man City star Guehi says taking the knee has lost impact after opting against anti-racism gesture
World.content:
Manchester City defender Marc Guehi believes the gesture of soccer players taking the knee before matches might have lost its impact and wants to see more done in the sport's fight against racism.

Also read: The big blot on the beautiful game | On racism in football

Guehi, who is Black, didn't take the knee prior to kickoff in City's home game against Ipswich in the Premier League on Saturday (October 17, 2026) in the first of two rounds of games dedicated to the competition's “No Room For Racism” campaign.

It isn't the first time Guehi refused to perform the gesture, which was introduced in June 2020 to show support for the Black Lives Matter campaign. Since the start of the 2022-23 season, the Premier League has decided against taking the knee ahead of every match, with players instead invited to do so on certain occasions each season.

Speaking Monday (October 19) at a news conference the day before City's Champions League match against AEK Athens, Guehi said it was “great” that the Premier League's anti-racism campaign was continuing.

“Whether more can be done — more can always be done,” he said. “We have to see how we can move the campaign along.

“I don't think it's necessarily a football issue. I think it's a wider societal issue and football is that beacon of hope to try to get the message out. But whether more can be done, we will try, hopefully with the PFA [English footballers union], with the league.”

Asked whether taking the knee had lost its meaning, Guehi said: “Maybe. I haven't been taking the knee for a while now, to be honest. I'd always clap, just because of what that actually signifies.”

Guehi didn't go into more detail about his reasons for not taking the knee.

Another player not performing the gesture at the weekend was Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who stood while his teammates and opposition players for Manchester United knelt.

“Dom is more or less like, No, I don't go down. I show my respect by standing up, more or less,'” Leeds manager Daniel Farke said after the match, in which Calvert-Lewin scored in a 1-1 draw.

“I think each individual is different and shows respect for this campaign in a different way.”

In 2021, Wilfried Zaha — a Black player who was at Crystal Palace at the time — said he would no longer be taking the knee, describing the gesture as “degrading.”

“I feel like taking a knee is degrading,” Zaha was quoted by The Guardian newspaper as telling the FT Business of Football conference. “Growing up, my parents just let me know that I should just be proud to be black, no matter what, and I just think we should stand tall.

“I think the meaning behind the whole thing is becoming something that we just do now. That's not enough."

Premier League CEO Richard Masters said the current "No Room For Racism" initiative, which comes during the U.K.'s Black History Month, intends to use “the reach of our players to send an important message: we are united in the fight against racism.”

World.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine got no early warning from partners as Russia hits power grid again
World.content:
Russia launched new attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure using ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday (October 19, 2026), adding that Kyiv again received no early warning of the attack from partner countries that previously shared that intelligence.

Mr. Zelenskyy is grappling with recent Washington moves benefiting Russian President Vladimir Putin, including waiving U.S. sanctions on Moscow and signing a deal to import diesel from Moscow.

Another Russian ballistic missile attack came in several waves overnight, and once again, there was no early warning from our partners. They again targeted energy facilities and infrastructure, but a medical clinic, a school, a metro station, and ordinary residential buildings were also damaged. In total, the Russians launched 16 ballistic missiles in a deliberate attack on Kyiv and the Kyiv region. The Russians also launched more than 200 drones of various types, including jet-powered "shaheds," with attacks spanning from the Kharkiv and Dnipro regions to the Volyn, Rivne, and Odesa regions. Sadly, there are casualties. My condolences to their families and loved ones. Those who were injured are receiving assistance. Overnight and this morning, Russia attacked energy facilities in the Vinnytsia, Volyn, Kirovohrad, Kyiv, Mykolaiv, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi, Kharkiv, Ternopil, Odesa, and Rivne regions. In this one night alone, more than 10 energy infrastructure facilities were damaged, and the lights went out for at least 550,000 families. Repair crews are working at the sites. Ukraine never wanted this war, and we have welcomed literally EVERY attempt by our partners to bring this war to a dignified end. We have responded positively to EVERY ceasefire proposal. Russia's response, time and again, has been ballistic missiles, "shaheds," and killings. Putin not only doesn't want to end this war – he doesn't even want to take any steps toward de-escalation. EVERY ONE of our partners has experienced this firsthand when they heard Russia's refusals. And it is crucial to call things what they are. To call the aggressor an aggressor and help Ukraine defend lives. When deliveries of missiles for Ukraine's air defense are blocked while Russia is granted relief or delays in sanctions, this is, unfortunately, a denial of reality on the part of our partners. The reality is that the war continues, and it continues solely because of Russian strikes and Russia's desire to drag this war out. I thank everyone who recognizes this reality and helps Ukraine! — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) October 19, 2026

In parallel, limits on Kyiv's use of the military-grade version of U.S. company SpaceX's satellite internet service have choked Ukrainian drone operations, according to Mr. Zelenskyy. Also, a severe shortage of American-made Patriot air defence systems has made Ukraine more vulnerable.

Western intelligence sharing has helped Ukraine counter Russia's devastating ballistic missiles and hold back Moscow's invasion, which began more than 4½ years ago.

U.S. President Donald Trump says Washington hasn't stopped providing intelligence to Kyiv. Secretary of State Marco Rubio repeated that position on Monday (October 19), saying he had no information about the previous night's Russian attack.

Russian barrage on power grid kills a 21-year-old woman

The Russian nighttime barrage damaged more than 10 energy infrastructure facilities across Ukraine, depriving more than half a million people of electricity, heat and running water, Mr. Zelenskyy said on social media.

Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and its surrounding region, Mr. Zelenskyy said, with officials in the capital reporting a 21-year-old woman was killed.

The Russian Defence Ministry said that it struck Ukrainian targets including a data centre, a logistics hub storing components for drones and cruise missiles, an industrial facility making drone components, and a locomotive depot where missiles are stored.

Ukraine says it has made every diplomatic effort for peace

Donald Trump accuses Mr. Zelenskyy of not wanting the war with Russia to end. Washington's efforts to bring peace, meanwhile, have failed, including a recent truce covering energy infrastructure that Mr. Trump had demanded.

Help from Western allies has been vital for Ukraine's defence against Russia's bigger military, but fears have mounted that Mr. Trump may be turning his back on Ukraine.

Western analysts and officials say Mr. Putin believes that he can wait for foreign support for Ukraine to unravel and that Russia's bigger military will then crush Ukraine's resistance.

“Ukraine never wanted this war, and we have welcomed literally EVERY attempt by our partners to bring this war to a dignified end. We have responded positively to EVERY ceasefire proposal,” Mr. Zelenskyy said on social media. “The reality is that the war continues, and it continues solely because of Russian strikes and Russia's desire to drag this war out.”

Ukraine has held back Moscow's forces on the front line and has hit back with long-range strikes deep inside Russia on oil refineries that triggered fuel shortages.

On Sunday (October 18), Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia in one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, setting fire to an oil export terminal and a depot in St. Petersburg.

Some Kyiv residents shrug, but others express growing alarm

Russia has sought to disrupt daily life in Ukraine by attacking trains, shopping malls, gas stations and supermarkets, among other sites.

Kyiv resident Serhii Brezhniuk, owner of a shopping mall store that was damaged on Monday (October 19), said he had grown used to the relentless bombardment.

“It's what we see every single day,” he told The Associated Press. “We've grown accustomed to it.”

Alla Suska, 66, said she noticed many people walking around with bags under their eyes from a lack of sleep.

“Since there are attacks every night and air raid alerts all day long, naturally, we don't get any proper rest,” she said.

Maksym Maksymovych, 44, said he felt the tension mounting amid Russia's escalation, saying his son's school was damaged in the latest attack.

“You sort of get used to all these events -- after all, we've been living in Kyiv since the war began -- but you can see the explosions drawing closer and closer,” he said.

Possibility of US-China-Russia talks on the war is rejected by Kyiv

U.S. and Russian officials said on Monday (October 19) that talks are continuing on the possibility of a trilateral meeting involving Putin, Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at an APEC summit in China next month to try to negotiate a deal on Ukraine, without Kyiv's participation. The possibility was first reported by the Wall Street Journal.

Mr. Rubio said he was aware of the possibility. “I mean, I think there have been talks of a meeting. I don't know if anything's been finalised,” he told reporters.

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said that while the possibility of such a meeting has been mentioned, “no substantive proposals or agreements regarding the meeting itself nor its potential agenda and content have been discussed or put forward by anyone.”

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha dismissed the idea of an end to the war being discussed without Kyiv officials being present, saying it would embolden Putin.

“Inviting Putin to such a meeting would feed his appetite for self-aggrandisement and give him a stature he does not deserve,” Mr. Sybiha said on X.

Lithuania steps up security after Starlink base arson attempt

Lithuania is raising alert levels at more than 15 strategic infrastructure sites after an arson attempt Sunday at a Starlink base station in Vilnius, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius said on Monday (October 19).

European officials and law enforcement have warned repeatedly that Russia is waging a hybrid war against Europe, including sabotage, arson and vandalism, as well as influence operations.

World.title: Tiger Shroff firing: Three suspects detained in Kota; one was in touch with Bishnoi gang aide, says police
World.content:
Three people, including a minor, allegedly involved in the firing at actor Tiger Shroff were detained on Monday (October 18, 2026) in Rajasthan’s Kota city from the Pune-Jaipur Superfast Express, police said.

Addressing a press conference in Mumbai, DCP Raj Tilak Roshan said one of the accused is 18 years old, and the other two are 22 years old.

“Two accused are from Haryana, and one is from Bihar. Two of the three arrested assailants had fired five to six rounds at Tiger Shroff’s car,” he said.

The DCP said the motorcycle used by them was found in Mumbai’s Andheri area.

“No weapon was recovered from three suspects. Mumbai Police have taken custody of the three suspects and are bringing them to Mumbai from Rajasthan,” he said.

Mr. Roshan said there was no complaint earlier of any threat to Tiger Shroff.

“The motive behind firing on the actor is not yet ascertained. We will find it out after interrogating the suspected assailants,” the DCP added.

He said the three suspects were nabbed from a train in Kota, Rajasthan, within 15 hours of the incident in a swift inter-state operation executed by 20 special teams of the crime branch, with active technical and operational assistance from the Delhi, Gujarat, and Rajasthan police forces.

“A special Mumbai crime branch team has taken custody of all three suspects from Rajasthan Police and is bringing them to the metropolis for interrogation,” the DCP added.

The shooting targeting the popular “War” star on a busy Sunday evening was captured on video, the clip showing gunshots being fired at close range at his car. While the 36-year-old, who is also veteran actor Jackie Shroff’s son, escaped relatively unhurt, his driver and a bystander were injured.

A case was subsequently registered at the Juhu police station under sections 109(1) (attempt to murder) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), read with Sections 3 and 25 of the Arms Act.

“Following the attack, crime branch teams analysed technical footprints and recovered the motorcycle used in the crime near Andheri (West) railway station. Tracing the vehicle owner’s details, investigators tracked the suspects’ escape route to Surat, where they boarded the Pune-Jaipur train,” the DCP said.

Sharing real-time intelligence with law enforcement in other states, the Mumbai Police coordinated with their counterparts in Kota, who intercepted the train at Kota junction and nabbed all three suspects within minutes of their arrival at the station.

Further investigation has been handed over to the Anti-Extortion Cell (AEC) of the Crime Branch, the DCP said.

Roshan said authorities are verifying social media claims in which certain individuals purportedly accepted responsibility for the shooting.

“The firearms used in the crime are yet to be recovered, and police are probing all potential angles, including whether any handlers or external conspirators were involved,” he added.

World.title: El Nino effect: Prepare micro level contingency plans to avert drinking water, electricity shortages, says Telangana Chief Secretary
World.content:
Telangana Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju on Monday (October 19, 2026) directed officials to chart micro level contingency plans to prevent drinking water and electricity shortages in view of El Niño effect.

At a video conference held by the top official on Monday (October 19, 2026) on the prevailing conditions due to the weather phenomena and measures being taken in erstwhile districts, officials discussed groundwater levels, levels in reservoirs, electricity generation, alternative options to earn livelihood for people and other subjects.

Although electricity generation in the State has not been encouraging, the government is continuing to supply power for agricultural and domestic requirements. The Chief Secretary said that power cuts were not being imposed on industries and asked management of the units not to worry. Officials were directed to take all necessary measures to ensure maximum electricity generation at all thermal power stations.

Permission only to deepen existing borewells for drinking water

Special Chief Secretary to the government, Jayesh Ranjan said that permission to drill new borewells in Hyderabad should not be granted for construction or other activities. He said that currently, the permission is being granted only to deepen existing borewells exclusively for drinking water requirements. The senior official said that treated water from Sewerage Treatment Plants (STPs) would be supplied to construction sites in the city through dial-a-green water tanker service.

Special Chief Secretary, Vikas Raj said that groundwater levels in Rangareddy district were declining significantly and alternative plans were being implemented to ensure that there would be no shortage of drinking water.

Palair reservoir needs to have 4 thousand million cubic feet (tmcft) of water to provide drinking water to Mahabubabad, Khammam and Suryapet districts until June. However, it now has only 2 tmcft, said Anudeep Durishetty, Special Officer for Khammam district.

World.title: Heavy rain causes flooding in a few localities in west Velachery
World.content:
The heavy rains which lashed on Saturday (October 17, 2026) night resulted in stagnation of water in a few localities of west Velachery despite the presence of storm water drain network.

The residents of AGS Colony, Saraswathi nagar, Bhuvaneshwari Nagar, Aandal nagar and Mohanapuri, suffered flooding like situation because of the slow discharge of rainwater in the Veerangal Odai, which is ultimately linked to the Pallikaranai Marshland.

Geetha Ganesh, a resident of AGS Colony, said that water stagnated for one-feet in some localities including the 4th Main road but within a few hours of rain stopping in the early morning on Sunday rainwater had receded as the Chennai Corporation had installed a heavy duty pump in the Veerangal Odai to pump out the rainwater.

In Sakthi Nagar main road which links Velachery to Adambakkam, the construction of storm water drain and footpath resulted in stagnation of rain water. However in the morning the rainwater receded. Most of the houses which are on low level compared to the road height were flooded with rainwater.

In Andal Nagar and Bhuvaneshwari Nagar, several individual houses are low lying because of the increasing height of the road and SWD being on a high level causing rainwater to back flow into the houses.

The Southern Railway has installed a earth mover for desilting the six-vent culvert located near the Velachery railway station of the Mass Rapid Transit system (MRTS) which has helped in prevention of flooding in the localities of east Velachery.

World.title: CDF Munir, new Saudi envoy express satisfaction at progress made under Makkah pact: ISPR
World.content:
The new Saudi envoy in Pakistan, Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy, met with Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir on Monday, with both sides expressing satisfaction over the progress made under the trilateral Makkah defence agreement, according to the military’s media wing.

Albugamy assumed his diplomatic responsibilities in Islamabad last Thursday, reaffirming the commitment to strengthening the strategic and fraternal ties between the two countries.

Inter-Service Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement on Monday that the ambassador called on CDF Munir at General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi. According to the statement, matters of mutual interest and regional security dynamics were discussed.

“Both the dignitaries expressed satisfaction over the progress made under the framework of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and underscored the importance of strengthening defence collaboration, institutional linkages and strategic coordination,” the statement read.

CDF Munir congratulated the ambassador on his appointment and expressed confidence that his tenure would further strengthen the longstanding fraternal ties between Islamabad and Riyadh, which are “rooted in shared faith, mutual trust and strategic partnership”.

Last week, Albugamy met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.

PM Shehbaz reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its “sovereignty, security and territorial integrity” amid a recent escalation in Houthi attacks during their meeting.

DPM Dar, meanwhile, underscored longstanding fraternal and strategic ties between Islamabad and Riyadh when he met Albugamy. He also reaffirmed Islamabad and Riyadh’s “shared commitment to further strengthen bilateral cooperation for mutual progress and prosperity”.

Islamabad and Riyadh have signed two defence pacts aimed at collective deterrence, the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between the two and the Makkah Joint Defence Alliance that also includes Turkiye.

Earlier this month, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye convened an emergency meeting under the Makkah alliance and agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom.

While the statement did not specifically name any threat, the development came against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

The Makkah defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

In an interview aired on Sunday, the military’s spokesman said Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels against the kingdom.

World.title: 'We never gave up': Naqvi highlights Pakistan's peace efforts in US-Iran war at Qatar forum
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday highlighted Pakistan’s mediation efforts between the United States and Iran, affirming that Islamabad “never gave up”.

He made the remarks while addressing the 8th Global Security Forum being held in Qatar’s capital, Doha. Convened under the title “The Future of Alliances“, the forum brings together high-ranking officials and dignitaries from over 100 nations, according to Qatar News Agency.

“The last few months have been very difficult for our region. The conflict involving Iran and the United States created serious risks not only for the Middle East, but for the entire world,” Naqvi noted.

He added that at such a critical time, Pakistan chose the path of peace and made “every possible effort to reduce tensions”.

Naqvi, who has been involved in Islamabad’s peace efforts and has made several trips to Iran since the war began, said: “There were moments when the situation was extremely tense, but we never gave up.

“We continued talking, listening and working to build trust. And I can tell you from my experience: peace is not achieved in one meeting; it requires patience, trust and continuous efforts.”

He particularly highlighted the “remarkable role” of Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir in Pakistan’s efforts to reduce tensions.

CDF Munir, accompanied by Naqvi, had visited Iran in August “as part of Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and stability”. The interior minister last made a visit to Iran in September, with Tehran describing the trip as part of bilateral engagements.

Speaking at the Doha forum, Naqvi recalled the June 18 signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Iran and the US. The 14-point MoU , which Pakistan signed as a mediator, provided a framework for ending the war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb 28.

The interior minister recalled that the MoU was followed by the Lake Lucerne Summit in Switzerland, organised by mediators Pakistan and Qatar.

“There, I saw something I will never forget,” he said, adding that Qatar’s Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani and CDF Munir worked for “more than 16 hours without a single break”.

“No cameras, no announcements; only two men who refused to let the talks fail,” Naqvi remarked, emphasising that the only aim of the two mediating countries was to “stop further conflict and to save innocent lives”.

The minister praised Qatar’s peace efforts, noting it had “done so much”. “In the diplomacy of our time, when others chose sides, Qatar chose to keep talking. Pakistan has seen this closely because we have worked beside you.”

He stressed that Pakistan has always believed that “dialogue is better than war”.

“Our recent experience has taught us three important lessons: never close the door to dialogue, trust is the most important key for any kind of talk, and thirdly, peace requires sincere efforts from everyone.”

The senator emphasised that no single country could achieve regional peace alone.

“Pakistan is proud of the role it has played in the regional peace efforts,” he said, reaffirming that Islamabad would continue to support dialogue, peace and cooperation.

“We believe that winning peace is far more important than winning a war,” the minister remarked.

He conveyed Pakistan’s message: “We do not want credit for stopping wars. We want a future where wars do not start.”

The war between Washington and Tehran began in February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran , which responded with retaliatory attacks on nearby Gulf countries.

While diplomatic engagements continue, there has been a lack of progress in recent weeks in negotiations to end the war.

After an interim ceasefire collapsed, Iran in September presented its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — the key oil trade route that has remained central to the conflict.

The US said it had rejected that proposal, while Iran’s security chief said negotiations have stalled because Washington failed to address all seven conditions for reopening the strait. On Sunday, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran’s offer to the US to reopen the waterway within seven days was still on the table.

Meanwhile, the Middle East is currently facing heightened tensions on another front as Houthi rebels attack Saudi Arabia after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s coalition government unravelled in July.

Makkah alliance ‘not for war’

During his address, Naqvi cited the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed among Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in August as an example of Islamabad’s commitment to regional security.

“It is a pact for defence, not for war,” he declared, adding that no country could “enjoy lasting peace if its neighbours are facing conflicts”.

The pact , under which the three countries have formed the Makkah Defence Alliance, empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Naqvi also spoke about countering security challenges and called for stronger international cooperation on the matter.

“As Pakistan’s interior minister, I also understand the price of terrorism and insecurity. Pakistan has suffered greatly; thousands of our citizens, soldiers, and policemen have lost their lives. Even today, we continue to fight.”

Describing terrorism as a “common enemy”, he called for “stronger cooperation, better intelligence-sharing and joint efforts to defeat it”.

The senator noted that counterterrorism cooperation was not something Pakistan has only sought, but also provided. He then highlighted the country’s contributions to the United Nations’ peacekeeping missions.

“Our UN police peacekeepers have helped protect civilians, support local police and restore peace in countries affected by conflict. We are proud of their services and sacrifices,” he said.

World.title: Punjab govt to ban 'spying objects' equipped with hidden cameras, recording devices
World.content:
The Punjab government decided on Monday to ban objects equipped with hidden cameras and recording devices, including pens, eyeglasses and watches.

A statement by the Punjab Home Department identified such objects as those “used for spying” and said the decision was taken to protect the citizens’ privacy and personal information, particularly those of women and children.

The statement said “strict legal action” would be taken against the use, purchase and sale of “spying devices and covert electronic devices”, further warning that the “illegal use” of objects equipped with hidden cameras would result in “severe penalties”.

The statement also mentioned that complaints had been received about the use of “spying devices” for “illegal surveillance, harassment and blackmailing”.

Punjab Home Secretary Ahmad Javed Qazi told Dawn that a formal notification for the implementation of the ban would be issued in a few days. He explained that the announcement about the ban had been made prior to the issuance of the notification to give people some time to discard such items.
